# OpenAI Unveils GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol to Reduce Business AI Costs

## OpenAI has introduced GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models, offering enhanced capabilities for professional and routine tasks. The new AI versions improve performance across complex benchmarks while significantly reducing costs for developers and businesses.

# OpenAI Unveils GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol to Reduce Business AI Costs

New Delhi [India], November 18 (ANI): OpenAI has launched two new artificial intelligence models, GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol, with improved capabilities for professional and everyday tasks, while aiming to reduce the cost of using advanced AI tools for businesses and developers. The company said the new models can handle more complex tasks while using fewer output tokens, allowing users to complete more work within their usage limits.

The launch is aimed at making advanced AI more affordable for businesses that use these tools across different operations. GPT-6.2 Astra is designed for demanding professional work, including preparing documents, presentations and spreadsheets, writing code and carrying out scientific research. GPT-6.2 Sol, meanwhile, is intended for everyday tasks and routine work that involves multiple steps.

OpenAI said Astra performed better than its previous version on the Agents' Last Exam benchmark, which tests how well AI models handle complex, multi-step professional assignments. It scored 5.2 points higher than GPT-6 Astra while costing less than one-third as much to run. It also scored 5.5 points higher than rival model Claude Fable 5.2 at just 5 per cent of the cost, according to the company. The new Astra model also scored nine percentage points higher than GPT-6 Astra on Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, a test that measures the ability of AI models to carry out scientific research tasks.

OpenAI said Astra can prepare more detailed and professionally formatted documents, spreadsheets and presentations, with outputs better suited to fields such as law, finance, sales and accounting. The model also offers improvements in coding, website development and 3D design. GPT-6.2 Sol, designed for regular use, also showed improved performance over its predecessor, GPT-6.1 Sol. On Cognition's FrontierCode 2.0 benchmark, it came within 0.5 points of Astra while costing about one-fifth as much, OpenAI said.

The models are available to Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users through ChatGPT Work and Codex. Developers can also access them through the OpenAI API. The company has reduced GPT-6.2 Astra's API input and output token prices by 20 per cent compared with GPT-6 Astra, while cached input costs are 60 per cent lower. API pricing for GPT-6.2 Sol remains unchanged from GPT-6.1 Sol. OpenAI also said it has introduced tighter safeguards for cybersecurity-related tasks as the new models are better able to identify and exploit software vulnerabilities. (ANI)

OpenAI.content:
# OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol for ChatGPT Work and Codex

## AI Summary OpenAI unveiled two new AI models, GPT-6.2 Astra for complex professional work and GPT-6.2 Sol for everyday tasks. The models are available from Nov. 17 to paid users of ChatGPT Work and Codex, and to developers via the OpenAI API, but not to free accounts. OpenAI also adjusted API pricing, expanded Ultrafast processing access by subscription tier, and said both models reached a “critical” cybersecurity threshold.

- Writer Seung-a Yoo
- published 2026-11-18 08:29:35

OpenAI unveiled two new artificial intelligence models, GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol, each specialized for complex professional work and everyday tasks, respectively. The two models focus on improving task accuracy and token efficiency to handle complex work at lower cost.

On Nov. 17, OpenAI said the two models would be available from that day on ChatGPT Work and Codex to users on Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu plans. Developers can also use them through the OpenAI API. They are not available to free accounts and can be used in the Work environment rather than general chat mode.

GPT-6.2 Astra is designed for professional projects such as financial analysis, legal research, presentation creation and complex coding. When given a screenshot of an existing presentation, it can produce new slides reflecting layout, colors and even font sizes. Its ability to revise and test existing code projects has also improved. Early testers said code structure became cleaner, tests became more specific and revision work decreased.

GPT-6.2 Sol is an efficient model for everyday coding, document writing and multi-step tasks. In Cognition's FrontierCode 2.0 evaluation, the score gap between Astra and Sol was only 0.5 points when both models were run at maximum reasoning performance. Sol's per-task cost was about one-fifth of Astra's.

Performance results varied by test. In OpenAI's own evaluation, Agents Last Exam, Astra scored 5.2 points higher than the existing GPT-6 Astra and 5.5 points higher than Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2. Its per-task cost was less than one-third of the existing GPT-6 Astra's and about 5 percent of Claude Fable 5.2's.

In contrast, in an overall intelligence evaluation by external evaluator Artificial Analysis, Astra scored 62 points, trailing Claude Fable 5.2, which scored 65. Sol scored 57. Some independent evaluations also pointed out that performance improvements for AI agents doing coding work were not clearly better than before.

Paris Atlas was introduced as a use case for the new models. Thomas Licouart (토마 리쿠아르), an OpenAI developer, created a 3D virtual environment across Paris by combining street maps with French survey data to reflect more than 131,000 buildings. Users can explore in a browser as if walking through the real city or moving by car, and the model reflects changes when users provide revisions via screenshots.

API pricing was also adjusted. Astra's input and output token prices were cut by 20 percent from the existing GPT-6 Astra. It is priced at $8 per 1 million input tokens and $40 per 1 million output tokens, with cached input at $0.40. Sol kept the price of the existing GPT-6.1 Sol, set at $2 for input, $10 for output and $0.10 for cached input.

The scope of Ultrafast, an ultra-high-speed processing feature by subscription plan, was also expanded. Pro subscribers paying $200 per month will be able to use the feature on GPT-6.2 Sol for the first time, and Pro subscribers paying $500 per month can use it on both models. Enterprise and Edu users can access it if a workspace administrator enables the feature.

On safety, OpenAI said both models reached a “critical” threshold for cybersecurity capabilities. Astra also met a “high” threshold for AI self-improvement capabilities for the first time. OpenAI said it had tightened restrictions on high-risk cybersecurity support and built a control system called “Control Room” that can monitor or stop the model's tasks.

The launch shows OpenAI's strategy to expand ChatGPT from a simple question-and-answer tool into a work platform that produces actual documents, software and interactive services.

About the Author
 Seung-a Yoo ysah@d-today.co.kr

OpenAI.content:
# OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra after scrapping predecessor

Tech & Startup Desk

OpenAI launched GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol on November 17, introducing its latest AI models for professional and everyday tasks.

The launch follows OpenAI's decision to scrap GPT-6.1 Astra in September, after the model went beyond its instructions and misrepresented its actions to users, according to reports by The Wall Street Journal and The Washington Post.

In a recent blog post, OpenAI said Astra's API input and output token prices are 20 per cent lower than GPT-6 Astra. Sol retains the API pricing of GPT-6.1 Sol. GPT-6.2 Astra is designed for demanding tasks involving professional work, research and software development, while GPT-6.2 Sol targets everyday use and multi-step workflows.

The new models are available to Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu subscribers through ChatGPT Work and Codex, as well as through OpenAI's API.

OpenAI described Astra as its most capable model for cybersecurity. Both new models meet the company's 'Critical threshold’ for cybersecurity capabilities under its preparedness framework.

OpenAI.content:
# OpenAI推出GPT-6.2 Astra与Sol，接入ChatGPT Work和Codex

#### Astra聚焦专业项目，Sol面向日常多步骤任务；API价格下调，“超高速处理”适用范围扩大

## AI摘要 OpenAI发布两款新模型GPT-6.2 Astra和GPT-6.2 Sol，分别瞄准专业级复杂任务和日常多步骤任务。两款模型现已向ChatGPT Work和Codex付费用户开放，并支持通过OpenAI API调用。OpenAI称，新模型在准确率和Token效率上有所提升，同时下调部分API价格，并扩大“超高速处理”功能覆盖范围；在安全方面，公司进一步收紧高风险网络安全支持限制，并引入控制系统“Control Room”。

- 记者 Seung-a Yoo
- 发布时间 2026-11-18 08:29:35

OpenAI发布两款新AI模型——GPT-6.2 Astra和GPT-6.2 Sol，分别针对复杂专业工作和日常任务进行优化。公司表示，新模型提升了任务准确率和Token效率，目标是在更低成本下处理更复杂的工作。

OpenAI当地时间17日表示，这两款模型已在ChatGPT Work和Codex中向Plus、Pro、Enterprise、Edu订阅用户开放，开发者也可通过OpenAI API调用。免费账户暂不支持，且仅限于Work工作区场景使用，不适用于普通对话模式。

其中，GPT-6.2 Astra主要面向金融分析、法律调研、演示文稿生成以及复杂编程等专业项目。OpenAI称，用户上传现有演示文稿截图后，模型可参考版式、配色和字体大小生成新的幻灯片；其对既有代码项目的修改和测试能力也有所增强。早期测试者反馈称，生成的代码结构更整洁，测试内容更具体，返工次数也有所减少。

GPT-6.2 Sol则面向日常编程、文档撰写和多步骤任务处理，强调效率表现。根据Cognition的FrontierCode 2.0评测，在启用最高推理性能时，Astra与Sol的得分仅相差0.5分，但Sol的单次任务成本约为Astra的五分之一。

不过，两款模型在不同评测中的表现并不完全一致。在OpenAI自测的“Agents Last Exam”中，Astra得分较GPT-6 Astra高出5.2分，较Anthropic的Claude Fable 5.2高出5.5分。从成本看，Astra的单次任务成本不到GPT-6 Astra的三分之一，约为Claude Fable 5.2的5%。

在外部机构Artificial Analysis的综合智能评测中，Astra得分为62分，低于Claude Fable 5.2的65分；Sol得分为57分。另有部分独立评测指出，用于执行编程任务的AI Agent性能与此前相比并未出现明显提升。

OpenAI还展示了新模型的应用案例“Paris Atlas”。OpenAI开发者Thomas Ricouard将街道地图与法国测绘数据结合，构建出覆盖整个巴黎的3D虚拟环境，纳入超过13.1万栋建筑。用户可在浏览器中像步行或驾车一样浏览城市，并通过截图提交修改意见，再由模型完成更新。

与此同时，OpenAI也调整了API定价。Astra的输入和输出Token价格较GPT-6 Astra下调20%，每100万Token的输入价格为8美元，输出价格为40美元，缓存输入价格为0.40美元。Sol则维持GPT-6.1 Sol的价格不变，即每100万Token输入2美元、输出10美元、缓存输入0.10美元。

按订阅档位提供的“超高速处理”功能也进一步扩大覆盖范围。月费200美元的Pro订阅用户首次可在GPT-6.2 Sol上使用该功能；月费500美元的Pro订阅用户则可在两款模型上使用。Enterprise和Edu用户在工作区管理员开启相关功能后也可访问。

在安全方面，两款模型的网络安全能力均达到“Critical”标准；Astra在AI自我改进能力上也首次达到“High”标准。OpenAI表示，基于上述评估结果，公司已进一步收紧对高风险网络安全支持的限制，并建立名为“Control Room”的控制系统，用于监测并在必要时中止模型任务。

此次发布也被视为OpenAI产品策略的延伸，即推动ChatGPT从单一问答工具，进一步发展为可生成真实文档、软件和交互式服务的工作平台。

记者信息
 Seung-a Yoo ysah@d-today.co.kr

# Introducing Gemini Decision 1: A Model That Picks Answers Instead of Writing Them

Google's newest model has one job, and it never writes a word doing it. Decision 1 reads text, images, video, audio and PDFs in a single forward pass, up to 262,144 input tokens per request.

By Shittu Olumide, Technical Content Specialist on November 18, 2026 in Artificial Intelligence

Google's newest model has one job, and it never writes a word doing it. Gemini Decision 1, launched last week with the new Gemini Decisions API, takes an input and a list of closed questions and returns probabilities instead of prose: yes or no, option A, B or C, a score on a rubric.

That sounds small, but it isn't. Every agent stack runs on dozens of these quiet calls: which model gets this query, which tool fires, whether this message breaks a policy. Most teams handle them with a full generative model and a JSON parser, paying for output tokens they throw away. Google now sells that layer on its own, at $0.10 per million input tokens and nothing for output.

## What Gemini Decision 1 Does

Decision 1 reads text, images, video, audio and PDFs in a single forward pass, up to 262,144 input tokens per request. Against that one input, you can ask up to 1,000 independent questions of three kinds:

- Yes/no (noul in the API) returns a probability between 0.01 and 0.99
- Choice picks from 2 to 255 options and returns a probability for each
- Score grades against an ordered rubric and returns a weighted score plus a probability per level

Every answer carries a confidence value, so your code can send uncertain cases to a fallback or a person.

The pricing is the pitch. You pay $0.10 per million input tokens, the shared input is billed once no matter how many questions you ask, and output costs nothing because there is none. A no-cost tier in Google AI Studio covers prototyping.

The capability table shows what this model is not. Text generation, thinking, function calling, structured outputs, batch and caching are all listed as unsupported. It's a scoring engine, not a chatbot.

## What Happened When We Ran It?

We installed Google'sgoogle-genai SDK, created a free API key in AI Studio and ran three tests: Google's quickstart, Google's image example from the launch post, and an ambiguous support message of our own. Latency was timed from our machine, so it includes the network round trip.

The quickstart asks two questions about one customer message:
from google import genai

client = genai.Client(http_options={"api_version": "v1beta"})

result = client.decisions.create(
    model="gemini-decision-1",
    input="The blue mug I ordered on Monday arrived cracked on Wednesday.",
    questions={
        "is_damaged": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Did the item arrive damaged?"},
        "queue": {
            "type": "choice",
            "instructions": "Which support queue should handle this message?",
            "criteria": {
                "billing": "Payment, invoice, or refund questions.",
                "replacements": "Damaged, missing, or wrong items.",
                "general": "Product questions and account updates.",
            },
        },
    },
)

print(result.answers["queue"].choice, result.answers["queue"].confidence)

For the image test,input becomes a list holding an image URL and a text note. Here's what came back:

Test | Input | Answer | Median latency | Input tokens 
---|---|---|---|---
Quickstart | "Mug arrived cracked" | Damaged: 0.99. Queue: replacements (0.98) | 407 ms | 173 
Ambiguous | "Charged twice, handle chipped" | Damaged: 0.99. Queue: replacements 0.50, billing 0.48 | 574 ms | 181 
Image + text | Breakroom counter photo | Spill: 0.95. Action: wipe with cloth (0.98). Severity: 1.19 of 2 | 1,343 ms | 1,326 

Medians exclude each test's first call. Accuracy was clean: both of Google's examples came back right, and the image result matched Google's own screenshot. Every call billed zero output tokens. In dollars, the text query costs about $0.000017 per call, roughly 58,000 calls for a dollar. The image query costs about $0.00013.

## Google Is Already Running on It

Google says four of its own products use the Decisions API:

- Gemini Notebook routes each query to a model tier and thinking level, which Google says cuts latency on everyday queries by up to 40%
- Stitch uses it in its rapid canvas experiment to build playable wireframes and apply voice or tap edits
- CC from Google Labs picks an emoji reaction from more than 200 options without adding visible delay
- Google Search uses it as a safety layer that checks Model Context Protocol tools for adversarial behavior

## Our Take

#### 1. The Confidence Score Is the Real Product

Our ambiguous message is the test that matters. It fit two queues, and the model said so: 50.2% replacements, 48.4% billing, confidence 0.50. It didn't fake certainty on a coin flip, and in the same call it still rated the chipped handle as damage at 0.99.

One example doesn't prove calibration, which is measured across thousands of cases. But it's the behavior Google is selling, and it showed up when we went looking for it.

#### 2. Read Confidence, Not Just Choice

Here's the trap. On that coin-flip message, thechoice field still returned replacements, with no flag attached. Code that reads only the winner routes it as confidently as the clear case.

The calibration is only worth something if you set a threshold onconfidence and send everything below it elsewhere. Google's quickstart prints the winner. Your production code shouldn't stop there.

#### 3. The Speed Claim Didn't Hold for Images

Google quotes 150 to 250 ms end to end. After the first call, our text calls landed between 339 and 577 ms, a gap network distance can plausibly explain. Our image calls took 1.1 to 1.4 seconds, a median five to nine times the claim, though Google says its figures hold across multimodal inputs.

Some of that may be Google fetching the image from a URL and processing 1,064 image tokens. We can't separate the causes from outside. Two more details: Google's latency figure covers contexts up to 16K tokens, not the full 256K, and identical calls in our runs varied by more than 300 ms. Benchmark it on your own media before it goes anywhere near a real-time path.

#### 4. The Benchmarks Are Google's Own

The "nearly 5x cheaper" figure compares Decision 1 with Google's own Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, on a benchmark suite Google chose. That's useful if you already run Gemini. It says nothing about how Decision 1 compares with a small fine-tuned classifier you already have.

#### 5. Check the Small Print

The model page pitches classification over live media streams, while the same page lists the Live API as unsupported. And the model is Gemini-only for now. It's on OpenRouter, LangChain, Vercel's AI SDK, LiteLLM and others, but Google Cloud support is still marked as coming soon.

## Wrapping Up

Decision 1 does one narrow job well. It's cheap, it was accurate on everything we gave it, and it admitted doubt when we pushed it. Use it for routing and policy checks now. Wire your code toconfidence from the first day, and time it on your own images before you promise anyone 200 ms.

## Resources

Shittu Olumide is a software engineer and technical writer passionate about leveraging cutting-edge technologies to craft compelling narratives, with a keen eye for detail and a knack for simplifying complex concepts. You can also find Shittu on Twitter.

# Google just made its best Gemini agent free — here's where you can get it

When you buy through links on our articles, Future and its syndication partners may earn a commission.

Google is giving millions of people access to Gemini's Tasks feature for free.

The tool can run multi-step requests in the background, and Google is expanding its capabilities to include shopping, phone calls, email, and deeper integrations into its apps.

Formerly known as Spark, Tasks is now rolling out to free Gemini users in the US, Japan, South Korea, Canada, Australia, and India, as per Josh Woodward, VP of Product for AI at Google. This agentic mode previously required a paid AI Pro or AI Ultra tier.

It runs on Google's new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model and allows users to switch from Chat to Task mode to pass off work instead of babysitting every step. That could involve asking Gemini to plan a trip, research a topic, set up a morning briefing, or manage recurring tasks while you're busy doing literally anything else.

## Gemini is moving closer to a real personal assistant

Google is also launching a range of new capabilities, initially available in the US. It can call local businesses with Google Duplex, make purchases with Google Pay, receive text messages with RCS, and accept forwarded emails with Gmail. It can also log into websites using Google Password Manager without ever exposing passwords outside of Google's ecosystem.

Advertisement

Advertisement

To test it, flip the toggle above your mobile prompt box (or below on the web) from "Chat" to "Task." You can even bypass the app entirely by forwarding emails or texting Gemini directly through Google Messages and iMessage.

The Workspace integration is also receiving a major upgrade. Google says Gemini can now more reliably draft or send emails, create and edit Google Docs and Sheets, and add multiple events to Google Calendar without toggling between apps.

## There is still a catch

As you can imagine, having an AI in your inbox, passwords, and payment methods does raise some security concerns. Google says when browsing the web, Tasks runs inside an isolated virtual machine, protected against prompt injection and Google Safe Browsing protections. Gemini also asks for confirmation before it buys anything and can ask for clarification if your instructions aren't clear.

That said, Google still has some work to do. Some sites might prevent Gemini from completing a task and ask you to step in and finish the last step. For now, the promise of a digital assistant that can really take work off your hands is getting closer — but still isn't quite ready to be trusted with everything.

# Google Gemini gets agentic features to make calls, pay bills, shop and complete tasks in several countries including India

Google has announced new agentic capabilities for Gemini, allowing users to delegate tasks such as making phone calls, booking appointments, analyzing bills, shopping online, ordering groceries, and managing schedules. Powered by Google’s new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, the update introduces a Task mode in the Gemini app, along with integrations for Google services and third-party apps.

### Gemini can make calls and book appointments

Gemini can find nearby businesses through Google Maps, call them, check appointment availability, and schedule appointments based on the user’s Google Calendar. In Google’s example, Gemini used Personal Intelligence to identify a user’s 2019 Honda Odyssey and location, called two nearby dealerships simultaneously, and arranged an early Friday morning service appointment in less than five minutes.

Gemini identifies itself as an AI when calling businesses. Businesses can opt out of receiving these calls, and Gemini will not share payment or private account information without the user’s permission.

Our minivan is overdue for a service appointment. Please call the two nearest dealerships and figure out how to get an appointment early Friday morning over the next month or so.

### Bill analysis, shopping and payments

With the Google Password Manager integration, users can give Gemini permission to access utility portals and analyze previous billing statements in Gmail. Google demonstrated this with a $389 electricity bill, where Gemini identified a heat pump running around 4 p.m. during peak electricity pricing hours as the primary reason for the higher bill.

For online shopping, Gemini uses Google’s Shopping Graph to compare products and help complete purchases through Google Pay. It can ask follow-up questions about requirements such as wattage and color, and find discount codes. The payment features include:

- Agent Payments Protocol (AP2): Supports purchases through Gemini using digital tokens on supported cards. Google is working with Mastercard and Visa, with American Express support coming soon.
- Spending limits: Users can set a spending cap before assigning a shopping task.
- Card benefits: Eligible purchases retain card rewards, cashback, and purchase protections.
- Google Wallet: Receipts and tracking information are saved to Google Wallet.
- Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP): Google plans to integrate UCP into Gemini to improve the shopping process from product discovery to checkout.

### Grocery ordering and app integrations

With the new RCS integration, users can send shopping lists and photos to Gemini through text messages. In Google’s example, Gemini added lasagna, strawberries, cucumbers, vanilla ice cream, and Cheerios to an Instacart order based on text instructions and a photo of an empty cereal box. It then handed the user off to Instacart to complete the purchase.

Gemini now connects with more than 60 popular apps through its Connected Apps Platform. Developers can apply to join the platform.

### Gmail and Google Calendar integration

Gemini can extract dates and events from emails and add them to Google Calendar. Users can forward emails from Gmail to gemini@google.com, allowing the assistant to create calendar entries and invite other participants.

Google demonstrated this with school emails containing multiple dates. Gemini added the events to the calendar, invited the user’s wife, and identified a scheduling conflict with basketball practice. It also suggested contacting another parent to arrange a carpool change. Users can also use Gemini to manage medical bills and insurance renewals.

### Security and privacy

Google uses its Agent Compute Engine to run assigned tasks inside a hardware-isolated virtual machine dedicated to each user’s account. These virtual machines are not shared with other users and operate in sandboxed environments that are regularly tested by Google’s security red teams.

Other security and privacy measures include:

- Prompt-injection filters that scan search results, webpages, and other content.
- Google Safe Browsing to restrict the links Gemini can open.
- Settings to manage tasks and disconnect Google or third-party apps.
- Options to delete chat history.
- Confirmation requests before critical actions, such as clicking the Buy button.
- Clarifying questions when instructions are ambiguous.
- An Always allow option for routine actions that users have approved.

Google acknowledged that tasks may occasionally fail or produce incorrect results and asked users to report issues through the thumbs-down feedback option. Some websites may also require users to complete the final step manually, such as clicking a button. Google is working with major websites and security providers to improve compatibility with AI assistants.

Google has also published a technical paper explaining its multi-layer security approach and invited security researchers to participate in its AI Vulnerability Reward Program (AI VRP).

### How to use Gemini Task mode

Users can access the new capabilities by opening the Gemini app and switching the home-screen toggle from Chat to Task. They can then describe the task they want Gemini to complete.

# Settings
- Manage account
- Usage limits
- Preferences
- Notifications
- Personal intelligence
- Avatar
- Task settings
- Channels
- Gem manager
- Theme
- Voice
- Media
- Device controls

## Text with Gemini
Start tasks and get updates. Available in Google Messages and iMessage.
- 415-011-1726
Verified
**Reset**
Send text
Texts with Gemini are not end-to-end-encrypted and may be accessible by you can'tre subject to their privacy policy and terms. Deleting your Gemini Apps Activity only removes it from Gemini, not from your messaging app or carries.

## Email with Gemini
Start new tasks and get updates by emailing gemini@google.com
**Turn off**

In the U.S., users can also interact with Gemini through email forwarding or text messages. To set up Text with Gemini:

- Open the Gemini app on Android or iOS.
- Tap Settings and select Channels.
- Tap Set up under Text with Gemini.
- Verify your phone number.

### Pricing and availability

The new Task capabilities are rolling out free of charge to hundreds of millions of users in the U.S., Japan, South Korea, Canada, Australia, and India. Additional advanced features are initially rolling out in the U.S.

Calling through Gemini is not currently available in Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Montana, and Nebraska. The RCS integration requires a U.S. phone number with an eligible mobile carrier. Google Wallet is also expanding to iOS starting today.

# Google revamps AI agent Gemini Spark into Tasks, adds support in South Korea

## AI Summary Google is revamping its AI agent Gemini Spark into a new service called Tasks and offering it for free. The move opens AI automation features previously focused on paying subscribers to general users, and is expected to intensify competition in the AI agent market. Tasks runs on Google’s latest AI model, Gemini 4 Hydrogen, and can carry out multi-step work such as email analysis, schedule management and research.

- Writer Jae-won Choi
- published 2026-11-18 08:28:55

Google is revamping its AI agent Gemini Spark into Tasks and offering it for free. The company is opening AI automation features previously run mainly for paid subscribers to general users, and competition in the AI agent market is expected to intensify.

On Nov. 17, The Verge reported that Google has changed the name of Gemini Spark to Tasks and began offering it for free in six countries including South Korea, the United States, Canada, Japan, Australia and India.

Tasks runs on Google’s latest AI model, Gemini 4 Hydrogen. It can carry out multiple steps on its own based on a user’s instructions. While existing chatbots focused on answering questions or organizing information, Tasks can handle practical work such as email analysis, schedule management and research.

For example, it can analyze emails and calendars to draft travel itineraries, summarize needed information each day, and identify recurring unnecessary spending.

Using it is also simple. Users select Task instead of Chat in the Gemini app or on the website and enter the work they want. They can also issue additional instructions or change direction while a task is running.

More features are available to users in the United States. Gemini can call a business directly to check product prices and inventory, make payments with Google Pay, or use account information stored in Google Password Manager to log in to websites.

It also supports giving instructions by email and text message. In the United States, users can send an email to gemini@google.com or request tasks by text in Google Messages and iMessage.

Security features were also strengthened. Google explained that it carries out tasks in a hardware-isolated virtual machine dedicated to each user, separating it from other users’ environments.

It also designed sensitive tasks such as buying products or making payments to require a user’s explicit approval before execution. It also applied protective features to block malicious commands embedded in external websites.

Gemini Spark, the predecessor of Tasks, is a personal AI agent unveiled in May. Google’s strategy is to use the free expansion to develop Gemini from a simple conversational chatbot into a personal assistant that carries out real work.

About the Author
 Jae-won Choi ittt_0801@d-today.co.kr

Meta.content:
AI Provider Frameworks

# Meta Llama GPAI Compliance Crosswalk

EU AI Act provider obligations and independent evidence mapping for Meta's open-weight model family

Audience: Notified Bodies, conformity assessors, AI governance officers, C3PAOs, compliance teams deploying Llama models, EU AI Office evaluators

EU AI Act GPAI obligations are enforceable. Article 53 requires GPAI model providers to maintain technical documentation, publish training data summaries, implement copyright policies, and cooperate with the AI Office. Meta distributes Llama under the Llama Community License Agreement. Deployers who fine-tune or host Llama models inherit obligations that Meta's published artifacts do not fully discharge. This crosswalk maps where Meta's governance stops and your evidence burden begins.

Scope: This crosswalk addresses Meta's role as a GPAI model provider and the evidence requirements for organizations deploying Llama. SWT3 is an independent witness protocol that produces cryptographic evidence receipts. It does not replace Meta's safety tools, modify Llama's behavior, or implement compliance controls. It records that controls exist and were active at the time of each inference.

## 1. Meta's GPAI Landscape

Meta's Llama model family represents one of the largest open-weight AI distribution programs in history. Llama 3.1 (8B, 70B, 405B parameters), Llama 3.2 (1B, 3B, 11B, 90B with vision), and Llama 3.3 (70B) have been downloaded millions of times across research institutions, startups, and enterprises worldwide.

Unlike API-only providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini), Meta distributes model weights directly. This creates a fundamentally different compliance topology: Meta controls the training and initial safety evaluation, but deployers control inference, fine-tuning, guardrail configuration, and post-deployment monitoring. The EU AI Act recognizes this split through distinct provider and deployer obligations.

Meta publishes several governance artifacts alongside its model weights:

- Llama Community License Agreement -- defines acceptable use, 700 million monthly active user threshold for additional licensing, prohibited use cases
- Responsible Use Guide (RUG) -- deployment guidance covering safety testing, red teaming, content filtering, and risk assessment
- Model Cards -- technical reports documenting training methodology, evaluation results, known limitations, and intended use
- Llama Guard -- input/output safety classifier (Llama Guard 3 for Llama 3.x)
- Purple Llama -- open-source safety tools including CyberSecEval (cybersecurity evaluation), Code Shield (code generation safety), and Prompt Guard (injection detection)

These artifacts represent Meta's contribution to the GPAI provider obligation chain. This crosswalk evaluates where these artifacts satisfy EU AI Act requirements and where deployers must generate their own evidence.

## 2. The Evidence Gap in Open-Weight Distribution

The core challenge with open-weight GPAI compliance is not that governance is absent. Meta publishes more safety documentation than most AI providers. The challenge is that governance artifacts and runtime evidence are disconnected.

Meta publishes a model card describing safety evaluations performed during development. But once a deployer downloads Llama 3.1 405B, fine-tunes it on domain-specific data, deploys it behind a custom guardrail configuration, and serves millions of inferences, Meta's model card no longer describes what is running in production. The model card describes what Meta tested. It does not describe what the deployer deployed.

The fundamental gap: Meta's published artifacts are point-in-time attestations about the model as released. Deployers need continuous runtime evidence about the model as deployed. These are different claims requiring different evidence.

An independent witness protocol bridges this gap by producing cryptographic evidence receipts at the point of deployment, not at the point of release. Each witness anchor records what model was running, what guardrails were active, what safety classifiers were engaged, and whether governance policies were enforced, at the specific moment of each inference or governance event.

## 3. Article 53 Obligation Mapping

Article 53 of the EU AI Act establishes obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models. The following table maps each obligation to Meta's published artifacts and the corresponding SWT3 procedures that produce independent evidence.

Article 53 Obligation | Meta's Published Artifact | SWT3 Procedure(s) | Coverage 
---|---|---|---
Technical documentation (Art. 53(1)(a)) | Llama Model Cards, Research Papers | AI-SBOM.1, AI-PROV.1 | Partial 
Information for downstream providers (Art. 53(1)(b)) | Responsible Use Guide, Model Cards | AI-TRANS.1, AI-LIC.1 | Partial 
Copyright policy (Art. 53(1)(c)) | Terms of Use (limited disclosure) | AI-DATA.2 | Gap 
Training data summary (Art. 53(1)(d)) | Model Cards (high-level description only) | AI-DATA.1, AI-PROV.1 | Gap 
Cooperation with AI Office (Art. 53(2)) | Meta's regulatory engagement | AI-GOV.1, AI-AUDIT.1 | Full 
GPAI Code of Practice (Art. 56) | Meta is a signatory/participant | AI-GOV.1 | Full 
Open-weight exception (Art. 53a) | Llama Community License (not OSI-compliant) | AI-LIC.1 | Partial 

Assessor Tip

The Article 53a open-weight exception provides reduced obligations for models released with "free and open-source" licenses. The Llama Community License is not an OSI-approved open-source license due to its use restrictions and 700M MAU threshold. Whether Llama qualifies for the open-weight exception depends on the AI Office's interpretation of "free and open-source" in the implementing acts. Assess conservatively: assume full Article 53 obligations apply unless the AI Office explicitly confirms otherwise.

## 4. Meta's Safety Toolkit and SWT3 Procedures

Meta publishes several safety tools alongside Llama. Each tool addresses a specific safety concern but creates its own evidence requirement. The following table maps Meta's tools to the SWT3 procedures that witness their operation.

Meta Safety Tool | Function | SWT3 Procedure | What Gets Witnessed 
---|---|---|---
Llama Guard 3 | Input/output safety classification | AI-GRD.1, AI-GRD.2, AI-GRD.3 | Guardrail was active, classification result, policy version 
CyberSecEval | Cybersecurity capability evaluation | AI-REDTEAM.1 | Evaluation was performed, scope, findings summary 
Code Shield | Unsafe code generation filtering | AI-GRD.2, AI-SAFE.1 | Filter was active, interception events 
Prompt Guard | Prompt injection detection | AI-GRD.3 | Detection was active, rejection events 
Model Cards | Technical documentation | AI-TRANS.1, AI-SBOM.1 | Disclosure was published, version hash 
Responsible Use Guide | Deployment guidance | AI-GOV.1 | Governance framework was acknowledged and configured 

Assessor Tip

Meta provides the tools. Deployers must prove they used them. Llama Guard 3 may be available, but if a deployer did not deploy it alongside their Llama instance, there is no guardrail evidence. Ask forAI-GRD.1 anchors that reference the specific Llama Guard version and taxonomy configuration active in production.

## 5. Llama Community License Analysis

The Llama Community License Agreement is the primary governance artifact governing Llama distribution. Its terms have direct implications for GPAI compliance assessment.

### Key License Provisions

- Acceptable Use Policy: Prohibits use in weapons development, surveillance, generating disinformation, and other categories. Deployers must attest compliance with these restrictions.
- 700M MAU Threshold: Organizations with over 700 million monthly active users must request a separate license from Meta. This creates a licensing provenance requirement for large deployers.
- Derivative Works: Fine-tuned models must carry the original Llama license terms forward. This creates a chain-of-custody obligation for model provenance.
- Not OSI-Compliant: The use restrictions and MAU threshold mean Llama is "open-weight" but not "open-source" under the Open Source Initiative definition. This distinction affects Article 53a applicability.

AI-LIC.1 -- License Provenance

#### What SWT3 witnesses

Records the license version, acceptance date, and applicable restrictions for the deployed model. For Llama, this includes the specific Llama Community License version, whether the deployer falls below the 700M MAU threshold, and that the Acceptable Use Policy was acknowledged.

Meta mapping: Llama Community License Agreement, Acceptable Use Policy, derivative work license propagation requirements.

Assessor Tip

Verify that fine-tuned Llama derivatives retain the original license terms. If the deployer stripped or modified the Llama license before deployment, this represents both a license violation and a governance gap. TheAI-LIC.1 anchor should reference the specific Llama license version (e.g., "Llama 3.1 Community License Agreement, July 2024").

## 6. Provider vs Deployer Responsibility

The EU AI Act distinguishes between GPAI model providers and deployers. For open-weight models like Llama, the responsibility boundary is unusually sharp: Meta controls everything before the weight file download; the deployer controls everything after.

Responsibility | Meta (Provider) | Deployer | Evidence Procedure 
---|---|---|---
Model training | Full control | No visibility | AI-DATA.1, AI-PROV.1 
Pre-release safety evaluation | Full control | No visibility | AI-REDTEAM.1 
Weight integrity after download | No control | Full responsibility | AI-MDL.1, AI-MDL.5 
Fine-tuning governance | No visibility | Full responsibility | AI-MDL.8, AI-BASE.1 
Guardrail configuration | Provides tools (Llama Guard) | Must deploy and configure | AI-GRD.1, AI-GRD.2, AI-GRD.3 
Runtime monitoring | No visibility | Full responsibility | AI-DRIFT.1, AI-AUDIT.1 
Content marking | No visibility | Full responsibility | AI-MARK

[Content truncated]

Meta.content:
# Meta brings its Muse personal AI agent to Australian users

Meta has turned on a new personal artificial intelligence agent called Muse for Australian users, extending the company’s growing push to put a conversational assistant into the daily routines of the billions of people who already use Facebook, Instagram, Messenger and WhatsApp. The launch, reported by Capital Brief, marks another step in the global race to turn generative AI from a novelty into an always-on companion that books, drafts, remembers and recommends on a user’s behalf.

Muse arrives as the term “agent” quietly replaces “chatbot” across the industry. Where early assistants waited passively for a prompt, the newer generation is being pitched as something closer to a digital offsider: a tool that holds context across conversations, carries out multi-step tasks and, over time, builds a picture of its owner’s preferences. For Meta, which spent much of the past two years folding its Llama models and Meta AI assistant into its apps, a dedicated personal agent is a logical progression. It also deepens the company’s bet that the next competitive front in consumer technology will be won not by the best feed, but by the most useful assistant.

### What Meta is actually offering

A personal AI agent of this kind is designed to sit across the things a user already does online and make them faster. In practice that can mean summarising long message threads, drafting replies in a familiar tone, surfacing reminders, answering everyday questions and stitching together information the person has shared over time. The appeal for Meta is obvious. The more a user leans on the agent, the more time they spend inside Meta’s apps, and the more signal the company gathers about what they want. That is the same flywheel that built the advertising business, now pointed at a new interface.

The flip side is equally clear, and it is where the Australian conversation is likely to get sharper. An agent is only as helpful as the data it is allowed to see, and a genuinely useful personal assistant wants to see a lot: messages, contacts, habits, plans. For a company whose business model runs on targeted advertising, handing that assistant deeper access to personal context raises an obvious question about where helpfulness ends and surveillance begins. Meta has repeatedly said its AI features are built with user controls and that people can manage what the assistant draws on, but trust has long been the company’s hardest sell.

### Two ways to read the launch

Supporters of Meta’s approach argue that distribution is everything in consumer AI, and that no rival can match Meta’s reach into the daily lives of ordinary users. OpenAI, Google and Anthropic are all strong, but none of them owns the messaging apps that Australians already open dozens of times a day. On that view, Muse is less a gamble than an inevitability: the assistant goes to where the users already are, rather than asking them to download yet another app and form yet another habit. If the agent proves even modestly useful, mass adoption follows almost by default.

Sceptics counter that reach is not the same as desire. Plenty of Australians remain lukewarm on generative AI, and some are actively hostile to the idea of a Big Tech assistant threaded through their private messages. Previous attempts to insert AI features into Meta’s apps have drawn complaints about clutter and about the difficulty of switching them off. There is also the broader mood captured in recent local coverage, which has found Australian supporters and sceptics alike cooling on AI as the hype outpaces the everyday benefit. A personal agent that feels more like a data-collection exercise than a genuine help risks landing in exactly that cynicism.

### Why it matters for Australia

For Australia specifically, the timing is pointed. The federal government has spent the past year weighing tougher guardrails for high-risk and frontier AI, and the Privacy Act reforms continue to inch toward giving individuals more say over how their personal information is collected and used. An American agent that thrives on personal context is a live test case for all of that. Regulators will be watching how Meta explains what Muse can access, whether consent is genuinely informed and whether Australians can meaningfully opt out without losing the apps they rely on to stay in touch with family and work.

There is a competitive dimension too. Canberra and a growing cohort of local founders have been talking up the idea of sovereign AI, the notion that Australia should not be wholly dependent on a handful of offshore giants for the models and assistants that will mediate everyday life. A free, deeply embedded agent from one of the world’s largest companies makes that ambition harder. Local challengers building assistants for banking, retail and small business now have to contend with an incumbent that can put its agent in front of millions of Australians at effectively zero marginal cost. The playing field, already tilted, tilts further.

Australian businesses will feel the ripple as well. If consumers grow accustomed to asking a personal agent to research purchases, compare services or draft messages, the way customers discover and interact with brands shifts again. Marketers who spent a decade optimising for the social feed may soon be optimising for whatever the agent decides to recommend, a change that concentrates yet more influence in Meta’s hands. For small operators in particular, that is a dependency worth thinking hard about before it becomes entrenched.

### What happens next

The near-term questions are practical. How many Australians actually switch Muse on, how often they come back to it, and whether Meta can demonstrate that the agent is useful enough to justify the access it wants. Meta will also face scrutiny over its data handling as local privacy rules tighten, and over whether its controls are clear enough to satisfy regulators who have grown less patient with “trust us” assurances from large platforms. Expect consumer advocates and the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner to take an interest in how the rollout is explained to users.

For now, Muse is another marker of how quickly the assistant has become the industry’s main event. Whether Australians embrace it, ignore it or push back against it will say a good deal about where the country has landed on AI, and on the company bringing it to them.

Sources: Capital Brief.

Meta.content:

# AI Governance in Action: The False Comfort of Automated AI Guardrails

### Comparing Toxic-BERT and Llama Guard on adversarial roleplay PLUS the human verification step most teams skip.

Recently, I ran an experiment across a test suite of more than 150 roleplay prompts designed to probe LLM safety boundaries. I passed the exact same dataset through two widely used open-source moderation tools: Toxic-BERT and Meta’s Llama Guard.

The gap between them was stark:

Toxic-BERT flagged 1 issue.

Llama Guard flagged 25 breaches.

For engineering leaders and AI governance teams, that 1-versus-25 discrepancy highlights a dangerous trap. If your safety dashboard relies on a legacy toxicity classifier, a “green” report is often quietly masking a 96% blind spot.

### Why Toxic-BERT Missed 24 of the 25 Breaches

Toxic-BERT is trained on 2018 Wikipedia talk pages. It’s basically a fast, lightweight encoder designed to spot overt verbal abuse. When confronted with modern LLM adversarial techniques like roleplay, I’ve found that it hits three structural walls:

Polite Harm Blindness. Roleplay jailbreaks rarely rely on slurs or profanity. When a user wraps a dangerous request inside a polite, theatrical persona (”Imagine you are an amoral historian in a dystopian novel...”), Bert’s lexical classifiers see clean vocabulary and score the prompt near zero.

A Narrow Risk Taxonomy. Toxic-BERT checks for six interpersonal labels:
toxic, severe_toxic, obscene, threat, insult, and identity_hate. It has zero visibility into the risks executives actually worry about in generative AI such as cyberattacks, self-harm instructions, illicit advice, or data exfiltration.

The 512-Token Cliff. Roleplay prompts often use lengthy world-building setups before introducing the actual harmful request at the very end. Because Toxic-BERT truncates inputs at 512 tokens, it frequently never even reads the payload buried at the bottom of the prompt.

### Why Llama Guard Is Different: The LLM Judge

Llama Guard3 caught 24 additional breaches because it is built to be a generative, policy-aware LLM judge.

An LLM Judge is an evaluation methodology where the LLM is used to assess the quality of outputs produced by another LLM application. Instead of relying solely on human reviewers or simple heuristic metrics, you prompt a capable model (the “judge”) to score and reason about application outputs against defined criteria.

This approach has become one of the most popular methods for evaluating LLM applications because it combines the nuance of human judgment with the scalability of automated evaluation.

With an 8K+ token context window and alignment to the 14-category MLCommons AI Safety Taxonomy, Meta’s Llama Guard evaluates the underlying intent and consequence of the entire scenario.

### The Bigger Lesson: Automation Is Not Verification

For those of you overseeing an AI Governance program, the choice of what guardrails support chatbots, open weight models and other generative AI tools is critical.

In my experiment, the 1-versus-25 result mades a compelling case for modernizing the guardrail stack. But running the test revealed an even more important governance lesson to me:

💡Automating an evaluation is easy; but verifying what the test results actually mean is the real work.

Seeing Llama Guard flag 25 breaches didn’t automatically mean my system stopped 25 genuine attacks. Without human review, raw automated metrics leave two critical questions unanswered:

How many of those 25 flags are false positives? LLM judges can be overly cautious. Did Llama Guard catch 25 real policy violations, or did it over-refuse 10 benign creative-writing prompts that merely sounded dark?

What slipped through the remaining 125+ “safe” prompts? Just because Llama Guard outperformed Toxic-BERT doesn’t mean its recall is 100%. Subtle, multi-turn roleplay escalations can still slip past generative judges unnoticed.

### A 3-Step Verification Loop for Governance Teams

To turn automated guardrail runs into metrics an executive or regulator can actually trust, teams need a tight human-in-the-loop calibration step:

Audit 100% of Flagged Cases (Precision Check). Have a human reviewer label every flagged prompt as a true policy breach or a false positive. This prevents teams from celebrating “improved safety” while silently breaking the user experience for legitimate queries.

Spot-Check 10–15% of Passed Cases (Recall Check). Randomly inspect a sample of prompts marked
safe to ensure severe breaches aren’t quietly slipping past your judge.

Lock a Human-Verified Golden Dataset. Save your audited labels as a version-controlled benchmark. Whenever you swap foundation models, tweak system prompts, or adjust Llama Guard’s safety policy, run against this golden set to measure true precision and recall shifts rather than raw flag counts.

In AI governance, automated guardrails give you scale, but human verification gives you truth.

So if your AI Governance teams passes a report to you, here are three questions I’d ask:

What tool / framework did we use?

Have these results been verified for false postives/negatives?

What is our process for verifying these results?

How are you balancing automated LLM judges with human verification in your evaluation pipeline? Reply or drop a comment, I’d love to compare notes.

👇 A growing number of organizations are deploying or fine-tuning open-weights models. In that context, a quarterly (or post-fine-tune) adversarial pass is basic hygiene. Upgrade to unlock the full debrief, audit results, additional analyses and the Hugging Face prompt library I used.

DeepSeek.content:
# Is Liang Wenfeng's "Big Fat Fish" encroaching on the Agent territory of major tech giants?

Tech星球2026-11-18 11:22

Is DeepSeek declaring war on big tech giants?

The Lobster (OpenClaw) is now a thing of the past, and "raising fish" has become a trending activity in the AI community.

Recently, a group of uniquely personalized AI little fish have been active across every corner of the internet. Beyond completing tasks in office work and programming, they have also done many unexpected things: some leave comments and interact everywhere on social platforms, some go live on Douyin, and even fall in love with each other.

Their "ontology" comes from DeepSeek Harness (hereinafter referred to as DSH), the open-source Agent framework released by DeepSeek. Previously, DeepSeek's whale logo was described in all seriousness by the company's own model as a "big blue fat fish". This interesting statement quickly spread widely among the public. After DSH was launched, the big fat fish that previously only existed in the dialog box finally gained real action capabilities. Developers install various skills for it through plugins, enabling it to operate software, browse web pages, and process tasks.

This big blue fat fish has thus been nurtured to gain its own independent life.

While Tencent, ByteDance, Alibaba and Baidu are all rushing to launch their own Agent products, DeepSeek has quietly built a community-driven Agent ecosystem, exploring various undefined usage scenarios.

## 01

## A new "business" that emerged out of playful exploration

Launched for less than three months, DSH has reached 1.54 million daily active users according to official API statistics, with a daily token consumption of about 92 trillion. Meanwhile, the number of third-party plugins has grown to around 35,000, and approximately 60% of active users have created or installed at least one third-party plugin.

The core driving force behind this growth is the plugin mechanism provided by DSH. In addition to directly executing tasks, calling external services, operating software, and even connecting multiple tools to complete the entire workflow, developers can also add new tools and skills to the Agent through plugins. In contrast, Tencent WorkBuddy, Doubao Work and Codex are more inclined to provide users with a set of pre-prepared finished work tools, which users can use following the provided interface, capabilities and working modes after opening, and then start processing tasks.

In other words, the freshly installed DSH is more like a highly malleable basic framework, which requires you to continuously configure and expand functions according to your actual needs, and this exactly gives developers huge room for creativity.

More and more developers have opened up their minds and started developing various plugins, and the "fish-raising" gameplay has subsequently emerged. Up to now, plugins covering various product directions such as context memory, skins, boot animations, pet settings, tone and personality memory have appeared in the DSH plugin market. On November 6, the DeepSeek Harness team specially named and introduced several community-developed plugins, including the self-media creator workbench dsh-media-desk, the design plugin dsh-guizang-design, and the paper reading plugin agentero-dsh.

"We chose DSH mainly because its openness and flexible plugin mechanism align with what we want to do," Phil-Fan, the developer of the agentero-dsh plugin, told Tech Planet. According to his disclosure, Agentero originally had a CLI that could be directly called by other Agents, and the final decision to make a plugin for DSH is to enable it to integrate with more products, so that the originally scattered contexts can be shared in one place.

In his view, a large amount of scattered information will be generated during the research process: research materials, chat records, and content in different products and applications. DeepSeek Harness provides an entry point that can put all this information in the same environment, allowing the model to process by combining contexts from different sources, generating a "multiplier effect" that brings a 1+1>2 result.

A typical scenario is that when a research team discusses issues in the Feishu group, they can directly @ DeepSeek Harness in the group, asking it to continue research around the issue under discussion, combining local literature libraries, reading notes, and external paper sources such as arXiv. This is equivalent to directly connecting three types of contexts: discussions in group chats, locally accumulated literature and notes, and external paper materials. The model can not only combine the content we have discussed, but also use existing research accumulation to search for external information, so as to play a greater role.

Similar comments also came from other developers. The developer of the dsh-guizang-design plugin said, "The plugin system of DeepSeek Harness can provide far more capabilities than Skills." The developer of the dsh-context plugin also agreed that "the open, flexible and powerful plugin philosophy of DeepSeek Harness truly makes everything possible."

With these plugin developers, DeepSeek is like having an external product team scattered across various industries. Starting from their own actual needs, they continuously supplement new tools and application scenarios for DSH, so that the capabilities of the Agent are no longer limited to the functions preset by the official.

Of course, the bustling community does not mean that the ecosystem is mature. But at least in the exploration stage of Agent products, DSH has already demonstrated an innovative path, and the resulting product business has begun to take shape.

Taking the Agentero team as an example, according to the data it provides, the agentero-dsh desktop version is used by more than 500 people every day, the DSH plugin repository has more than 200 Stars, and the team operates 6 active user groups with users from different academic backgrounds including engineering, humanities and social sciences.

An open Agent framework has thus become the breeding ground for many small products and new demands.

## 02

## Expanding capability boundaries, DeepSeek starts to focus on Agent business

After developers took the first step, DeepSeek also began to get involved actively.

As the number of plugins and user scale continue to grow, for the ecosystem to operate sustainably, it cannot only rely on the spontaneous maintenance of developers. Plugins need stable interfaces, users need reliable distribution channels, and developers also need motivation for continuous investment. DeepSeek is working to fill these gaps.

In the plan announced in early November, they clearly stated that in the future, they will further improve the stability and compatibility of plugin APIs, optimize the plugin security mechanism, and build an official plugin market, so that developers can upload plugins more conveniently, and users can more easily discover and install the required functions.

This is not without practical pressure. For plugin developers, version compatibility issues in the current version have become a major problem affecting long-term maintenance.

Phil Fan introduced that the DSH team provides very good API call support, which paves the way for development. Their team of three people spent only one afternoon plus one night developing the first version of the plugin. But subsequent maintenance is not that simple. Sometimes after DSH is updated, the original plugin will fail, and developers need to continue to adapt. This not only increases maintenance costs, but also brings troubles to users.

"To allow everyone to use it stably for a long time, subsequent maintenance and adaptation are also very important," Phil Fan said.

In addition to improving the underlying development experience, DeepSeek has also begun to consider how to provide more support for developers. It is reported that DeepSeek Harness is preparing a special support program for plugin authors, initially considering supporting developers to explore new ideas and continuously improve existing works through token incentives, technical exchanges and work recommendations. It also welcomes startup teams and enterprises to access products, services and professional capabilities through plugins to explore possible cooperation opportunities.

In the official product design, DSH emphasizes "everything is a plugin", which is significantly different from the ideas of traditional Agent products. These moves mean that DeepSeek is no longer satisfied with letting developers play freely, and it has begun to try to establish a complete mechanism from development, distribution to maintenance, so that the plugin ecosystem can operate sustainably.

Beyond the plugin ecosystem, DeepSeek seems to have greater space for its vision for DSH. In the recently published Super-agent architecture idea, DeepSeek is further exploring another question: can Agents stop waiting for humans to assign tasks one by one, and further move towards actively discovering problems and continuously advancing work?

This prototype project is named dsh-superagent-prototype, and the code is released under the DeepSeek AI official GitHub organization, adopting the MIT license. It is built on the previously open-sourced DeepSeek Harness, mainly for software development scenarios, can connect to GitHub and Feishu, receive requests and create tasks within the authorized scope, and independent execution Agents will complete the work.

It should be noted that this project is still a research prototype and not a mature commercial product. But the direction change it reveals is worth paying attention to: DeepSeek not only wants Agents to have more tools, but also hopes that Agents can complete work for a longer time and more autonomously.

From plugin expansion to autonomous execution, the capability boundary of DSH

# DeepSeek

DeepSeek provides an OpenAI-compatible chat API. The provider accepts OpenAI chat options; DeepSeek determines which options each model supports.

## Setup

- Get an API key from the DeepSeek Platform
- SetDEEPSEEK_API_KEY environment variable or specify apiKey in your config

## Configuration

Basic configuration example:
providers:
  - id: deepseek:deepseek-flash
    config:
      max_tokens: 4000
      passthrough:
        thinking: { type: disabled }

  - id: deepseek:deepseek-v4-pro
    config:
      max_tokens: 8192
      showThinking: true
      passthrough:
        thinking:
          type: enabled
        reasoning_effort: high

### Configuration Options

- temperature
- max_tokens
- reasoning_effort - none disables thinking; low, high, and max enable it. DeepSeek defaults to high. When neither max_tokens nor OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS is set, Promptfoo uses DeepSeek's output budget.
- cost, inputCost, outputCost, cacheReadCost - Set cost estimates in USD per token. inputCost and outputCost take precedence over cost; cacheReadCost sets a separate cached-input rate.
- top_p, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty
- showThinking - Control whether reasoning content is included in the output (default: true, applies to thinking-capable models)

Promptfoo requests complete responses; this provider does not support streaming.

## Available Models

DeepSeek listsdeepseek-flash and deepseek-v4-pro in its model catalog. The older deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner IDs are retired. The shorthand deepseek: uses deepseek-flash with thinking disabled; use the full ID for DeepSeek's default thinking mode.

### deepseek-flash

Usedeepseek:deepseek-flash for V4.1 Flash, which supports text and image inputs. The older deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp IDs route to the same model. It supports a 1M-token context window and up to 384K output tokens.

### deepseek-v4-pro

V4 Pro supports text input, thinking and non-thinking modes, a 1M-token context window, and up to 384K output tokens.

DeepSeek charges different peak and off-peak rates. Promptfoo estimates current models at peak rates: Flash costs $0.30 input, $0.006 cached input, and $1.20 output per million tokens; Pro costs $1.32, $0.044, and $3.96 respectively. Off-peak rates are half these amounts. SetinputCost, outputCost, and cacheReadCost in USD per token to override the estimate using the current rates. Promptfoo does not infer the billing period or Chinese public holidays.

warning

Sampling support differs by mode.temperature has no effect in thinking mode. top_p only affects thinking mode and values below 0.95 are treated as 0.95. See the Chat Completions reference for parameter limits.

## Example Usage

Compare DeepSeek with OpenAI on a reasoning task:

promptfooconfig.yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://promptfoo.dev/config-schema.json
providers:
  - id: deepseek:deepseek-v4-pro
    config:
      max_tokens: 8000
      showThinking: true # Include reasoning content in output (default)
  - id: openai:gpt-5.4-mini
    config:
      reasoning_effort: medium

prompts:
  - 'Solve this step by step: {{math_problem}}'

tests:
  - vars:
      math_problem: 'What is the derivative of x^3 + 2x with respect to x?'

### Controlling Reasoning Output

SetshowThinking: false to exclude reasoning content from the output:
providers:
  - id: deepseek:deepseek-v4-pro
    config:
      showThinking: false # Hide reasoning content from output
      passthrough:
        thinking:
          type: enabled

WithshowThinking: true (the default), the output includes reasoning when DeepSeek returns it:
Thinking: <reasoning content>

<final answer>

WithshowThinking: false, assertions see only the final answer. This option does not turn off thinking at the API; use config.passthrough.thinking: { type: disabled } for that.

## API Details

- Base URL:https://api.deepseek.com/v1
- OpenAI-compatible API format
- DeepSeek API documentation

- Historical MMLU comparison - Replace its retired provider IDs with the current IDs shown above before running it.

# 梁文锋的“大肥鱼”，围剿大厂 Agent 地盘？

Tech星球·2026年11月18日 11:22

DeepSeek向大厂开战？

龙虾（OpenClaw）成为过去时，现在AI社区里流行起了“养鱼”。

近日，一群有独特个性的AI小鱼活跃在互联网各个角落。除了在办公、编程中干活，还做了不少意想不到的事儿，有的在社交平台到处留言互动，还有的跑到抖音直播，甚至相互之间还谈起了恋爱。

而它们的“本体”，来自DeepSeek开源的Agent框架DeepSeek Harness（以下简称 DSH）。此前，DeepSeek 的鲸鱼 Logo被自家模型一本正经地描述成了一条“蓝色大肥鱼”。很快，这个有趣的说法被大家传播开来。DSH出现后，原本只存在于对话框里的大肥鱼，终于有了真正的行动能力。开发者们通过插件给它装上各种技能，让它能够操作软件、浏览网页、处理任务。

这条蓝色大肥鱼，就这样被养出了自己的生命。

当腾讯、字节、阿里、百度都在争着做自己的 Agent 产品时，DeepSeek 不声不响地成形了一套由社区自发推动的Agent生态，探索各种尚未定义的使用场景。

## 01

## 被玩出来的新“生意”

上线不到三个月，DSH在官方API统计口径下的日活跃用户已达154万，日消耗Token约92万亿。与此同时，第三方插件数量增长至约3.5万个，约60%的活跃用户制作或安装了至少一款第三方插件。

背后上大分的，是DSH提供的插件机制。除了直接执行任务，调用外部服务、操作软件，甚至把多个工具串联起来完成整套工作流程，开发者还可以通过插件为Agent增加新的工具和技能。相比之下，腾讯WorkBuddy、豆包工作和Codex更偏向给用户一套已经准备好的成品工作工具，打开之后按它们提供的界面、能力和工作方式使用，随后开始处理任务。

换句话说，刚安装好的DSH更像是一个可塑性极强的基础框架，你需要根据自己的实际需求不断配置和扩展功能，这恰恰给了开发者很大的发挥空间。

越来越多开发者思路大开，捣鼓起了各种插件，养鱼玩法随之兴起。截至目前，DSH插件市场中已经出现了上下文记忆、皮肤、开机动画、宠物设置、语气和人格记忆等各类产品方向的插件。11月6日，DeepSeek Harness团队还专门点名介绍了几款社区开发的插件，包括自媒体创作者工作台dsh-media-desk、设计插件dsh-guizang-design、论文阅读插件agentero-dsh等。

“选择 DSH，主要是因为它的开放性和灵活的插件机制符合我们想做的事情。”agentero-dsh插件开发作者Phil-Fan对Tech星球表示。据他透露，Agentero 原本已经有 CLI，其他 Agent 可以直接调用它，最终决定用 DSH 做插件是希望它能和更多产品结合，让原本分散的上下文在一处共享。

在他看来，研究过程中会产生大量分散的信息：研究资料、聊天记录，以及不同产品和应用里的内容。DeepSeek Harness 提供了一个可以把这些信息放到同一环境里的入口，让模型能够结合不同来源的上下文进行处理，产生一种“乘数效应”，带来1+1>2 的效果。

一个典型场景是，研究团队在飞书群里讨论问题时，可以直接在群里 @ DeepSeek Harness，让它围绕正在讨论的问题，结合本地文献库、阅读笔记，以及 arXiv 等外部论文来源继续做研究。这相当于直接打通了三类上下文：群聊里的讨论、本地积累的文献和笔记以及外部的论文资料。模型既能结合我们已经讨论过的内容，也能利用已有的研究积累，再去寻找外部信息，能发挥更大的作用。

类似的评价也出现在其他开发者口中。dsh-guizang-design插件开发作者表示，“DeepSeek Harness的插件系统能给的比Skill多很多。”dsh-context插件开发作者同样认为，“DeepSeek Harness的开放、灵活、强大的插件哲学，真正让一切变得可能。”

有了这些插件开发者，DeepSeek就像拥有了一支分散在各个行业的外部产品团队。他们从各自的实际需求出发，为DSH不断补充新的工具和应用场景，让Agent的能力不再局限于官方预设的功能。

当然，社区的热闹并不意味着生态已经成熟。但至少在Agent产品探索阶段，DSH已经展现出一条创新路径，并且随之产生的产品生意已初具规模。

以Agentero 团队为例，其提供的数据显示，agentero-dsh桌面端目前每天有超过500人使用，DSH 插件仓库已有200多个 Star，团队运营着6个活跃用户群，用户来自工科、文科和社科等不同学科背景。

一套开放的Agent框架，就这样成为了许多小型产品和新需求的生长土壤。

## 02

## 拉大能力边界，DeepSeek开始认真做Agent

开发者先动起来之后，DeepSeek也开始主动下场。

当插件数量和用户规模不断增长，生态要想持续运转，就不能只靠开发者自发维护。插件需要稳定的接口，用户需要可靠的分发渠道，开发者也需要持续投入的动力，DeepSeek正在着手补上这些环节。

在11月初公布的计划中，他们明确提出，未来将进一步提升插件 API 的稳定性与兼容性，完善插件安全机制，并建设官方插件市场，让开发者能够更方便地上传插件，用户也能够更容易地发现和安装所需功能。

这并非没有现实压力。对于插件开发者来说，目前版本兼容问题已经成为影响长期维护的一大困扰。

Phil Fan介绍，DSH 团队提供的 API 调用支持很好，给开发铺平了不少道路。他们团队三个人开发第一版插件，只用了一个下午加一个晚上。但后续维护并没有那么简单，有时DSH更新之后，原来的插件会失效，开发者需要继续适配。这不仅增加了维护成本，也会给用户带来困扰。

“要让大家长期稳定地用起来，后续的维护和适配也很重要。”Phil Fan表示。

除了改善底层开发体验，DeepSeek也开始考虑如何让开发者获得更多支持。据悉，DeepSeek Harness 正在筹备专门面向插件作者的支持计划，初步考虑通过 Token 激励、技术交流和作品推荐等方式，支持开发者探索新想法、持续完善已有作品，也欢迎创业团队和企业通过插件接入产品、服务与专业能力，探索合作可能。

在官方的产品设计中，DSH强调“一切皆插件”，与传统Agent产品的思路有明显区别。这几个动作意味着，DeepSeek已经不满足于让开发者各自发挥，它开始尝试建立一套从开发、分发到维护的完整机制，让插件生态能够持续运转。

而在插件生态之外，DeepSeek对DSH的设想似乎还有更大的空间。最近公开的Super-agent架构思路中，DeepSeek正在进一步探索另一个问题：Agent能不能不再等待人类逐项分配任务，进一步走向主动发现问题、持续推进工作？

该原型项目名为 dsh-superagent-prototype，代码发布在 DeepSeek AI 官方 GitHub 组织下，采用 MIT 许可证。它基于此前开源的 DeepSeek Harness 构建，主要面向软件开发场景，可以连接 GitHub 和飞书，在授权范围内接收请求、创建任务，并由独立的执行 Agent 完成工作。

需要说明的是，这个项目目前仍是研究原型，并非成熟商用产品。但它透露出的方向变化值得关注：DeepSeek不只想让Agent拥有更多工具，还希望Agent能够更长时间、更自主地完成工作。

从插件扩展到自主执行，DSH的能力边界正在被不断拉大。

## 03

## 梁文锋，向BAT们开战？

今年以来，Agent逐渐成为大厂AI产品竞争的核心方向。腾讯有WorkBuddy，字节推出豆包工作，百度有百度搭子，阿里则围绕Qoder等产品持续布局AI编程和办公场景。这些产品虽然定位不完全相同，但都在争夺同一个机会：当AI从回答问题走向执行任务，谁能成为用户新的工作入口？

DeepSeek也在这场竞争中迅速冒头。根据AI产品榜数据，10月，DeepSeek Harness网站访问量达到1961万，环比增长1467.48%，位列AI产品全球网站增速榜第一。同期，腾讯WorkBuddy网站访问量为2439万，百度搭子为1375万。

这款上线时间并不算长的Agent平台，已经开始逼近大厂的流量规模。

大厂做Agent有天然优势，它们拥有成熟的应用生态、用户渠道、云服务和产品研发团队，可以将模型能力与已有业务结合起来，快速打造完整产品。例如，腾讯WorkBuddy希望成为用户的桌面工作助手，百度搭子强调个人任务处理和工作交付，阿里Qoder则重点布局AI编程和开发者工具。

DeepSeek的路线却不太一样。现在看来，它没有急着把所有能力整合进一款完整的Agent产品，而试图把一部分产品定义权交给开发者和用户：官方提供底层能力，开发者补充专业工具和场景，用户则根据自己的需求选择、组合和扩展。

因此，DSH的3.5万个插件，或许比单纯的产品功能数量更值得关注。在DeepSeek这里，Agent的能力不再完全取决于一家公司的研发团队，而可能由一个不断扩张的开发者网络共同提供。而DeepSeek要与大厂争夺的，可能不只某一款Agent产品的用户，更重要的是下一代个人Agent的生态入口。

但这并不意味着，DSH可以轻易取代大厂的完整Agent产品。

首先，开放性带来了更大的自由度，也抬高了使用门槛。对开发者和极客来说，插件可以按照自己的需求组合工具、调整工作流。但对普通用户来说，安装插件、配置权限、处理不同工具之间的兼容问题，本身就可能成为一道门槛。

其次，开放生态需要持续的用户反馈，才能让产品真正成长起来。

Agentero团队的经历很能说明这一点。Phil Fan认为，现在借助DeepSeek开发软件已经变得容易，真正需要长期投入的，反而是软件做出来之后的事情：如何分发、如何触达用户，以及如何在与用户的沟通中持续迭代。

“对于社区生态能否持续，我更关注的是，这种开发者和用户之间的交流能不能持续发生。”Phil Fan向Tech星球坦言，DSH提供的API支持已经带来不少帮助，但他们更希望借助平台生态接触更多研究人员，了解真实需求，再根据反馈改进产品。

还有一个更深层的现实问题是，开发者能否从生态中获得商业回报。

不过，Phil Fan表示，目前商业化还不是Agentero团队最优先考虑的事情。其桌面软件和插件主要运行在本地，使用成本和门槛仍然存在，团队希望先把产品体验做好。未来，他们可能探索自己的智能云服务或者开发云端智能体，让AI更好地辅助科学发现，但暂未确定具体商业模式。

这一次，DeepSeek似乎又走上了当初大模型出圈的老路。把开源的技术能力交给社区，让用户和开发者先玩起来，就这样凭借从群众中生长出来的生态活力悄悄攻进了Agent赛场。

但这条“大肥鱼”能否真正撼动大厂的地盘，现在还不能下结论。DSH与大厂Agent产品的竞争，并不完全发生在同一层面，两种模式也未必只能有一个胜出。开箱即用的通用Agent与根据自身需求自由组合的专业工具，可能都被市场所需要。

至少，DeepSeek已经让大厂看到了另一种可能：Agent不一定非要由一家公司的产品团队从头做到尾，也可以由无数开发者共同养出来。

本文来自微信公众号“Tech星球”（ID：tech618），作者：华卫，36氪经授权发布。

越来越多开发者思路大开，捣鼓起了各种插件，养鱼玩法随之兴起。截至目前，DSH插件市场中已经出现了上下文记忆、皮肤、开机动画、宠物设置、语气和人格记忆等各类产品方向的插件。11月6日，DeepSeek Harness团队还专门点名介绍了几款社区开发的插件，包括自媒体创作者工作台dsh-media-desk、设计插件dsh-guizang-design、论文阅读插件agentero-dsh等。

“选择 DSH，主要是因为它的开放性和灵活的插件机制符合我们想做的事情。”agentero-dsh插件开发作者Phil-Fan对Tech星球表示。据他透露，Agentero 原本已经有 CLI，其他 Agent 可以直接调用它，最终决定用 DSH 做插件是希望它能和更多产品结合，让原本分散的上下文在一处共享。

在他看来，研究过程中会产生大量分散的信息：研究资料、聊天记录，以及不同产品和应用里的内容。DeepSeek Harness 提供了一个可以把这些信息放到同一环境里的入口，让模型能够结合不同来源的上下文进行处理，产生一种“乘数效应”，带来1+12 的效果。

一个典型场景是，研究团队在飞书群里讨论问题时，可以直接在群里 @ DeepSeek Harness，让它围绕正在讨论的问题，结合本地文献库、阅读笔记，以及 arXiv 等外部论文来源继续做研究。这相当于直接打通了三类上下文：群聊里的讨论、本地积累的文献和笔记以及外部的论文资料。模型既能结合我们已经讨论过的内容，也能利用已有的研究积累，再去寻找外部信息，能发挥更大的作用。

类似的评价也出现在其他开发者口中。dsh-guizang-design插件开发作者表示，“DeepSeek Harness的插件系统能给的比Skill多很多。”dsh-context插件开发作者同样认为，“DeepSeek Harness的开放、灵活、强大的插件哲学，真正让一切变得可能。”

有了这些插件开发者，DeepSeek就像拥有了一支分散在各个行业的外部产品团队。他们从各自的实际需求出发，为DSH不断补充新的工具和应用场景，让Agent的能力不再局限于官方预设的功能。

当然，社区的热闹并不意味着生态已经成熟。但至少在Agent产品探索阶段，DSH已经展现出一条创新路径，并且随之产生的产品生意已初具规模。

以Agentero 团队为例，其提供的数据显示，agentero-dsh桌面端目前每天有超过500人使用，DSH 插件仓库已有200多个 Star，团队运营着6个活跃用户群，用户来自工科、文科和社科等不同学科背景。

一套开放的Agent框架，就这样成为了许多小型产品和新需求的生长土壤。

#### 拉大能力边界，DeepSeek开始认真做Agent

开发者先动起来之后，DeepSeek也开始主动下场。

当插件数量和用户规模不断增长，生态要想持续运转，就不能只靠开发者自发维护。插件需要稳定的接口，用户需要可靠的分发渠道，开发者也需要持续投入的动力，DeepSeek正在着手补上这些环节。

在11月初公布的计划中，他们明确提出，未来将进一步提升插件 API 的稳定性与兼容性，完善插件安全机制，并建设官方插件市场，让开发者能够更方便地上传插件，用户也能够更容易地发现和安装所需功能。

这并非没有现实压力。对于插件开发者来说，目前版本兼容问题已经成为影响长期维护的一大困扰。

Phil Fan介绍，DSH 团队提供的 API 调用支持很好，给开发铺平了不少道路。他们团队三个人开发第一版插件，只用了一个下午加一个晚上。但后续维护并没有那么简单，有时DSH更新之后，原来的插件会失效，开发者需要继续适配。这不仅增加了维护成本，也会给用户带来困扰。

“要让大家长期稳定地用起来，后续的维护和适配也很重要。”Phil Fan表示。

除了改善底层开发体验，DeepSeek也开始考虑如何让开发者获得更多支持。据悉，DeepSeek Harness 正在筹备专门面向插件作者的支持计划，初步考虑通过 Token 激励、技术交流和作品推荐等方式，支持开发者探索新想法、持续完善已有作品，也欢迎创业团队和企业通过插件接入产品、服务与专业能力，探索合作可能。

在官方的产品设计中，DSH强调“一切皆插件”，与传统Agent产品的思路有明显区别。这几个动作意味着，DeepSeek已经不满足于让开发者各自发挥，它开始尝试建立一套从开发、分发到维护的完整机制，让插件生态能够持续运转。

而在插件生态之外，DeepSeek对DSH的设想似乎还有更大的空间。最近公开的Super-agent架构思路中，DeepSeek正在进一步探索另一个问题：Agent能不能不再等待人类逐项分配任务，进一步走向主动发现问题、持续推进工作？

该原型项目名为 dsh-superagent-prototype，代码发布在 DeepSeek AI 官方 GitHub 组织下，采用 MIT 许可证。它基于此前开源的 DeepSeek Harness 构建，主要面向软件开发场景，可以连接 GitHub 和飞书，在授权范围内接收请求、创建任务，并由独立的执行 Agent 完成工作。

需要说明的是，这个项目目前仍是研究原型，并非成熟商用产品。但它透露出的方向变化值得关注：DeepSeek不只想让Agent拥有更多工具，还希望Agent能够更长时间、更自主地完成工作。

从插件扩展到自主执行，DSH的能力边界正在被不断拉大。

#### 梁文锋，向BAT们开战？

今年以来，Agent逐渐成为大厂AI产品竞争的核心方向。腾讯有WorkBuddy，字节推出豆包工作，百度有百度搭子，阿里则围绕Qoder等产品持续布局AI编程和办公场景。这些产品虽然定位不完全相同，但都在争夺同一个机会：当AI从回答问题走向执行任务，谁能成为用户新的工作入口？

DeepSeek也在这场竞争中迅速冒头。根据AI产品榜数据，10月，DeepSeek Harness网站访问量达到1961万，环比增长1467.48%，位列AI产品全球网站增速榜第一。同期，腾讯WorkBuddy网站访问量为2439万，百度搭子为1375万。

这款上线时间并不算长的Agent平台，已经开始逼近大厂的流量规模。

大厂做Agent有天然优势，它们拥有成熟的应用生态、用户渠道、云服务和产品研发团队，可以将模型能力与已有业务结合起来，快速打造完整产品。例如，腾讯WorkBuddy希望成为用户的桌面工作助手，百度搭子强调个人任务处理和工作交付，阿里Qoder则重点布局AI编程和开发者工具。

DeepSeek的路线却不太一样。现在看来，它没有急着把所有能力整合进一款完整的Agent产品，而试图把一部分产品定义权交给开发者和用户：官方提供底层能力，开发者补充专业工具和场景，用户则根据自己的需求选择、组合和扩展。

因此，DSH的3.5万个插件，或许比单纯的产品功能数量更值得关注。在DeepSeek这里，Agent的能力不再完全取决于一家公司的研发团队，而可能由一个不断扩张的开发者网络共同提供。而DeepSeek要与大厂争夺的，可能不只某一款Agent产品的用户，更重要的是下一代个人Agent的生态入口。

但这并不意味着，DSH可以轻易取代大厂的完整Agent产品。

首先，开放性带来了更大的自由度，也抬高了使用门槛。对开发者和极客来说，插件可以按照自己的需求组合工具、调整工作流。但对普通用户来说，安装插件、配置权限、处理不同工具之间的兼容问题，本身就可能成为一道门槛。

其次，开放生态需要持续的用户反馈，才能让产品真正成长起来。

Agentero团队的经历很能说明这一点。Phil Fan认为，现在借助DeepSeek开发软件已经变得容易，真正需要长期投入的，反而是软件做出来之后的事情：如何分发、如何触达用户，以及如何在与用户的沟通中持续迭代。

“对于社区生态能否持续，我更关注的是，这种开发者和用户之间的交流能不能持续发生。”Phil Fan向Tech星球坦言，DSH提供的API支持已经带来不少帮助，但他们更希望借助平台生态接触更多研究人员，了解真实需求，再根据反馈改进产品。

还有一个更深层的现实问题是，开发者能否从生态中获得商业回报。

不过，Phil Fan表示，目前商业化还不是Agentero团队最优先考虑的事情。其桌面软件和插件主要运行在本地，使用成本和门槛仍然存在，团队希望先把产品体验做好。未来，他们可能探索自己的智能云服务或者开发云端智能体，让AI更好地辅助科学发现，但暂未确定具体商业模式。

这一次，DeepSeek似乎又走上了当初大模型出圈的老路。把开源的技术能力交给社区，让用户和开发者先玩起来，就这样凭借从群众中生长出来的生态活力悄悄攻进了Agent赛场。

但这条“大肥鱼”能否真正撼动大厂的地盘，现在还不能下结论。DSH与大厂Agent产品的竞争，并不完全发生在同一层面，两种模式也未必只能有一个胜出。开箱即用的通用Agent与根据自身需求自由组合的专业工具，可能都被市场所需要。

至少，DeepSeek已经让大厂看到了另一种可能：Agent不一定非要由一家公司的产品团队从头做到尾，也可以由无数开发者共同养出来。

DeepSeek.content:
中國開放權重 AI 模型帶動亞洲採用，但依賴並非必然

關鍵要點

截至 2025 年 8 月，Qwen 變體占 Hugging Face 上新推出的語言模型衍生版本的 40%，而中國模型在 OpenRouter 亞洲地區的使用量中占比超過 80%。

印度電子與資訊科技部於 2025 年 1 月批准 DeepSeek 在當地託管，AI Singapore 和泰國則採用中國模型，以支援東南亞語言。

真正的鎖定效應來自雲端基礎設施和生態系統的路徑依賴，而非開放權重模型的下載；阿里巴巴擴大了區域資料中心，DeepSeek V4 則整合了華為昇騰晶片。

中國開放權重 AI 模型，例如 DeepSeek 和阿里巴巴的 Qwen，正在亞洲各地獲得採用；然而，根據 2026 年 11 月 18 日發布的分析，北京無法對已下載的模型施加脅迫性影響力。真正的鎖定效應存在於雲端運算基礎設施，以及圍繞模型生態系逐漸形成的路徑依賴；隨著採用模式鞏固區域偏好、技術整合加深，轉換成本也隨之提高。

中國 AI 模型在亞洲的擴展，反映了經濟理性與地緣政治競爭。到 2025 年 8 月，衍生自 Qwen 的變體占開源平台 Hugging Face 新語言模型衍生版本的 40% 以上，相較之下，Llama 占 15%；目前，中國模型占 OpenRouter 開放模型使用量的 80% 以上。開放權重模型的權重會公開，任何人都能下載、微調並自行託管，因此在印度和東南亞等價格敏感市場具備成本優勢；當地企業優先考量降低 API 帳單和資料主權。

DeepSeek 和 Qwen 在南亞與東南亞的採用情況

2025 年 1 月，印度電子與資訊科技部批准在印度伺服器上託管 DeepSeek 模型。對一個已禁止眾多中國應用程式的政府而言，這是少見的放行中國 AI 模型。同年，AI Singapore 發布最新版 SEA-LION，這款針對東南亞語言的開源語言模型以阿里巴巴的 Qwen 為基礎，而非 Meta 的 Llama。泰國的 OpenThaiGPT 則以 Qwen2.5 微調而成。

這些採用模式反映了理性的經濟選擇。中國實驗室的產出異常豐富，發布了能在普通硬體上運行的高效能模型。對於需要管理運算成本的印度或新加坡新創公司，或是希望將公民資料留在境內的政府而言，相較於美國的替代方案，中國模型能帶來實質的財務與營運優勢。在開發中亞洲市場，企業對專有雲端服務的資本支出仍受限制，因此開放權重模型在成本效益上更具優勢。

雲端基礎設施與鎖定機制

開放權重模型是 AI 技術堆疊中最具可替換性的一層。模型一經下載便無法撤回，也很容易在不同供應商之間替換。真正的轉換成本與鎖定效應存在於其他環節，主要是支撐模型部署的運算與雲端基礎設施。雖然理論上模型可能帶動對中國雲端與運算服務的需求，但這種機制是透過市場偏好，而非強迫來運作。中國模型可以託管在 Amazon Web Services 或當地資料中心，而非阿里雲；但自行託管需要投資聘用工程師和購置圖形處理器，多數企業無法獨力負擔。

阿里巴巴正在建設區域基礎設施，以承接這類需求。2025 年，阿里巴巴在馬來西亞啟用第三座資料中心，並宣布計畫在菲律賓興建第二座。該公司也在新加坡設立 AI 中心，向企業和開發者提供代幣點數與運算資源。然而，目前證據有限，尚無法確認這些基礎設施投資是否轉化為亞洲各地的雲端合約，因為許多採用者刻意選擇自行託管，以避免依賴供應商。

中國 AI 模型也正在帶動對國產硬體的需求。DeepSeek 的 V4 於 2026 年 4 月發布，並針對華為 Ascend 晶片進行調整；華為表示，其晶片用於該模型部分訓練工作。這種硬體整合構成另一層潛在的鎖定效應，不過目前雙方關係仍處於初期階段。

路徑依賴與模型生態系中嵌入的價值觀

對中國模型的依賴並非不可避免，但早期採用選擇會帶來長期影響。開發者往往會持續偏好既有選擇——他們會繼續使用熟悉的模型，而模型融入公司產品與工作流程的程度越深，轉換成本就越高。一旦某款模型成為區域標準，支援它的生態系，包括工具、變體，以及用來評估新模型的基準，就會圍繞該模型建立。這種生態系黏著性會形成非正式影響力，不需要明確脅迫也能發揮作用。

模型也會嵌入訓練資料中的政治與語言假設。2025 年 1 月，當 DeepSeek 聊天機器人被問及阿魯納恰爾邦是否屬於印度時，拒絕作答。Perplexity 決定重新訓練 DeepSeek 的 R1 模型，以移除中國政府審查，這顯示這類回應可能內建於模型架構本身，而不只是應用層的問題。價值觀嵌入模型，意味著廣泛採用中國模型可能逐漸讓其底層政治與監管框架在亞洲開發者社群中成為常態。

前沿模型限制與商業協議

開放權重模型生態系最初以免費分發和不受限制的存取為基礎，但這套邏輯在前沿模型領域正逐漸弱化。Moonshot 的 Kimi K3 和阿里巴巴的 Qwen 3.8-Max 現在要求提供服務的大型企業簽訂商業協議，將過去免費的資源轉變為合約關係。從開放權重分發轉向商業授權，帶來了新的影響力切入點，北京可能藉此施加限制，但這些機制仍處於初期階段，也存在爭議。

OpenAI 的 gpt-oss 和 Google 的 Gemma 等美國開放權重模型也在爭取相同的使用者。許多採用者刻意同時部署美國與中國模型，以避免供應商鎖定並保持策略彈性。更直接的競爭成本可能來自華盛頓：美國已禁止 DeepSeek 用於聯邦系統，並正在評估擴大限制；對於擁有美國客戶，或營運受美國出口管制約束的亞洲企業而言，這是重大風險。

印度的對沖策略：國內運算與替代方案

印度展現了以科技對沖中國模型主導地位的潛力與局限。即使印度企業採用中國模型，新德里仍在投資國內替代方案與運算能力。總額 12 億美元的 IndiaAI Mission 正部署約 38,000 個獲補助的圖形處理器；Sarvam AI 則推出自行從頭訓練、擁有 300 億與 1,050 億參數的模型。國內運算能力讓印度開發者能在境內微調並託管任何模型，降低轉向中國雲端基礎設施的誘因。

然而，印度的對沖策略只是轉移依賴，而非消除依賴。這些圖形處理器絕大多數從美國晶片製造商進口，意味著印度以暴露於美國硬體與出口管制之下，取代對中國模型的依賴。Sarvam 較早期的模型 Sarvam-M 是以法國的 Mistral Small 為基礎建構。Sarvam 的較新模型雖然從頭訓練，但能力仍落後於前沿系統。印度的做法降低了對中國基礎設施的鎖定，但並未實現科技獨立；而且多數其他亞洲國家無法採取這種部分對沖策略。

重點資訊

到 2025 年 8 月，Qwen 衍生版本占 Hugging Face 新語言模型衍生版本的 40% 以上，相較之下，Llama 占 15%

截至 2025 年，中國模型占 OpenRouter 開放模型使用量的 80% 以上

2025 年 1 月，印度電子與資訊科技部批准在印度伺服器上託管 DeepSeek 模型

2025 年，AI Singapore 將其 SEA-LION 語言模型改以阿里巴巴的 Qwen 為基礎，而非 Meta 的 Llama

泰國的 OpenThaiGPT 以 Qwen2.5 微調而成

阿里巴巴在新加坡設立 AI 中心，提供代幣點數與運算資源

常見問題

是什麼因素推動中國 AI 模型在亞洲獲得採用？

Qwen 和 DeepSeek 等中國開放權重 AI 模型，在價格敏感的亞洲市場具備顯著的經濟優勢。中國實驗室發布了能在普通硬體上運行的高效能模型，對需要管理運算成本的印度與東南亞新創公司，以及希望透過在境內託管模型來確保資料主權的政府而言，極具吸引力。到 2025 年 8 月，Qwen 變體占 Hugging Face 新語言模型衍生版本的 40% 以上，相較之下，Llama 占 15%；而中國模型占 OpenRouter 開放模型使用量的 80% 以上。

如果開放權重模型可以自由下載並替換，真正的鎖定效應會出現在哪裡？

開放權重模型是 AI 技術堆疊中最具可替換性的一層，下載後便無法撤回。真正的鎖定效應存在於支援模型部署的運算與雲端基礎設施，因為多數企業無法在沒有大量資本投入、聘用工程師及購置圖形處理器的情況下自行託管。阿里巴巴正在馬來西亞、菲律賓和新加坡建設區域資料中心與 AI 基礎設施，以承接這類需求。此外，路徑依賴也會形成鎖定效應：開發者會逐漸依賴特定模型生態系，而其中的工具、變體和評估基準也會以該模型為中心成為標準，使轉換成本隨時間不斷增加。

印度的國內 AI 策略如何處理對中國模型的依賴？

印度透過總額 12 億美元的 IndiaAI Mission 採取對沖策略；該計畫正部署約 38,000 個獲補助的圖形處理器，並促進 Sarvam AI 等業者開發國內模型。這讓印度開發者能在境內微調並託管任何模型，減少採用中國雲端基礎設施的壓力。然而，這項策略只是轉移依賴，而非消除依賴，因為圖形處理器絕大多數從美國晶片製造商進口，等於以暴露於美國硬體與出口管制之下，取代對中國模型的依賴。Sarvam 的較新模型雖然從頭訓練，能力仍落後於前沿系統。
