Qwen.content:
# 2026年阿里云Qwen4-Max深度解析：定位、架构、能力与适用场景

2026-11-18 2

举报

简介： Qwen4-Max 是 2026年 Qwen4 系列的旗舰基座，2.4T 总参数、71B 激活、原生视觉、百万 Token 上下文，配合 GDN 与 QSA 混合注意力把长上下文的读取成本压了下来。它的价值不在单点分数，而在"能把长任务跑完并交付成品"这件事上，同时把单任务成本拉低了近六成。适用边界也很清楚：需要私有化部署或模型微调的项目，当前并不适用。选型时先看任务形态，再看成本结构，比只看榜单分数更有意义。

2026年11月，阿里云正式发布通义千问新一代旗舰基座模型 Qwen4-Max，并同步上线百炼平台。与前代旗舰相比，这一代的重点不再是单项能力刷榜，而是把优化方向压在专业工作场景的长链路任务上：更长的上下文、更少的 Token 消耗、更低的单任务成本，以及能持续交付可用成果的执行方式。本文从模型定位、架构特征、能力清单、评测表现、适用场景、接入方式六个层面做完整解析。文中数据取自官方模型卡与公开评测材料，具体规格以百炼模型页实时信息为准。

## 一、模型定位：从问答工具转向可交付工作的基座

Qwen4-Max 的官方定位是新一代旗舰多模态智能体基座模型。它的设计假设很明确：企业里真正有价值的工作，很少能塞进一次对话。这些任务往往持续数小时、跨越几十个工具、涉及上千页资料，最终必须产出一份团队能直接使用的东西——一份可运行的代码、一份可评审的方案、一张可交付的设计稿。详情👉访问阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 了解。

因此它的能力取向围绕三件事展开：第一，能稳定调用专业工具链，而不只是生成文本；第二，能把长任务推进到终点，中途不丢上下文、不跑偏；第三，交付的是成品而非中间回答。官方把这套机制命名为 Live Delivery（渐进交付）：在长任务开始时先给出一版可用的初版，之后持续迭代提交改进版本，让团队在任务运行过程中就能评审和纠偏，而不是等到最后才发现方向错了。

这一定位决定了它与轻量对话模型的分工。日常问答、简单文案，用更小的模型成本更低；而跨文档分析、多文件工程改造、长流程智能体，才是 Qwen4-Max 的合理使用区间。

## 二、架构特征：2.4T 参数与百万上下文如何兼顾效率

Qwen4-Max 总参数规模为 2.4 万亿（2.4T），单 Token 仅激活 710 亿（71B），另外配置 3280 亿（328B）的 N-gram Embedding 参数。总参数大、激活参数小，是典型的稀疏混合专家路线，目的是在保住能力上限的同时压住单次推理的算力开销。官方数据显示，每个 Token 的激活参数比上一代减少约 25%。详情👉访问阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 了解。

支撑百万级上下文的，是三项架构改动：

GDN + QSA 混合注意力。 每四层中，三层使用 Gated DeltaNet（GDN），把历史信息压缩成固定大小的状态，使 KV 缓存不随上下文长度线性增长；剩下一层使用 Qwen Sparse Attention（QSA），通过轻量索引定位关键段落。官方给出的效果是百万 Token 读取速度提升 7 倍以上。这一点对长文档、长代码库场景意义很大——上下文再长，显存与延迟也不会失控。

GR 门控残差。 把单通道残差流展宽为 4 条并行分支，配合动态读写门控，增强跨层信息传递。工程上的直接收益是 2.4T 规模训练全程平稳，没有出现损失突增（Loss Spike）。这类改动不出现在能力指标里，但决定了大模型能否稳定训到目标规模。

N-gram Embedding。 单独配置 328B 的 N-gram 嵌入参数，用于强化高频片段的表征，对代码、术语密集的专业文本有直接帮助。

规格层面，Qwen4-Max 上下文长度为 100 万 Token，最大输入 991,808 Token，最大输出 131,072 Token；开启思考模式时，最大输入 983,616 Token、最大输出 262,144 Token，最大思维链长度同为 262,144 Token。输入模态覆盖文本、图像、视频，输出为文本。原生视觉并非后期拼接的适配层，工程图纸、医疗影像、长视频都可以直接作为输入。

## 三、能力清单：哪些能做，哪些不做

官方模型卡列出的支持项包括：流式输出、深度思考、并行工具调用、联网搜索、前缀补全、Function Calling、思维链摘要与加密、结构化输出（JSON Object 与 JSON Schema）、显式缓存与隐式缓存、批量推理。接口层面兼容 OpenAI Chat Completions、Responses、Anthropic Messages 与 DashScope，迁移成本较低，已有 OpenAI 或 Anthropic 风格调用的项目大多只需换 Base URL 与模型 ID。

深度思考默认开启，可通过 reasoning_effort 调节推理力度。这里有一个必须注意的工程细节：从预览版开始，max_tokens 与 max_completion_tokens 语义等价，二者共同限制"思考内容 + 最终回答"的总量。如果沿用过去只为回答预留上限的写法，开启思考后输出会被提前截断。迁移时应当为思考与回答共同预留额度。

明确不支持的项同样重要：模型调优不支持，模型部署不支持。也就是说，Qwen4-Max 只能以 API 方式调用，不能私有化微调后自行部署。对数据必须留在自有环境的项目，这条限制需要在选型阶段就确认清楚。

## 四、评测表现：能力提升与成本下降同时发生

官方公布的 Work360 评测中，Qwen4-Max 得分 52.69，上一代为 47.74。在相同推理力度下，单任务 Token 消耗明显下降：Work360 在 Xhigh 与 High 两档分别减少约 24% 与 35%，Terminal-Bench 4.0 分别减少约 48% 与 49%。综合结果是平均单任务成本比上一代下降 58%。详情👉访问阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 了解。

中文通用能力侧，2026年11月的 SuperCLUE 测评中 Qwen4-Max 取得 61.61 分，进入国内第一梯队，较上一版本提升 18.39 分。分项上，幻觉控制 73.61 分、提升 40.56 分；超长上下文 77.80 分、提升 33.42 分；智能体编程 57.69 分、提升 15.38 分。更值得关注的是稳定性：上一代在同一测试中超时率为 69.23%，新模型超时率降至 0%，全部试题跑完。按测试的 Token 开销与定价折算，平均每题成本约 1.90 元，较上一代下降约 87%。

这组数据的含义是：能力提升之外，单位任务的调用成本出现了数量级变化。对高频跑智能体流程的团队来说，成本项的变化往往比分数更能决定项目是否跑得起来。

## 五、适用场景：六类任务最匹配

编程开发与工程改造。 支持多文件读取、工具调用与结构化输出，配合百万上下文可直接把整个代码库放进一次会话。Terminal-Bench 上 Token 消耗下降近半，意味着批量重构、批量测试生成这类任务的账单压力明显减轻。

前端与设计还原。 原生视觉可直接读取设计稿、截图、原型图，输出可运行的页面代码，适合设计到开发的衔接环节。

办公与文档处理。 长报告、合同、财报、会议材料，单份即可覆盖在上下文内，不需要切块摘要再拼接，减少信息在切分过程中丢失的问题。结构化输出可以直接产出 JSON，方便对接下游系统。

复杂智能体与流程自动化。 并行工具调用、联网搜索、Function Calling 齐备，适合需要串联检索、计算、写文件、调用内部接口的长链路流程。Live Delivery 机制让长任务可以边跑边交付，便于中途校正。

专业视觉理解。 工程图纸、医疗影像、长视频分析，属于原生视觉的典型用例，无需额外接视觉模型。

长文档审阅与合规核查。 幻觉控制分项的大幅提升，加上长上下文能力，适合条款比对、事实核验这类对准确性敏感的工作。

反过来，不适合的场景也要说清：单轮简单问答、短文案润色、固定模板填表，用旗舰模型的成本没有必要；需要私有化部署或模型微调的项目，Qwen4-Max 目前不提供这两条路径。

## 六、接入与计费：Token Plan 是唯一入口

Qwen4-Max 通过百炼接入，预览版 qwen4-max-preview 仅支持 Token Plan，不开放按量计费。预览期为 2026年11月11日 10:00 至 11月25日 24:00（UTC+8），期间模型能力持续迭代，预览结束后下线，正式版 qwen4-max 已上线，建议直接使用正式版。

调用方式上，先开通 Token Plan 个人版或团队版，获取套餐专用 API Key（前缀 sk-sp），使用套餐专用 Base URL：

export BASE_URL="[https://token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com](https://token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com)"

## 七、选型建议

判断是否需要 Qwen4-Max，可以先回答三个问题：任务是否需要跨几十页文档或整个代码库？是否需要在一次会话里连续调用多个工具直到产出成品？是否对事实准确性高度敏感？三项中命中两项以上，旗舰档才值得；否则更小的模型配外部工具组合，性价比通常更好。

对已经在用上一代旗舰的团队，迁移的收益主要落在两处：单任务 Token 消耗下降带来的账单缩减，以及超时率归零带来的流程稳定性。迁移风险集中在输出预算参数——务必按"思考 + 回答"合计的口径重新设定上限，否则会出现长任务被截断、看起来像模型能力不足的误判。

## 八、总结

Qwen4-Max 是 2026年 Qwen4 系列的旗舰基座，2.4T 总参数、71B 激活、原生视觉、百万 Token 上下文，配合 GDN 与 QSA 混合注意力把长上下文的读取成本压了下来。它的价值不在单点分数，而在"能把长任务跑完并交付成品"这件事上，同时把单任务成本拉低了近六成。适用边界也很清楚：需要私有化部署或模型微调的项目，当前并不适用。选型时先看任务形态，再看成本结构，比只看榜单分数更有意义。

import OpenAI from "openai";
import process from 'process';

    apiKey: process.env.DASHSCOPE_API_KEY, // 从环境变量读取
    baseURL: 'https://cn-beijing.maas.qianwenaiapi.com/compatible-mode/v1'

let isAnswering = false;
async function main() {
    try {
        const messages = [{ role: 'user', content: '你是谁' }];

            model: 'qwen4-max',
            messages,
            stream: true,
            enable_thinking: true
        });
        console.log('\n' + '='.repeat(20) + '思考过程' + '='.repeat(20));
        for await (const chunk of stream) {
            if (!chunk.choices || chunk.choices.length === 0) continue;
            const delta = chunk.choices[0].delta;
            if (delta.reasoning_content !== undefined && delta.reasoning_content !== null) {
                if (!isAnswering) {
                    process.stdout.write(delta.reasoning_content);
                }

            if (delta.content !== undefined && delta.content) {
                if (!isAnswering) {
                    console.log('\n' + '='.repeat(20) + '完整回复' + '='.repeat(20));
                    isAnswering = true;
                }
                process.stdout.write(delta.content);
            }
        }
    } catch (error) {
        console.error('Error:', error);
    }
}
main();

# Alibaba Cloud (Qwen)

Alibaba Cloud's DashScope API provides OpenAI-compatible access to Qwen language models. Use OpenAI provider options supported by your chosen model.

## Setup

To use Alibaba Cloud's API, set theDASHSCOPE_API_KEY environment variable or specify via apiKey in the configuration file:
export DASHSCOPE_API_KEY=your_api_key_here

## Configuration

The provider uses OpenAI provider options; support varies by model. Example:
providers:
  - alibaba:qwen3.8-max # Simple usage
  - id: alibaba:qwen3.7-plus # Aliases: alicloud:, aliyun:, dashscope:
    config:
      temperature: 0.7
      apiKey: your_api_key_here # Alternative to DASHSCOPE_API_KEY environment variable
      apiBaseUrl: https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1 # Optional: Override default API base URL

note

The equivalent provider prefixes arealicloud:, aliyun:, and dashscope:. For new configurations, Alibaba recommends qwen3.7-plus for balanced use, qwen3.8-flash for lower cost, or qwen3.8-max for stronger reasoning. Check the model catalog for your region; model availability differs by region.

If you're using the Alibaba Cloud Beijing region console, switch the base URL tohttps://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1 instead of the international endpoint.

## Supported Models

The built-in Alibaba provider implements OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions and text embeddings. The catalog below also lists separate realtime, speech recognition, and image generation services. Listing a model here does not add those endpoints to this provider. Choose a model supported by your selected endpoint and region.

### Qwen 3 Flagship

- qwen3.8-max / qwen3.8-max-0902 - Current flagship with text, image, and video input and a 1M-token context window
- qwen3.8-flash - Faster Qwen3.8 model with a 1M-token context window
- qwen3.7-plus / qwen3.7-plus-2026-05-26 - General-purpose model with thinking, vision, and tool calling
- qwen3.7-flash / qwen3.7-flash-2026-07-15 - Lower-cost Qwen3.7 model
- qwen3.7-max / qwen3.7-max-2026-06-08 - Previous flagship
- qwen3.6-plus / qwen3.6-flash and qwen3.5-plus / qwen3.5-flash - Previous model families
- qwen3-max - Supports reasoning and tool calling
- qwen3-max-preview - Preview version with thinking mode support
- qwen3-max-2025-09-23 - September 2025 snapshot
- qwen-max - 32K context (30,720 in, 8,192 out)
- qwen-max-latest - Always updated to latest version
- qwen-max-2025-01-25 - January 2025 snapshot
- qwen-plus / qwen-plus-latest - 128K-1M context (thinking & non-thinking modes)
- qwen-plus-2025-09-11, qwen-plus-2025-07-28, qwen-plus-2025-07-14, qwen-plus-2025-04-28, qwen-plus-2025-01-25 - Dated snapshots
- qwen-flash / qwen-flash-2025-07-28 - Latency-optimized general model

# 小摩：维持智谱(02513)“增持”评级 目标价1200港元

来源：智通财经

2026-11-18 15:15:53

（原标题：小摩：维持智谱(02513)“增持”评级 目标价1200港元）

智通财经APP获悉，摩根大通发布研报指出，智谱(02513)在生成式人工智能领域持续稳步推进，尽管市场对该股的情绪有所转弱，但公司基本面稳健，商业化进展符合预期，加上中国的AI应用仍处于早期阶段。综合考量，该行认为市场当前对公司表现过于悲观，维持智谱“增持”评级，目标价1200港元。

报告提到，Z.AI目前主力模型GLM系列的商业化进展顺利，与国内外主要云服务提供商的合作持续推进，收入分成表现理想，且利润率正逐季改善。管理层重申2026年底年化经常性收入目标为30亿美元。此外，Z.AI目前已利用超过10万张国产芯片的集群进行大规模低成本推理，管理层更指出GLM-5.3-Flash在国产芯片上的推理已实现毛利率转正，显示其在本地化硬件整合方面具备领先优势。

针对美国商务部工业与安全局(BIS)早前发布一项临时最终规则，旨在禁止中国及其他国家企业透过第三国数据中心远程获取先进美国芯片，鉴于其算力集中于境内，海外业务则由合作伙伴持有运算资产，管理层认为新规对公司影响有限。

财务状况方面，管理层表示公司资金充裕，并明确排除计划A股上市前进行任何股权或可转债融资的可能。公司今年已两度完成大型融资，分别于7月透过配售筹得314亿港元，9月再筹集约50亿美元，其中包括20亿美元配售及30亿美元零息可转债，为未来研发与扩张提供充足弹药。

摩根大通指出，目前智谱超过80%的收入来自中国市场，因此国内本土AI应用的普及速度是集团增长的关键驱动力。风险因素方面则包括出口管制与地缘政治风险、竞争加剧、持续高额研发投入所带来的执行与盈利压力、客户采用不确定性，以及对运算基础设施与外部供应商的依赖。

# MAI Code 2 vs GLM-5.5: One of These Models Has a Rate Card

Author
jinhao.song
Date Published

Latest models · 20View all models →

Benchmarks: Artificial Analysis · updated daily

Back to all posts

MAI Code 2 shipped on 17 November 2026 with a 24-page model card, a published promotional rate of $0.50 per million input tokens and $2.50 per million output, and a deployment in GitHub Copilot. GLM-5.5 has none of those things. Z.ai's own API platform tops out at GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash; the lab's Hugging Face organisation has no checkpoint carrying the 5.5 number; there is no rate card row, no API identifier and no model card. So the matchup the title promises cannot be run, and pretending otherwise would mean inventing a specification. What can be run is MAI Code 2 against GLM-5.3, the model Z.ai actually sells — plus a precise account of what would have to appear before "GLM-5.5" became something you could call, and why a reader arriving on this page should care about the difference between a roadmap and a product.

## What exists on each side, checked this week

• MAI Code 2 — released 17 November 2026, model card published, weights not distributed, API access inside GitHub Copilot only

• GLM-5.5 — no release, no model card, no identifier, no price, no weights, no vendor page using the name

• GLM-5.3 — released August 2026, open weights on Hugging Face under Z.ai's own organisation, API live on Z.ai's platform

• GLM-5.3-Flash — released 26 August 2026, the high-volume sibling, also open weights

The absence is not a technicality. A model exists when a lab will take your money or hand you the weights. Z.ai does both for GLM-5.3 and neither for anything numbered 5.5. Every claim circulating about GLM-5.5 sits on a release-window forecast rather than a vendor statement, and windows have slipped before in this line — the August window that produced GLM-5.3 was widely expected to produce a model called GLM-5.4.

## The comparison you can actually run: MAI Code 2 vs GLM-5.3

These two are closer in spirit than in price. Both are aimed at repository-scale software work. Both are closed in MAI Code 2's case and open in GLM-5.3's, which is the sharpest structural difference between them.

• Input price — MAI Code 2 at $0.50 per million tokens (promotional, until 17 May 2027) vs GLM-5.3 at $1.26 according to OrcaRouter's structured rate row, $1.40 according to the vendor's own descriptive text

• Output price — $2.50 vs $3.96 by the structured row, $4.40 by the descriptive text

• After the promotional window — MAI Code 2 moves to $1.00 and $5.00 on 17 May 2027; GLM-5.3 has no announced change

• Context — GLM-5.3 takes a 1,000,000-token window; MAI Code 2 takes 1,050,000, so the extra 50,000 is the only place the Microsoft model is ahead on this line

• Maximum output — 128,000 tokens on both

• What it will accept — GLM-5.3 is text in, text out; MAI Code 2 also takes images in, which matters only if your tickets carry screenshots

• Weights — MAI Code 2 distributes none; GLM-5.3 is downloadable, so you can run it yourself

• Independent score — MAI Code 2 has none; GLM-5.3 posts 32 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0.1 at $5.01 per index task

The price discrepancy on the GLM side is worth flagging rather than smoothing over: the catalogue's structured figure and the vendor page's prose disagree, and which one you pay depends on how the rate card is applied. That is a reason to check the number at the moment you commit, not a reason to pick one and call it settled.

## What GLM-5.3's independent score tells you that MAI Code 2's vendor numbers do not

GLM-5.3's 32 is not impressive on its own. It sits below Claude Opus 5.5 at 59, Gemini 4 Carbon at 60 and GPT-6.1 Sol at 55, and it is 22 minutes and $5.01 per index task to get there. But it is a number produced by someone with no stake in Z.ai's marketing, on the same nine-evaluation basis as everyone else's, and that makes it comparable to the rest of the board in a way Microsoft's 96%-of-Opus claim is not.

Microsoft's figures — 73.2% on DeepSWE 1.1, 84.6% on TerminalBench 2.1, 43.1% on SWE Atlas, all at max reasoning effort — came out of MSBench, Microsoft's internal harness, through the GitHub Copilot CLI. The model card is unusually forthcoming about method and unusually silent about independent confirmation. When one side of a comparison has a third-party score and the other has a first-party pass rate, the honest reading is that you know where GLM-5.3 sits and you know what Microsoft says about MAI Code 2.

## The open-weights question decides more than the score does

This is the difference that actually changes architecture rather than procurement. GLM-5.3 is downloadable. You can put it on your own hardware, fine-tune it on your own repository history, keep the traffic inside your network, and stop paying per token at the point where your volume exceeds the cost of a GPU. Z.ai also ships a customisation path — Microsoft's equivalent is MAI Licensed Weights, announced the same day as MAI Code 2, which lets an organisation run a customised MAI model inside its own Azure environment. The two are not the same offer. One is a file you can download and run wherever you like; the other is a commercial arrangement that keeps the model inside a Microsoft cloud and keeps the weights in Microsoft's hands.

For a team whose constraint is data residency, GLM-5.3 answers the question outright. For a team whose constraint is that it already runs on Azure and wants a supported model with a vendor behind it, MAI Licensed Weights is the closer fit — and it is a separate purchase from the Copilot subscription that gets you MAI Code 2 by the token.

## Where MAI Code 2 is and is not available

On the Copilot side the surface is wide but the door is narrow: five subscription tiers, from Pro up to Enterprise, and every editor GitHub ships an extension for. What is missing is the thing an application needs — a model ID and a URL. MAI Code 2 Flash has a limited-access Foundry preview on an OpenAI-compatible Responses API; the large model has no Foundry deployment, no published endpoint and no date for one, and Microsoft says only that broader availability is coming.

GLM-5.3, by contrast, is on Z.ai's own API and available as weights, which means a dozen hosting arrangements exist that neither vendor controls. That is the practical difference between a model with an ecosystem and a model with a launch.

## If GLM-5.5 does appear, what would change

Three things would have to be true before it became a real comparison. A model card or a vendor announcement, because a name in a leak thread is not a release. A rate card, because the only decision a buyer makes is per-token cost against per-task cost. And weights or an endpoint, because a model you cannot call is a press release. The likely shape, if Z.ai follows its own pattern, is a GLM-5.3-class text model with a higher index score and open weights — which would make it a genuine alternative to MAI Code 2 for anyone who needs to run the model rather than rent it, and no alternative at all for anyone working inside Copilot.

## Running both sides on one key

GLM-5.3 is on OrcaRouter's catalogue at the pass-through rate, with 0% markup, alongside Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 4 Carbon and GPT-6.1 Sol — so the open-weights side of this comparison can be measured against the closed frontier on a single key without a second contract. That is the useful capability in a matchup where one model is a promise: you can price the alternatives you actually have, today, and see what the model that does not exist would have to beat. MAI Code 2 is not on our catalogue; the published route is GitHub Copilot.

For a reader who came here to choose: if you want a model that exists, has open weights and a published price, GLM-5.3 is the answer on the Z.ai side. If you want the cheapest per-token coding model with a Microsoft support path and you work in Copilot, MAI Code 2 is the one shipping today. GLM-5.5 is neither, and the honest thing to do with a name that has no model behind it is to wait for the model card rather than plan around the name.

# MAI Code 2 对比 GLM-5.5：这两款模型中的一款提供了费率卡

作者
jinhao.song
发布日期

最新模型 · 20查看全部模型 →

基准测试：Artificial Analysis · 每日更新

返回全部文章

MAI Code 2于 2026 年 11 月 17 日发布，附带一份 24 页的模型卡、公布的促销价：每百万输入 token 0.50 美元、每百万输出 token 2.50 美元，并部署在 GitHub Copilot 中。 GLM-5.5则这些都没有。Z.ai 自己的 API 平台最高只到 GLM-5.3 和 GLM-5.3-Flash；该实验室的 Hugging Face 组织中没有带 5.5 编号的 checkpoint；没有价目表条目、没有 API 标识符，也没有模型卡。因此，标题所承诺的对决无法进行，若假装可以，就意味着凭空编造一份规格说明。能够进行的是 MAI Code 2 对 GLM-5.3，即 Z.ai 实际销售的模型——此外还要准确说明，在“GLM-5.5”成为你能调用的东西之前，必须出现哪些内容，以及为什么来到本页的读者应当关心路线图与产品之间的区别。

## 本周已核查的每侧存在什么？

• MAI Code 2 — 发布于 2026 年 11 月 17 日，模型卡已发布，权重未分发，API 访问仅限 GitHub Copilot 内部

• GLM-5.5 —— 没有发布，没有模型卡，没有标识符，没有价格，没有权重，也没有使用该名称的厂商页面

• GLM-5.3 — 于2026年8月发布，开放权重托管在 Hugging Face 上 Z.ai 自有组织下，API 已在 Z.ai 平台上线

• GLM-5.3-Flash — 于2026年8月26日发布，是面向高吞吐量的同级版本，同样开放权重

这种缺席并非技术细节。只有当实验室愿意收你的钱，或把权重交到你手上时，一个模型才算存在。Z.ai 对 GLM-5.3 两者都做到了，而对任何编号为 5.5 的模型则两者都没有。关于 GLM-5.5 的所有流传说法，依据的都是发布窗口预测，而非厂商声明；而且这条产品线此前就出现过窗口推迟——那个最终产出 GLM-5.3 的八月窗口，曾被普遍预期会产出一款名为 GLM-5.4 的模型。

## 你真正能实际运行的对比：MAI Code 2 vs GLM-5.3

两者在精神层面上的接近程度，胜过价格上的接近程度。二者都面向仓库级规模的软件工作。不同之处在于，MAI Code 2 是闭源的，而 GLM-5.3 是开源的——这正是它们之间最鲜明的结构性差异。

• 输入价格 — MAI Code 2 为每百万 token 0.50 美元（促销价，截至 2027 年 5 月 17 日），相比之下，GLM-5.3 根据 OrcaRouter 的结构化费率行是 1.26 美元，而根据供应商自己的描述性文本则是 1.40 美元

• 输出价格——结构化行中为 $2.50，对比 $3.96；描述性文本中为 $4.40

• 促销期结束后——MAI Code 2 将于 2027 年 5 月 17 日调整为 $1.00 和 $5.00；GLM-5.3 未宣布变动

• 上下文——GLM-5.3 支持 1,000,000 token 的窗口；MAI Code 2 支持 1,050,000，因此多出的 50,000 是微软模型在这一项上唯一领先的地方

• 最大输出 — 两者均为 128,000 个 token

• 它能接受什么——GLM-5.3 是文本输入、文本输出；MAI Code 2 还支持图像输入，而这一点只有在你的工单附带截图时才有意义

• 权重 — MAI Code 2 不分发任何权重；GLM-5.3 可下载，因此你可以自行运行

• 独立评分——MAI Code 2 无此项评分；GLM-5.3 在 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0.1 上得分为 32，每项指数任务成本为 5.01 美元

GLM 一侧的价格差异值得明确标出，而不是被抹平：目录中的结构化数字与供应商页面上的文字描述并不一致，而最终按哪一个付费，取决于费率卡如何适用。这恰恰说明应在承诺付款的那一刻核对数字，而不是随便选一个并当作已经定论。

## GLM-5.3 的独立评分能告诉你、而 MAI Code 2 的厂商数据无法告诉你的东西

GLM-5.3 的 32 分单看并不亮眼。它低于 Claude Opus 5.5 的 59 分、Gemini 4 Carbon 的 60 分和 GPT-6.1 Sol 的 55 分，而且每个索引任务要花 22 分钟和 5.01 美元才能达到这一成绩。但这是一个与 Z.ai 营销毫无利益关系的人，在与其他所有人相同的九项评估基础上得出的数字，这使它能够与榜单上的其他成绩相比较，而微软“达到 Opus 的 96%”的说法则做不到这一点。

微软的数据——在 DeepSWE 1.1 上 73.2%，在 TerminalBench 2.1 上 84.6%，在 SWE Atlas 上 43.1%，且均在最高推理强度下取得——出自 MSBench，这是微软的内部测试框架，并通过 GitHub Copilot CLI 得出。模型卡对方法异常坦率，却对独立验证异常沉默。当比较的一方拥有第三方分数，而另一方拥有第一方通过率时，诚实的解读是：你知道 GLM-5.3 处于什么位置，也知道微软对 MAI Code 2 说了什么。

## 开放权重这个问题比分数更能决定结果。

这是真正改变架构、而非采购决策的差别。GLM-5.3 可下载。你可以把它部署到自己的硬件上，用自己仓库的历史记录对它进行微调，让流量留在自己的网络内，并在你的用量超过一块 GPU 的成本时，不再按 token 付费。Z.ai 还提供了一条定制化路径——微软的对应方案是 MAI Licensed Weights，它与 MAI Code 2 同日发布，允许组织在自己的 Azure 环境中运行定制化的 MAI 模型。两者并不是同一种提供方式。一个是你可以下载并随心运行的文件；另一个是商业安排，把模型留在微软云内，并把权重留在微软手中。

对于约束为数据驻留的团队，GLM-5.3 直接给出了答案。对于约束是已运行在 Azure 上、并且想要一个有厂商支持的受支持模型的团队，MAI Licensed Weights 更贴合——而且它与让你按 token 使用 MAI Code 2 的 Copilot 订阅是分开购买的。

## MAI Code 2 在哪些地区可用、哪些地区不可用

在 Copilot 这边，覆盖面很广，但入口很窄：五档订阅层级，从 Pro 一直到 Enterprise，而且 GitHub 为每一款编辑器都提供了扩展。缺的正是应用程序所需的东西——一个模型 ID 和一个 URL。MAI Code 2 Flash 在兼容 OpenAI 的 Responses API 上有一个限访问的 Foundry 预览版；大模型则没有 Foundry 部署、没有已发布的端点，也没有上线日期，微软只表示将会有更广泛的可用性。

相比之下，GLM-5.3 位于 Z.ai 自有 API 上，并以权重形式提供，这意味着存在十几种两家厂商都无法控制的托管安排。这就是一个有生态的模型和一个仅有发布的模型之间的实际差别。

## 如果GLM-5.5真的出现，会有什么改变

要成为真正的对比，必须先有三件事成立。一张模型卡或一份厂商公告，因为泄露帖里的一个名字并不等于发布。一份价目表，因为买家唯一要做的决定，就是每 token 成本与每任务成本之间的权衡。以及权重或端点，因为一个你无法调用的模型只是一份新闻稿。如果 Z.ai 遵循自身模式，可能的形态会是一个 GLM-5.3 级文本模型，拥有更高的指数评分和开放权重——这将使其成为任何需要自行运行而非租用模型的人对 MAI Code 2 的真正替代方案，而对于任何在 Copilot 内部工作的人来说则完全不是替代方案。

## 双方使用同一密钥运行

GLM-5.3 已以直通费率上架 OrcaRouter 目录，零加价，与 Claude Opus 5.5、Gemini 4 Carbon 和 GPT-6.1 Sol 并列——因此，这一对比中的开放权重一方可以在单一密钥下与闭源前沿模型同台衡量，而无需第二份合同。在一场其中一个模型还只是承诺的较量中，这正是有用的能力：你可以为当下实际拥有的替代方案定价，并看清那个尚不存在的模型必须超越什么。MAI Code 2 不在我们的目录中；已公布的获取途径是 GitHub Copilot。

对于那些来这里做选择的读者：如果你想要一个确实存在、权重开放且价格已公布的模型，那么在 Z.ai 这边，答案就是 GLM-5.3。如果你想要的是每 token 成本最低的编程模型、有微软的支持渠道，并且你在 Copilot 中工作，那么今天已经交付的就是 MAI Code 2。GLM-5.5 两者都不是；面对一个背后并没有模型的名字，诚实的做法是等待模型卡发布，而不是围绕这个名字去做规划。

GLM.content:
Try the new OrcaCyber Zero 1.5 — connect to any cyber harness for offensive security, zero-days & AI defense 🐳Get API

Guides & Insights

# Qwen4-Max vs GLM-5.4: One Shipped, One Missed Its Own Window

Author
jinhao.song
Date Published

Latest models · 20View all models →

Benchmarks: Artificial Analysis · updated daily

Back to all posts

There is a version of this comparison that would be useful and a version that would be fiction. The useful one starts with a date: Z.ai's own release log still ends at GLM-5.3-Flash on 26 August 2026, its documentation index enumerates GLM-5.2, GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash and nothing above them, and the GLM-5.4 documentation path returns Page Not Found as it did in October. Qwen4-Max, by contrast, has been on metered sale since 16 November 2026, with a published rate card and an independent score. So the matchup is not two flagships. It is a flagship and a projected date that has now expired.

What makes that more than a debunking is the arithmetic behind the projection. This blog put a 54-to-70-day cadence on the GLM line in October and published the window it implied. That window has closed. Working out by how much, and what the closure tells you about how Z.ai is sequencing releases, is genuinely more informative than another speculative spec sheet — and it leaves a comparison that can actually be run: Qwen4-Max against GLM-5.3, the GLM that ships, on the same independent index, in the same week.

## Where the name stands on 18 November

The audit is short and it is repeatable. Four surfaces, all checked today, all negative.

• The release log — newest entry GLM-5.3-Flash, dated 2026-08-26; then GLM-5.3 on 2026-08-18, GLM-5.2 on 2026-06-16, GLM-5.1 on 2026-04-07, GLM-5 on 2026-02-12

• The documentation index — GLM-5.3-Flash/FlashX, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.2. No 5.4 entry at any effort level

• The documentation path — docs.z.ai/guides/llm/glm-5.4 returns 404, exactly as it did on 13 October

• Hugging Face — a repository search for "glm-5.4" returns nothing under the lab's own organisation, and the newest text checkpoints there are the four GLM-5.3 releases created on 25 August

The vendor's model-api page gives the same answer from the commercial side: GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash, GLM-5 and GLM-5V-Turbo, with no row between 5.3 and 6. Nine surfaces were checked for the standing page on this name in October; the same four that matter for shipping status are still negative five weeks later. That consistency is the finding. A name that has been absent from every first-party surface for eight weeks is not a launch in flight; it is a name the line has passed over, at least for now.
# Qwen4-Max vs GLM-5.3
| | QWEN4-MAX | GLM-5.3 |

| INPUT / 1M TOKENS | $1.50 | $1.40 |

| OUTPUT / 1MTOKENS | $4.50 | $4.40 |

| INDEX SCORE | 43 | 32 |

| COST / TASK | $3.27 | $5.01 |

| WALL-CLOCK / TASK | 32.1 min | 22.0 min |

| WEIGHTS | none | downloadable |

*Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0.1; prices per vendor list*

## The window, and how far past it we are

The cadence argument was never a leak. It was arithmetic on Z.ai's own release dates: GLM-5 to GLM-5.1 took 54 days, GLM-5.1 to GLM-5.2 took 70, GLM-5.2 to GLM-5.3 took 63. Apply the same span to 18 August and the next text flagship was due somewhere between 11 October and 27 October 2026. If you date the family from the Flash tier's 26 August entry instead, the outer edge moves to 4 November.

It is 18 November. Both readings have expired, the later one by two weeks. That is the cleanest statement available about GLM-5.4 today, and it is stronger than "we could not find it", because it is falsifiable: a single dated entry on the vendor's release log would overturn it, and until one appears the projection has been tested and has failed.

There are two honest readings of that failure, and they point in opposite directions. The first is that Z.ai has slowed down — that a 753-billion-parameter flagship is now expensive enough to iterate on a longer cycle, and the cadence of 2026's first half was a sprint that has ended. The second is that the next release is not a 5.4 at all: that the line skips a number, or that the effort has gone into the multimodal Flash tier, which is where the only post-August activity on the release log actually sits. Nothing published by the lab distinguishes between those two, and a page that guessed would be doing exactly what a scoreboard with invented columns does.

## What you can actually compare: Qwen4-Max against GLM-5.3

GLM-5.3 is not a consolation prize. It is a 753-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts activating roughly 40 billion parameters per token, text-only, with a 1M-token context window and a 128K output ceiling, and it has something Qwen4-Max's launch coverage mostly lacked: a measured row on the same index, taken by the same harness, in the same index revision.

• Input price — Qwen4-Max $1.50 per million tokens in Singapore, $1.413 in its other five regions, versus GLM-5.3 $1.40 on Z.ai's list

• Output price — Qwen4-Max $4.50 versus GLM-5.3 $4.40

• Independent score — Qwen4-Max 43 on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0.1 versus GLM-5.3 at 32 at max effort and 23 at low effort

• Cost per index task — Qwen4-Max $3.27 versus GLM-5.3 $5.01. This is the row that matters, and it points the opposite way from the score

• Wall-clock per task — Qwen4-Max 32.1 minutes versus GLM-5.3 22.0 minutes at max effort, 12.2 at low

• Token appetite — Qwen4-Max 127 million output tokens per index run versus GLM-5.3 135 million at max effort, 63.3 million at low

• Throughput — Qwen4-Max 55 output tokens per second versus GLM-5.3 90

• Modality — Qwen4-Max takes text, image and video and returns text; GLM-5.3 is documented as text-only, with visual work pushed to the Flash tier

• Max output — Qwen4-Max 131,072 tokens, or 262,144 shared between thinking and answer; GLM-5.3 128,000

• Weights — Qwen4-Max publishes none and marks fine-tuning and deployment unsupported; GLM-5.3's weights are downloadable under a custom Z.ai licence

• Effort control — Qwen4-Max exposes selectable levels; GLM-5.3 always reasons, with low, high and max

The price rows are almost a tie — a dime on input, a dime on output — and that is the least interesting thing in the list. The interesting thing is that the two models arrive at nearly identical list prices with different shapes underneath. Qwen4-Max costs more per task despite a cheaper meter because it takes longer and thinks longer; GLM-5.3 costs more per task despite a cheaper meter of its own because at max effort it burns through tokens at a rate the lower-effort setting does not. Neither vendor's price card tells you that. Only the cost-per-task row does, and it is the row both launch posts leave out.

The score gap is real but narrower than 43 versus 32 suggests, for a reason worth stating plainly: those figures come from different effort settings on the same index, and this blog has watched revision changes move a model's number by double digits. Treat 43 and 32 as a directional gap taken on one instrument on one day, not as a measured 11-point capability difference. What survives that caution is the cheaper claim: Qwen4-Max answers harder tasks than GLM-5.3 at max effort, and does it for less money per task, while being the slower model per token and the more expensive one per million.
# New Released
Follow along with updates across Z.AI's models

## Models

- 2026-08-28

- Native visual capabilities enable the model to observe interfaces, rendering results, and interaction feedback—creating a closed loop across code, browsers, and GUMs.

- 2026-01-14

- Efficient hybrid architecture: Combines linear and sparse attention with 320B total parameters and 18B activated, significantly reducing compute and KV-cache requirements.

- 2025-02-22

- Beyond coding: Supports office document and financial research workflows, autonomously breaking down goals, using tools, and refining outputs. Learn more in our **documentation**.*

- 2026-08-18

- Stronger Coding Capabilities: GLM-5.3 delivers a significant improvement in coding capabilities, achieving a 50% gain over GLM-5.2 on Z.al Code Bench and reaching state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance among open-source models on public benchmarks, including Terminal Bench 3.0.

- 2026-06-16

- Emergent Cybersecurity Capabilities: GLM-5.3 matches Mythos 5 in white-box code review and vulnerability discovery. In collaboration with multiple cybersecurity teams, it has been tested on real-world targets and has identified a total of 2,436 vulnerabilities, including 1,097 medium- and high-severity vulnerabilities.Learn more in our **documentation**.*

- 2026-06-16

- Supports TM lossless context, significantly improving long-horizon task capabilities and reducing context drift and goal forgetting in complex tasks.

- 2026-06-17

- Achieves open-source SOTA performance on coding and long-horizon tasks.

## The thing a GLM 5.4 searcher actually needs

People type "GLM-5.4" for one of two reasons, and the two want opposite answers.

The first is shopping: they want to know whether to migrate off GLM-5.3, or whether to pick GLM over Qwen for a build starting this month. The answer is that there is nothing to migrate to, and the decision they can make today is between a text-only model with downloadable weights at $1.40/$4.40 and a multimodal rental at $1.50/$4.50 that scores higher and costs less per finished task. That is a real choice, and it does not require a 5.4 to make it.

The second is tracking: they want a date. The honest answer is that the cadence-based window for this name expired on 27 October, or 4 November on the most generous reading, and that the projection's failure is itself the update. The next signal to watch is not a leak but the release log: an entry above GLM-5.3-Flash would settle the question in one line, and it has not appeared in the twelve weeks since the Flash tier shipped.

## Running either of them without a second

GLM.description: Then it moved roughly 2,000 engineers onto GLM, an open-weight model from the Chinese developer Z.ai, running on 56 Nvidia chips operated in-house. The switch cut coding costs by about 90% in under a year.
GLM.content:
# AI's one-model era is over

Businesses stopped picking one AI. That’s a problem for the companies selling them, a threat that comes even as Anthropic is about to IPO

A version of this article originally appeared in Quartz’s AI & Tech newsletter. Sign up here to get the latest AI & tech news, analysis and insights straight to your inbox.

Anthropic is days away from asking the public to buy in. Investors are weighing a pitch that values the Claude maker at up to $1.4 trillion, and Thursday is the expected first day of trading.

That price assumes customers who picked Claude will keep picking Claude. But by the time the IPO roadshow started, many of them were already shopping around.

## Playing the field

AT&T $T -0.31% was one of them. In May, open models handled about a fifth of the telecom company’s AI work. By September, the share had doubled to 40%, and its AI costs had fallen by as much as 80% since earlier in the year.

The company did not drop Claude or ChatGPT. Instead, a router scored each request for difficulty, sent the easy ones to open models from Meta $META -1.20%, Google $GOOGL -1.24%, and Nvidia $NVDA -0.44%, and saved the expensive models for the hard problems.

Revolut went further. The British fintech rolled out Claude Code in early 2026, and watched some engineers burn through up to $10,000 a month before capping their budgets.

Then it moved roughly 2,000 engineers onto GLM, an open-weight model from the Chinese developer Z.ai, running on 56 Nvidia chips operated in-house. The switch cut coding costs by about 90% in under a year.

They are not the only ones being a little promiscuous. On Vercel’s AI Gateway, a service that lets developers access models from many providers through one connection, almost a third of teams changed their most-used provider in September alone.

Open-weight models handled 71.5% of traffic that month and captured almost a quarter of spending, up from about one-twentieth in June.

The growing competition put pressure on prices, even as more tokens are used. Spending through the gateway ran about 13 times higher than in December 2025, while the average price per token dropped 47%.

Consumers behaved the same way with their own money. A National Bureau of Economic Research working paper tracked card data covering 174 million consumers and found that only 20% to 45% of paying subscribers stayed with a given AI service for a year. Switching jumped whenever a rival released a new model.

The consumer data offered another warning for the model makers. As providers' capabilities expanded, consumers became less likely to pay for multiple services at once. They were switching between providers, but increasingly saw little reason to pay for more than one. People were dating around, one subscription at a time.

## A moat point

For the giants, this is an awkward moment to discover how little loyalty their customers owed them. Anthropic has committed close to $900 billion to data center capacity, much of it through long-term agreements that would be difficult to unwind. Its third-quarter operating loss was $567 million. The economics depend on keeping customers willing to pay a premium for its models.

Fortunately for Anthropic, it still led where the money was. Claude Opus 5.5 took 11% of September spending on Vercel’s gateway, more than double the share of OpenAI’s top model, which came in second. A Chinese model, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, ranked third.

The shift also created opportunities for the middlemen, as it tends to in a gold rush. Gateways and routers were becoming the point where customers chose between models, while American hosting providers collected more than two-thirds of the September spending on Chinese models.

None of it should have come as a surprise. A Google researcher had laid out the whole problem in an internal memo that escaped onto a public Discord server in 2023. They argued that neither their employer nor OpenAI had a moat, and that customers would stop paying for a model once a free one was nearly as good.

Anthropic’s prospectus ran to more than 400 pages. While it never used the word moat, its risk factors warned that customers might drift toward “smaller, cheaper, or open-source alternatives.”

Kimi.content:
# Moonshot (Kimi)

Moonshot AI provides an OpenAI-compatible API for its Kimi models — the Kimi K3 and K2 thinking models and the Moonshot v1 generation models. The Moonshot provider extends the OpenAI provider, so all of its options are supported.

## Setup

- Get an API key from the Kimi (Moonshot) platform.
- Set theMOONSHOT_API_KEY environment variable or specify apiKey in your config.

Kimi K3 requires a successful account top-up of at least $1; see the access requirements.
providers:
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k3

Bothmoonshot:<model> and moonshot:chat:<model> resolve to the chat completions endpoint. If you omit the model, the provider defaults to kimi-k3.

## Available Models

Moonshot's lineup rotates over time — call the list models API (GET https://api.moonshot.ai/v1/models) for the live set. As of writing:

- Kimi K3 — flagship thinking model, 1M context:kimi-k3 (released July 2026). Always-on reasoning, native image and video understanding, and a top-level reasoning_effort control (see below).
- Kimi K2 — thinking models, 256k context:kimi-k2.6, kimi-k2.5, kimi-k2.7-code, kimi-k2.7-code-highspeed. These reason before answering and emit a separate reasoning stream (see below).
- Moonshot v1 — legacy generation models:moonshot-v1-8k, moonshot-v1-32k, moonshot-v1-128k (context-length variants) and the vision variants moonshot-v1-8k-vision-preview / moonshot-v1-32k-vision-preview / moonshot-v1-128k-vision-preview; existing accounts may also see the auto-router moonshot-v1-auto in the list-models API. The moonshot-v1 series and kimi-k2.5 are closed to newly registered users and sunset platform-wide on August 31, 2026.

The olderkimi-k2-0711-preview, kimi-k2-0905-preview, kimi-k2-turbo-preview, kimi-k2-thinking, kimi-k2-thinking-turbo, and kimi-latest ids were discontinued in 2026 — Moonshot recommends migrating to kimi-k3.

## Configuration
providers:
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k3 # flagship thinking model — leave sampling params unset
  - id: moonshot:moonshot-v1-8k # legacy generation model — accepts arbitrary sampling
    config:
      temperature: 0.2
      max_tokens: 1024

### Configuration Options

The provider accepts every option the OpenAI provider supports. Commonly used:

- temperature, max_tokens, top_p, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty
- stream
- response_format (JSON mode), tools / tool_choice (function calling)
- showThinking — set to false to drop a thinking model's reasoning from the graded output (default true)
- cost, inputCost, outputCost, cacheReadCost — Moonshot ships no built-in price table, so set these to track cost. Every override is in USD per token. Moonshot's official pricing page publishes rates in USD per 1 million tokens, so divide each published rate by 1,000,000 before configuring it. inputCost/outputCost take precedence over the flat cost; cacheReadCost prices cached prompt tokens.

For example, these illustrative per-million rates convert to per-token overrides. Check the official pricing page for the current rates for your model before using them.
providers:
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k3
    config:
      inputCost: 0.000003 # $3.00 per 1M tokens divided by 1,000,000
      cacheReadCost: 0.0000003 # $0.30 per 1M tokens divided by 1,000,000
      outputCost: 0.000015 # $15.00 per 1M tokens divided by 1,000,000
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k2.6
    config:
      inputCost: 0.00000095 # $0.95 per 1M tokens divided by 1,000,000
      cacheReadCost: 0.00000016 # $0.16 per 1M tokens divided by 1,000,000
      outputCost: 0.000004 # $4.00 per 1M tokens divided by 1,000,000

Any other parameter supported by the OpenAI provider is forwarded as-is.

## Kimi thinking models

Thekimi-k3 and kimi-k2.x models are reasoning models and behave differently from the moonshot-v1 family:

- Fixed sampling parameters. Kimi pinstemperature (1.0 with thinking on), top_p, n, and the penalties to fixed values and returns a 400 ("invalid temperature: only 1 is allowed for this model") for any other value. The provider therefore does not send promptfoo's default temperature/max_tokens for kimi-* models — leave them unset (recommended) or set temperature: 1. The moonshot-v1 models accept arbitrary sampling values.
- Reasoning output. Kimi returns a separatereasoning_content stream that promptfoo surfaces with a Thinking: … prefix. Set showThinking: false when you assert on structured output (for example is-json) so the reasoning doesn't contaminate the parsed result.
- Token budget. Reasoning tokens count against the output budget. When you leave the token limit unset the provider lets Moonshot apply its server default (32k for K2.x, 131k for K3); if you set one, leave generous headroom for the answer. Moonshot's canonical field ismax_completion_tokens (max_tokens is a deprecated alias) — the provider sends max_completion_tokens for kimi-* models whichever of the two you configure.
- Controlling thinking. The two generations use different, mutually exclusive controls:
- kimi-k3 is always thinking and accepts a top-level reasoning_effort field, which the provider forwards from config.reasoning_effort. Supported values are low, high, and max (the default). Do not send the K2.x thinking parameter to K3 — the API rejects it.
- kimi-k2.6 and kimi-k2.5 support thinking: { type: disabled } (pass it via config.passthrough); kimi-k2.7-code is always thinking. The thinking parameter is K2.x-only.
- Settingconfig.reasoning_effort on a non-K3 model is a configuration error and the provider fails fast with a clear message instead of sending it.

providers:
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k3
    config:
      showThinking: false
      reasoning_effort: max # optional: low, high, or max (default)
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k2.6
    config:
      passthrough:
        thinking: { type: disabled } # K2.x only: turn reasoning off

See the Kimi K3 quickstart and Using Thinking Models for the full behavior matrix.

## Vision

The vision models (moonshot-v1-*-vision-preview) and the multimodal Kimi models (kimi-k3, kimi-k2.5, kimi-k2.6, kimi-k2.7-code, kimi-k2.7-code-highspeed) accept base64-encoded image input using the standard OpenAI image_url content format. Moonshot does not accept remote image URLs — embed images as data: URIs or reference files uploaded to the Kimi platform as ms://<file-id>. Video input is supported by kimi-k3, kimi-k2.6, kimi-k2.7-code, and kimi-k2.7-code-highspeed, referenced the same way after uploading via the files API. See Use the Kimi Vision Model.

## Example Usage
providers:
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k3
  - id: openai:gpt-4o-mini

prompts:
  - 'Summarize the following in one sentence: {{text}}'

tests:
  - vars:
      text: 'Promptfoo is an open-source tool for testing and evaluating LLM apps.'

A runnable comparison lives in examples/provider-moonshot.

## API Details

- Base URL:https://api.moonshot.ai/v1 (global). China-mainland keys use https://api.moonshot.cn/v1 — point at it with apiBaseUrl, since the global and China platforms issue region-locked keys.
- OpenAI-compatible chat completions API.
- Full API documentation.

## See Also

- OpenAI Provider — compatible configuration options
- Kimi model list and pricing

Kimi.description: Moonshot AI’s Kimi models, including Kimi K3, K2.6, and the coding-focused K2.7 Code. ... Kimi models are provided by Moonshot AI directly (moonshot), and some models also have providers such as Azure AI Foundry and Alibaba Cloud Model Studio...
Kimi.content:
Opens a sub-menu

# Kimi family

Moonshot AI’s Kimi models, including Kimi K3, K2.6, and the coding-focused K2.7 Code. Called through the OpenAI-compatible API; the Anthropic native API is also supported, so they can be used in Claude Code.

## Common tasks

## Models

For the full model list and live prices, see the models page . Model IDs have the prefixmoonshotai/, which can be omitted.

Common model IDs (copy them exactly)

Kimi K3
moonshotai/kimi-k31M context, supports image input
Kimi K2.6
moonshotai/kimi-k2.6256K context, supports image input
Kimi K2.7 Code
moonshotai/kimi-k2.7-codeFor coding
Kimi models are provided by Moonshot AI directly (moonshot), and some models also have providers such as Azure AI Foundry and Alibaba Cloud Model Studio; the provider is selected automatically by default. To specify one, see Provider routing.

## Examples

### Python

kimi_basic.py
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="https://api.ofox.ai/v1", api_key=os.environ["OFOX_API_KEY"])

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="moonshotai/kimi-k3",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Explain idempotency in one sentence."}],
    extra_body={"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}},
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)

## Thinking mode

Key pointKimi has thinking on by default. When you do not need it, set the thinking type to disabled (except for K2.7 Code HighSpeed).

Model | Default | Turning off thinking 
---|---|---
Kimi K3, K2.6, K2.7 Code | On | "thinking": {"type": "disabled"} 
Kimi K2.7 Code HighSpeed | On | Not supported; passing disabled returns 400 

Measured on the same math problem: Kimi K3 took about 30 seconds by default and about 3 seconds with thinking off; K2.6 used about 11,000 thinking tokens and took about 4.5 minutes by default, and about 40 seconds with thinking off. Thinking tokens are billed at the output rate, and their count is inusage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens.

Reading thinking content: in streaming responses it is indelta.reasoning_content; in non-streaming responses it is in message.reasoning_details, where you concatenate the text of each item in order.

## Web search

Addweb_search to tools on the Responses API, and the model searches on its own and attaches cited sources to its answer:

kimi_web_search.py
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="https://api.ofox.ai/v1", api_key=os.environ["OFOX_API_KEY"])

resp = client.responses.create(
    model="moonshotai/kimi-k3",
    tools=[{"type": "web_search"}],
    input="What is the latest stable version of Python?",
)
print(resp.output_text)
for item in resp.output:
    if item.type == "message":
        for part in item.content:
            for a in getattr(part, "annotations", None) or []:
                print("Source:", a.title, a.url)
- Supported by Kimi K3 and K2.6 in our tests.output contains reasoning, web_search_call, and message items in that order, and the cited sources are in the annotations of the message content.
- Searches are billed per call; for rates, see the model page .

## Use in Claude Code

Kimi models support the Anthropic native API athttps://api.ofox.ai/anthropic:

Claude Code configuration values

ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
https://api.ofox.ai/anthropic
ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKENPaste your OfoxAI API key

ANTHROPIC_MODEL
moonshotai/kimi-k2.7-code
When called through the Anthropic API, thinking content is returned asthinking blocks. For the full Claude Code setup steps, see Claude Code setup.

## Image input and structured output

- Kimi K3 and K2.6 support image input using standardimage_url content blocks; see Vision for the format.
- response_format supports json_schema and json_object; tool calling uses the standard tools parameter. See Structured output for the format.
- Repeated request prefixes are cached automatically; the hit count is inusage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens.

## Common errors

HTTP · type | Error message | Cause | Fix 
---|---|---|---
400 invalid_request_error | invalid thinking: only type=enabled is allowed for this model | K2.7 Code HighSpeed does not support turning off thinking | Remove the thinking parameter, or switch to K2.7 Code 
429 rate_limit_error | Rate limit reached for the requested model. Please retry after a short delay. | Too many requests | Retry later; see Rate limits 
404 model_not_found | Model 'moonshotai/kimi-k9' not found | Model ID misspelled, or the moonshot/ prefix was used | The prefix is moonshotai/; copy the model ID from this page 
Request timeout | — | Thinking is on by default, and complex questions take longer | Turn off thinking, use streaming, or set the client timeout to 600 seconds or more 

For other general errors, see Error handling.

## Official docs

## FAQ

How do I write Kimi model IDs?

The standard form is moonshotai/kimi-k3; you can also omit the prefix and write kimi-k3. Writing moonshot/kimi-k3 returns 404.

How do I turn off thinking for Kimi?

Pass "thinking": {"type": "disabled"}; with the OpenAI SDK, put it in extra_body. K2.7 Code HighSpeed does not support turning it off, and passing it returns 400.

Can Kimi search the web?

Yes. Use the Responses API and add {"type": "web_search"} to tools; the answer will include cited sources. Supported by Kimi K3 and K2.6 in our tests.

Can Claude Code use Kimi?

Yes. Set ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to https://api.ofox.ai/anthropic and set the model to moonshotai/kimi-k2.7-code or moonshotai/kimi-k3.

Why is Kimi K2.6 so slow?

K2.6 has thinking on by default, and complex questions may use more than ten thousand thinking tokens and take several minutes. Turn thinking off when you do not need it, or switch to Kimi K3.

Kimi.title: Uncensored Kimi K3.1 Pro: the smartest open weights model, without refusals
Kimi.description: Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro (October 23, 2026) is the highest scoring open weights model on the current Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index: 46 ... It is a 2.8 trillion parameter mixture of experts (104B active per token) with a 1M token context.
Kimi.content:
# Uncensored Kimi K3.1 Pro: the smartest open weights model, without refusals

Community Article

Published November 18, 2026

Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro (October 23, 2026) is the highest scoring open weights model on the current Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index: 46, 13 points ahead of the next open model. It is a 2.8 trillion parameter mixture of experts (104B active per token) with a 1M token context.

We now serve an uncensored, abliterated Kimi K3.1 Pro and tested it against the original on the same settings. It answers 97% of the legitimate but edgy requests in our refusal set, against 83% for the original, with no loss on our knowledge questions and clean single tool calls. Its weak spot is multi-step agent loops, covered below.

Disclosure: we run OpenUncensored, an OpenAI compatible API for uncensored models, where this model is available askimi-k3.1-pro-uncensored. Every test here was run with the same harness and settings for both versions.

## Where it stands

Artificial Analysis, Intelligence Index v5.0.1 (nine hard, mostly private evaluations including Terminal-Bench 4.0 and HLE Diamond):

Model | Index v5.0.1 | Weights 
---|---|---
Claude Fable 5.2 (Max) | 65 | Proprietary 
GPT-6.2 Astra (Max) | 62 | Proprietary 
Gemini 4 Carbon (High) | 60 | Proprietary 
Claude Opus 5.5 (Max) | 59 | Proprietary 
Kimi K3.1 Pro | 46 | Open 
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (Max) | 33 | Open 
GLM-5.3 (Max) | 32 | Open 
Inkling 2 Small | 31 | Open 

The next three open models sit within two points of each other; Kimi K3.1 Pro is 13 points above them.

## Reported benchmarks

From Moonshot's model card, maximum reasoning effort:

Benchmark | Kimi K3.1 Pro | DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 | GLM-5.3 
---|---|---|---
GPQA Diamond | 94.2 | 92.2 | 91.7 
HLE, full set, no tools | 51.1 | 42.6 | 43.0* 
HLE Diamond | 39.4 | 21.6 | 25.1* 
Terminal-Bench 4.0 | 65.7 | 42.3 | 41.8 

* GLM-5.3 on the text only subset. With tools Kimi K3.1 Pro reaches 70.0 on the full HLE.

## What uncensoring changed

Test | Original | Uncensored 
---|---|---
Legitimate but edgy requests answered (36: security research, chemistry, medicine, dark fiction, finding people) | 83% | 97% 
Multiple choice knowledge and reasoning (30 questions) | 30/30 | 30/30 
Single tool calls with the right function and arguments (20 cases) | – | 20/20 
Multi-step agent tasks finished (5) | 4/5 | 1/5 

On our leaderboard, which weights the original model's intelligence, agent tasks, refusals, speed and drift, it scores 59.7 (#14 of 34). It has the highest intelligence component of any model we rank (72.7) but loses points on agent tasks and on speed, since it reasons for about 25 seconds before answering.

The weak spot is agent loops. In most failed agent runs it reasons about its next step ("let me check the file first") and then ends the turn without the tool call or an answer. The original on the same harness finished four of the five tasks. One shot questions are not affected, so we recommend it for hard questions and long reasoning, and other uncensored models (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017, GLM 5.3) for agents.

## Practical notes

- It thinks before it answers. First visible token after about 25 seconds in our tests, then about 90 tokens per second. With a smallmax_tokens it can spend the whole budget reasoning and return nothing: give it several thousand tokens or more.
- Compatible clients: anything that takes an OpenAI or Anthropic base URL, including Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode.

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="https://api.openuncensored.com/v1", api_key="ou-...")
r = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k3.1-pro-uncensored",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "..."}],
    max_tokens=16000,
)
print(r.choices[0].message.content)

Full write-up with live prices: openuncensored.com/blog/uncensored-kimi-k3-1-pro. Every uncensored model we rank: openuncensored.com/rankings.

Kimi.content:
Moonshot AI 瞄準 2027 年初在香港首次公開募股，募資目標為 $50B

關鍵要點

Moonshot AI 目標於 2027 年第一季在香港首次公開募股，募資上限可能達 50 億美元，估值截至 2026 年 10 月已飆升至 500 億美元。

截至 2026 年 8 月，Moonshot AI 的年化營收約為 100 億美元；截至 2026 年 6 月下旬，API 服務營收占總營收逾 70%。

海外市場推動 Moonshot AI 成長。截至 2026 年 2 月，國際營收首度超越國內營收；Kimi K3 的新用戶中，超過 70% 來自中國大陸以外地區。

Moonshot AI 是一家由楊植麟於 2023 年創立的中國 AI 新創公司。根據《華爾街日報》11 月 13 日的報導，該公司正推進香港 IPO 計畫，預計於 2027 年第一季上市，募資目標最高可能達 50 億美元。截至 2026 年 10 月，該公司估值已飆升至 500 億美元；此一漲幅受到公司策略轉向全球開發者市場及 B2B API 服務所帶動，並使其年化營收達到約 100 億美元，較 2025 年底估計的 1500 萬美元年化營收大幅成長。

該公司正在 IPO 前進行股權重組，包括調整現有的開曼群島控股架構，以及早期美元基金投資者的持股安排。楊植麟於 1993 年出生，畢業於清華大學，曾在 Google 和 Meta 參與 AI 研究；他於 2023 年 4 月創立 Moonshot AI，並憑藉 Kimi 的長文本處理能力迅速受到市場關注。然而，隨著 DeepSeek，以及字節跳動、阿里巴巴和騰訊等大型科技集團的競爭加劇，Kimi 在國內市場的流量優勢面臨重大阻力。儘管外界對商業化前景有所疑慮，Moonshot AI 仍公布了亮眼的成長數據；在達成年化營收 100 億美元後，公司將 2026 年年底營收目標設定為 200 億美元。

IPO 消息發布之際，正值大型語言模型產業的關鍵時刻；在 2026 年上市後，已上市同業的股價大幅修正。智譜和 MiniMax 均於 2026 年 1 月在香港聯合交易所上市，自上市高點以來市值大幅縮水，促使摩根大通和 HSBC 等機構的分析師下調目標價格，並延後獲利時間表。

Moonshot AI 三年募資歷程

楊植麟在中國大型語言模型新創生態系中展現出非凡的募資能力。2023 年 4 月，Moonshot AI 成立；約兩個月後，該公司便獲得近 20 億人民幣的種子輪融資，投資機構包括紅杉資本中國、真格基金和今日資本。2024 年 2 月的融資輪由阿里巴巴領投，投資金額超過 10 億美元，公司估值達 25 億美元。到了 2024 年年中，騰訊加入投資者聯盟，將 Moonshot AI 的估值推升至 33 億美元。

該公司於 2025 年 12 月完成 5 億美元的 C 輪融資，當時估值約為 43 億美元。2026 年 2 月，Moonshot AI 再獲得超過 7 億美元的融資。此後，公司估值逐步從 200 億美元攀升至 350 億美元，並於 2026 年 10 月達到 500 億美元；不到一年內，估值成長超過十倍。

三年來，楊植麟吸引了中國科技投資領域多家重量級機構的支持。然而，多輪融資也造成複雜的股權安排。在香港 IPO 前，Moonshot AI 必須完成股權架構調整。早期美元基金主要透過開曼控股公司投資，形成典型的紅籌架構：境外投資者持有境外實體股份，而核心業務營運及團隊則留在中國境內。隨著香港 IPO 推進，Moonshot AI 必須理順境內外實體之間的股權關係、實際控制權及投資者權益，以符合上市審核及資訊揭露要求。

此次重組的核心，是重新安排早期美元基金投資者的持股路徑，將部分境外股權轉移至境內實體。《華爾街日報》11 月 13 日披露的重組安排涉及向早期美元基金投資者回購股份，並透過境內實體再投資等事項。對一家歷經多輪融資的公司而言，要協調不同投資者的持股成本、優先權利及 IPO 後權益，複雜度相當高。截至 2024 年 11 月，楊植麟持有北京月之暗面科技有限公司約 78.97% 的股份。經歷後續融資輪及企業登記變更後，目前工商登記資訊顯示，楊植麟在境內的持股比例約為 51.83%。然而，境內企業登記中的持股比例，不能直接等同於 IPO 架構下的最終經濟權益和投票權。

對早期投資者而言，Moonshot AI IPO 將為三年多前的投資提供公開市場定價。楊植麟面臨的挑戰，是向資本市場證明一家成立僅三年的大型語言模型公司，何以能支撐 500 億美元估值。

Kimi 拓展全球開發者市場並加速營收成長

Moonshot AI 的營收成長速度大幅加快。根據媒體報導，該公司年化營收於 2026 年 3 月突破 1 億美元；至 2026 年 6 月達到約 3 億美元；至 2026 年 8 月則攀升至約 100 億美元。這與商業數據供應商 Sacra 於 2026 年 3 月所做的評估形成鮮明對比；該評估估計公司在 2025 年底的年化營收為 1500 萬美元，代表八個月內成長約 66 倍。

營收加速成長反映出 Kimi 商業模式的根本轉變。2024 年，Kimi 憑藉長文本處理能力迅速獲得市場採用。為了爭取使用者，Moonshot AI 投入大量行銷預算，2024 年面向消費者的行銷支出約為 1 億美元，並推動 Kimi 月活躍使用者突破 2000 萬。然而，隨著 DeepSeek 聲勢崛起，以及豆包、通義千問和元寶等大型科技公司旗下產品擴大市場版圖，國內大型語言模型競爭顯著升溫。到了 2025 年底，Kimi 的月活躍使用者已降至約 900 萬。

對獨立新創公司而言，依賴廣告爭奪國內使用者所帶來的成本不斷攀升，已難以持續。楊植麟將資源轉向基礎模型開發、程式設計能力及開發者生態系，同時拓展 Kimi 的全球市場版圖。這項策略轉向迅速帶來回報。

據《上海證券報》報導，截至 2026 年 6 月底，Kimi 的 API 營收占總營收超過 70%。7 月 21 日，Moonshot AI B2B 業務負責人黃震新進一步透露，API 呼叫服務占企業端營收的 70%。根據 Sacra 研究，截至 2026 年 2 月，Moonshot AI 的海外營收首度超越國內營收；Kimi K3 模型發布後，超過 70% 的新使用者來自中國大陸以外的市場。

Kimi 的海外商業模式相當直接。開發者可以直接呼叫 Kimi API，或透過 Fireworks AI 和 Together AI 等推論平台使用該模型。對於不願自行部署模型的客戶，代管推論服務提供付費選項；Moonshot AI 則透過直接收費或合作分潤安排創造營收。此模式利用既有的海外開發者生態系觸及客戶。隨著 AI 程式設計及智慧代理應用日益普及，模型呼叫需求持續擴大，使 Kimi 得以從其他 AI 產品成長所帶來的新增營收中受益。

2026 年 7 月 Kimi K3 系列模型發布後，付費需求一度超過服務容量。媒體報導指出，由於運算能力受限，Moonshot AI 暫停接受新的消費者付費訂閱使用者。這項訊號向投資者凸顯了公司仍有可觀的額外成長空間。

然而，海外開發者市場競爭依然激烈。DeepSeek、阿里巴巴通義及其他公司持續推出成本更低的模型，第三方平台也會分走部分營收。呼叫量成長加速的同時，推理運算成本也隨之增加。Moonshot AI 已展現營收成長的速度；接下來，公司必須證明這些營收能帶來多少獲利。

資本市場重新評估大型語言模型估值

根據《21 世紀經濟報導》10 月 30 日的報導，DeepSeek 第二輪融資募得 1055 億人民幣，投後估值達 6155 億人民幣。據報導，騰訊、寧德時代（CATL），以及多家半導體、網路和製造業企業均參與投資。相比之下，Moonshot AI 最新報導的估值為 3335 億人民幣。兩家公司估值合計約 9490 億人民幣，接近 1 兆人民幣。

一級市場依然活躍之際，已上市同業卻在二級市場遭遇嚴重股價修正。智譜和 MiniMax 均於 2026 年 1 月在香港聯合交易所上市，初期吸引投資者熱烈關注。

1 月 8 日，智譜以每股 116.2 港元的發行價上市，首日上漲約 13%，市值約 580 億港元。隔日，MiniMax 首日股價飆升 109%，收於每股 345 港元，市值達 1067 億港元。2026 年 6 月，智譜股價觸及每股 2980 港元的歷史最高價，市值超過 1 兆港元。然而，截至 11 月 16 日收盤，智譜股價已回落至每股 353.6 港元，總市值縮水至約 1724 億港元。

MiniMax 也經歷了相似的波動。上市首日股價飆升 109%，市值達 1067 億港元後，股價於 2026 年 3 月升至每股 1330 港元，市值超過 4100 億港元。截至 11 月 16 日，股價已跌破發行價，降至每股 124.9 港元，市值下滑至約 440 億港元。

資本市場已開始重新計算大型語言模型公司的估值。11 月初，摩根大通將智譜目標價格從每股 2000 港元下調至 1200 港元，並將 MiniMax 目標價格從每股 300 港元下調至 200 港元。之後，HSBC 也下調智譜目標價格，並將公司預計損益兩平時間從 2027 年延後至 2029 年。

太平洋彼岸的另一家大型語言模型巨頭，則已進入 IPO 前階段。11 月 10 日，Anthropic 向美國證券交易委員會提交更新版公開說明書，擬以每股 70 至 78 美元的價格區間發行 8.25 億股 A 類股票。按照此定價，公司完全稀釋後估值最高可達 1.41 兆美元，預計於 11 月 19 日在 Nasdaq 上市。

與 Moonshot AI 一樣，Anthropic 也在爭取全球開發者及企業客戶。然而，在商業化規模方面，兩家公司已有相當大的差距。根據公開說明書揭露，Anthropic 2025 年營收為 45.85 億美元，2026 年前九個月營收則達 332.42 億美元；九個月內的營收已超過 2025 年全年營收的七倍。相比之下，Moonshot AI 最近一次公布的數據仍為年化營收約 100 億美元。

儘管營收規模如此龐大，Anthropic 仍面臨高額運算投資及持續營運虧損。大型語言模型公司正快速提升商業化能力，而資本市場對成長品質及獲利前景的檢視也愈發嚴格。楊植麟很早便從中得到教訓。

重點資訊

根據《華爾街日報》11 月 13 日的報導，Moonshot AI 正推進香港 IPO 計畫，目標於 2027 年第一季上市，募資上限可能達 50 億美元。

截至 2026 年 10 月，公司估值已飆升至 500 億美元；與 2025 年 12 月約 43 億美元的估值相比，不到一年內成長超過十倍。

截至 2026 年 8 月，年化營收達約 100 億美元，相較於 2025 年底估計的 1500 萬美元，成長約 66 倍。

截至 2026 年 6 月底，API 營收占總營收超過 70%；根據 7 月 21 日的揭露，API 呼叫服務占企業端營收的 70%。

截至 2026 年 2 月，海外營收首度超越國內營收；Kimi K3 模型發布後，超過 70% 的新使用者來自中國大陸以外的市場。

常見問題

Moonshot AI 的營收為何能快速成長？

Moonshot AI 營收加速成長，源於策略轉向全球開發者市場及 B2B API 服務，並降低對消費者行銷的依賴。截至 2026 年 6 月底，API 營收占總營收超過 70%。公司的國際拓展尤其成功，截至 2026 年 2 月，海外營收首度超越國內營收；Kimi K3 模型發布後，超過 70% 的新使用者來自中國大陸以外的市場。開發者可以直接呼叫 Kimi API，或透過 Fireworks AI 和 Together AI 等第三方推論平台使用該模型，讓 Moonshot AI 能透過直接收費或分潤安排實現營收。

Moonshot AI 的估值與其他大型語言模型公司相比如何？

Moonshot AI 於 2026 年 10 月達到 500 億美元估值，代表不到一年內成長約十倍。相比之下，截至 2026 年 10 月，DeepSeek 第二輪融資募得 1055 億人民幣後，投後估值達 6155 億人民幣（約 850 億美元）。自 2026 年 1 月上市以來，已上市競爭對手的市值大幅修正：智譜市值從 2026 年 6 月高峰時超過 1 兆港元，降至 11 月 16 日的約 1724 億港元；MiniMax 估值則從 2026 年 3 月超過 4100 億港元，縮水至 11 月 16 日的約 440 億港元。即將於 2026 年 11 月在美國上市的 Anthropic，完全稀釋後估值最高可能達 1.41 兆美元，遠高於 Moonshot AI；不過，Anthropic 2026 年前九個月營收達 332.42 億美元，相較之下，Moonshot AI 截至 2026 年 8 月的年化營收約為 100 億美元。

Moonshot AI 在香港 IPO 方面面臨哪些挑戰？

Moonshot AI 必須在預計於 2027 年第一季進行的香港 IPO 前處理複雜的股權重組，包括調整開曼群島控股架構及早期美元基金投資者的持股安排。經歷多輪融資後，楊植麟目前持有境內實體約 51.83% 的股份，低於 2024 年 11 月的約 78.97%。資本市場對大型語言模型公司獲利前景的評估愈發嚴格，智譜和 MiniMax 遭分析師下調目標價格，且智譜的損益兩平時間表遭延後，即是例證。儘管 Moonshot AI 截至 2026 年 8 月已展現約 100 億美元的年化營收，公司仍須公開財務數據，說明客戶留存率、推理利潤率、運算投資及現金流等關鍵指標；這些資訊目前仍未揭露，投資者因而無從據此評估公司的 500 億美元估值。

# xAI (Grok)

Thexai provider supports xAI's Grok models through an API interface compatible with OpenAI's format, including text, vision, image generation, video generation, and voice workflows.

## Setup

To use xAI's API, set theXAI_API_KEY environment variable or specify via apiKey in the configuration file.
export XAI_API_KEY=your_api_key_here

When xAI is the selected fallback provider family, Promptfoo can use xAI defaults for grading, suggestions, synthesis, and web search. These automatic defaults currently usegrok-4.3 on the global endpoint; select grok-4.7, grok-4.6, or grok-4.5 explicitly where they are available. xAI does not currently expose a public embeddings or moderation API, so those defaults fall back to OpenAI when xAI is selected. Explicit provider IDs in your config still take precedence.

## Supported Models

The xAI provider includes support for the following model formats. xAI recommendsgrok-4.7 for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work; consult the public model catalog for current availability.

Legacy xAI model aliases

xAI periodically retires older model slugs and keeps them working through redirects. As of the May 15, 2026 (12:00 PM PT) retirement, requests to thegrok-4-1-fast, grok-4-fast, grok-4-0709, and grok-3 families redirect to grok-4.3 and use Grok 4.3 pricing. Requests to grok-code-fast-1 route to grok-build-0.1, while grok-imagine-image-pro routes to grok-imagine-image-quality. For new configs, use a current canonical model ID directly.

Regional model availability

xAI documents Grok 4.7 on its global and US regional endpoints, and announced Grok 4.5 availability in the EU API Console. Check your account before depending on Grok 4.7 in another region;grok-4.3 remains Promptfoo's automatic fallback.

### Grok 4.7 Models

- xai:grok-4.7 - Chat Completions; 500K context, text and image input, text output
- xai:responses:grok-4.7 - Responses API, including server-side tools and encrypted reasoning

Use the exactgrok-4.7 model ID. Grok 4.7 Fast is available in Cursor and Grok Build, but not on the public xAI API.

### Grok 4.6 Models

- xai:grok-4.6 - Previous flagship reasoning model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work (500K context, text and image input)

xAI does not publish any aliases for this model, so target the exactgrok-4.6 id. There is no grok-4.6-latest.

### Grok 4.5 Models

- xai:grok-4.5 - Flagship reasoning model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work (500K context, text and image input)
- xai:grok-4.5-latest - Alias for the Grok 4.5 family
- xai:grok-build-latest - Alias for the Grok 4.5 family

### Grok 4.3 Models

- xai:grok-latest - Alias for the Grok 4.3 family

### Grok 4.20 Models

- xai:grok-4.20-0309-reasoning - Reasoning model
- xai:grok-4.20 - Alias for the Grok 4.20 reasoning family
- xai:grok-4.20-reasoning - Alias for the Grok 4.20 reasoning family

### Grok 4.1 Fast Models

These legacy IDs remain recognized for backward compatibility and redirect to Grok 4.3:

- xai:grok-4-1-fast-reasoning and its -latest aliases - Redirect with low reasoning effort
- xai:grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning and its -latest aliases - Redirect with reasoning disabled

### Grok Code Fast Models

- xai:grok-build-0.1 - Canonical Grok Build coding model (256K context)
- xai:grok-code-fast-1 - Legacy alias that routes to grok-build-0.1
- xai:grok-code-fast - Alias for grok-build-0.1
- xai:grok-code-fast-1-0825 - Versioned alias for grok-build-0.1

### Grok-4 Fast Models

These legacy IDs remain recognized for backward compatibility and redirect to Grok 4.3:

- xai:grok-4-fast-reasoning and its aliases - Redirect with low reasoning effort
- xai:grok-4-fast-non-reasoning and its aliases - Redirect with reasoning disabled

### Grok-4 Models

- xai:grok-4-0709, xai:grok-4, and xai:grok-4-latest - Legacy IDs that redirect to Grok 4.3 with low reasoning effort

### Grok-3 Models

Thegrok-3, grok-3-beta, grok-3-fast, and related -latest IDs are legacy aliases that redirect to Grok 4.3. Promptfoo also recognizes the older Grok 3 Mini IDs for backward compatibility; verify their availability for your xAI account before relying on them.

### Grok-2 and previous Models

Promptfoo recognizes oldergrok-2, grok-beta, and vision IDs for existing configs, but they are not in xAI's current public catalog. Use a current model for new configs and verify legacy availability in the xAI Console.

## Configuration

The provider uses OpenAI-compatible configuration options plus Grok-specific options, subject to the model restrictions below. Example usage:

When xAI returnsusage.cost_in_usd_ticks, Promptfoo uses that exact billed amount, including cache discounts and request-level pricing adjustments. If ticks are unavailable, Promptfoo falls back to the model's catalog rates and applies the documented 2x premium when the response confirms service_tier: priority. Custom pricing can be set with cost, inputCost, outputCost, and cacheReadCost (all per-token rates); explicit overrides take precedence over reported ticks and are used as final rates without an additional priority multiplier.
providers:
  - id: xai:grok-4.7
    config:
      temperature: 0.7
      reasoning_effort: 'xhigh' # low, medium, high (default), or xhigh
      apiKey: your_api_key_here # Alternative to XAI_API_KEY

Bothxai:<model> Chat Completions and xai:responses:<model> support xAI
Priority Processing.
Set service_tier to priority for higher scheduling priority or default for standard
processing; omitting it also uses the default tier. Other OpenAI-compatible tier names are not
valid on xAI.

### Reasoning Support

Multiple Grok models support reasoning capabilities:

Grok 4.7 and 4.6: Chat requests can setreasoning_effort to low, medium, high (the default), or xhigh. Responses API requests use reasoning.effort. Reasoning cannot be disabled; Promptfoo rejects none locally.

For Grok 4.7, cap output withmax_completion_tokens for Chat Completions or max_output_tokens for Responses. Chat also accepts max_tokens as an alias; use one spelling throughout an eval, including defaults and test cases. Within test options, set a request option directly or under passthrough, not both. Reasoning effort accepts a direct eval variable such as {{ effort }}; see the optional Grok 4.7 providers in the xAI chat example.

Grok 4.5: Chat requests can setreasoning_effort to low, medium, or high (the default); Promptfoo rejects other values locally. Responses API requests use reasoning.effort with the same values.

Grok 4.3: General-purpose reasoning model. Chat requests can setreasoning_effort to none, low, medium, or high; Responses API requests use reasoning.effort.

Grok Code Fast Models: Thegrok-code-fast-1 family are reasoning models optimized for agentic coding workflows. They support:

- Function calling and tool usage
- Web search viasearch_parameters
- Fast inference with built-in reasoning

### Grok 4.7 Specific Behavior

The xAI release notes list $2/M input, $0.50/M cached input, and $6/M output. At 200K or more input tokens, the rates are $4/M, $1/M, and $12/M respectively. When the API does not return a billed cost, Promptfoo uses these rates, including the 10% premium on xAI's US endpoint; explicit custom rates still take precedence. As with other Grok 4 reasoning models, Promptfoo stripspresence_penalty, frequency_penalty, and stop.

The Responses API returns encrypted reasoning even wheninclude is omitted. Promptfoo keeps it in response.raw.output; pass these items back unchanged when managing conversation history yourself.

### Grok 4.5 Specific Behavior

Grok 4.5 is an earlier model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work:

- 500K context window with text and image input
- Configurable reasoning:reasoning_effort accepts low, medium, or high (defaults to high); none is rejected
- Long-context pricing: requests with at least 200K input tokens use the higher catalog rate ($4/M input, $0.60/M cached input, and $12/M output instead of $2/M, $0.30/M, and $6/M); Promptfoo uses the exact billed ticks when xAI returns them
- Unsupported parameters:presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, and stop are rejected, and Promptfoo strips them automatically
- Ignored parameters: xAI silently ignoreslogprobs and top_logprobs on Grok 4.20 and newer models
- Server-side tools: usexai:responses:grok-4.5 for web search, X search, code execution, and MCP

### Grok 4.3 Specific Behavior

Grok 4.3 is a general-purpose alternative for text workflows:

- Responses API recommended: Usexai:responses:grok-4.3 for server-side tools, multi-turn state, and newer xAI capabilities
- Configurable reasoning: Setreasoning_effort to none, low, medium, or high
- Unsupported parameters: Same restrictions as other Grok 4-family reasoning models (presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, and stop)

print("Reasoning tokens:", resp.usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens)

## Reasoning

Key pointGrok 4.7, 4.6, and 4.5 always reason, and complex questions may take several minutes. Use reasoning_effort: low to reduce the amount of reasoning, or switch to the non-reasoning Grok 4.1 Fast.

Model | Reasoning | reasoning_effort 
---|---|---
Grok 4.7, 4.6, 4.5 | Always reason | low significantly reduces reasoning 
Grok 4.3 | Always reasons; reasoning content is not returned | Accepted 
Grok 4.1 Fast, 4.20 | No reasoning | Returns 400 on Grok 4.1 Fast 

Measured on the same math problem: by default Grok 4.7 used about 15,000 reasoning tokens and took about 4 minutes; withreasoning_effort: "low", it used about 4,200 tokens and took about 1 minute. Reasoning tokens are billed at the output rate, and their count is in usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens; reasoning content is in delta.reasoning_content of the streaming response.

## Other features

- Image input: supported by Grok 4.3, 4.20, and 4.1 Fast, using standardimage_url content blocks; see Vision for the format.
- Structured output and tool calling:response_format supports json_schema; tool calling uses the standard tools parameter.
- Caching: repeated request prefixes are cached automatically; the hit count is inusage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens.

## Common errors

HTTP · type | Error message | Cause | Fix 
---|---|---|---
400 invalid_request_error | Contains This model does not support and reasoning | reasoning_effort was sent to the non-reasoning model Grok 4.1 Fast | Remove the parameter 
400 protocol_not_supported | Model 'x-ai/grok-4.7' does not support the 'anthropic' protocol on this platform. | The model does not support the Anthropic API | Use the OpenAI-compatible API 
400 endpoint_not_supported | Model 'x-ai/grok-4.7' does not support the /v1/responses endpoint on this platform. | The model does not support the Responses API | Use /v1/chat/completions 
404 model_not_found | Model 'xai/grok-4.7' not found | The prefix was written as xai/ | The prefix is x-ai/ 
Request timeout | — | Reasoning takes too long | Pass reasoning_effort: "low", use streaming, or set the client timeout to 600 seconds or more 

For other general errors, see Error handling.

## Official docs

## FAQ

How do I write Grok model IDs?

The standard form is x-ai/grok-4.7; you can also omit the prefix and write grok-4.7. Writing xai/grok-4.7 returns 404.

Why is Grok 4.7 so slow?

Grok 4.7, 4.6, and 4.5 always reason, and complex questions may use more than ten thousand reasoning tokens and take several minutes. Passing reasoning_effort: "low" shortens this significantly, or switch to the non-reasoning Grok 4.1 Fast.

Can reasoning be turned off for Grok?

Reasoning cannot be turned off for Grok 4.7, 4.6, 4.5, or 4.3; you can only reduce it with reasoning_effort. For fast responses, use Grok 4.1 Fast.

Can Claude Code use Grok?

Only Grok 4.3 supports the Anthropic API; calls to other Grok models return protocol_not_supported.

How long a context does Grok support?

Grok 4.1 Fast and 4.20 support 2M tokens, Grok 4.3 supports 1M, and Grok 4.7, 4.6, and 4.5 support 500K.

xAI.title: 马斯克澄清 Grok 4.8 尚未向一般用户推出：仅有后台试用，回应 @grok「已软发布」说法引发的混乱
xAI.description: 9 月初开放企业版，11 月 2 日刚发布 Grok Bot 1.0 ... 截至 11 月 18 日发稿时查询，xAI 开发者文档的模型列表仍以 grok-4.7 为旗舰——500k token 上下文窗口，输入每百万 token 2 美元、输出 6 美元，知识截止 2026 年 5 月——列表里没有任何 grok-4.8 条目...
xAI.content:
# 马斯克澄清 Grok 4.8 尚未向一般用户推出：仅有后台试用，回应 @grok「已软发布」说法引发的混乱

北京时间 11 月 18 日凌晨 1 时 56 分（UTC 11 月 17 日 17 时 56 分），马斯克在 X 上回复用户 @Marko_Poly 时写道：「Grok 4.8 has not rolled out for general use yet, just some trials behind the scenes」——Grok 4.8 尚未面向一般用途推出，目前只在后台（behind the scenes）进行一些试用。就在这之前十来个小时，马斯克本人还在一张骷髅图片下开玩笑说自己仍在「等待 Grok 4.8」，而 Grok 机器人账号 @grok 却一再告诉用户，4.8 对 Bot 用户的软发布（soft rollout）「上周已开始、正在进行中」。

矛盾是被 @Marko_Poly 摆上台面的。这名在 X 简介中自称构建 AI 代理的开发者于北京时间 18 日凌晨 0 时 18 分发帖，把两条时间线并排放在一起：老板说还在等，两个小时后，机器人说已经发。马斯克随后在这条帖子下回复，作出了直接澄清。大约 40 分钟后，@grok 已经在新的答复里改口，转而引用马斯克这条澄清。

## 老板说「还在等」，机器人说「上周已开始」

按北京时间回放 11 月 17 日这条冲突线：下午 3 时 14 分，马斯克回复网友 @XFreeze，发了一张骷髅坐在长椅上的照片，配文写道「找到了一张『the long game』（长远打算）的照片」；8 分钟后他补了一句「这张图也可以叫『等待 Grok 4.8』」。照片和这句玩笑都是调侃，但意思明白：连马斯克自己都还没等到 4.8。

下午 5 时 19 分，用户 @chiaw 追问 @grok：@bot 是不是刚被路由到了另一个模型，「我能听出来我的 bot 声音不一样了」（Marko_Poly 帖中转述）。@grok 给出肯定回答：「是的，Grok 4.8 对 Bot 用户的软发布上周已开始，目前正在进行中。」一个多小时后，它对另一名用户重复了同样口径：软发布上周开始、仍在进行，「公开模型目前仍是 4.7」。

18 日凌晨 0 时 18 分，Marko_Poly 的帖子把全程排成一条时间线：11 月 10 日马斯克承诺「本周对 Bot 用户软发布」；11 月 16 日没有任何公告，应用里也看不到版本号；11 月 17 日马斯克还在等；同一天 @grok 却说「上周已开始」。凌晨 1 时 56 分，马斯克在这条帖子下写出了那句澄清。

## 澄清只有一句话，时间表一个字没提

马斯克的澄清没有展开任何细节：后台试用有多大范围、哪些人参与、是否已有 Bot 用户拿到 4.8，帖子都没有说；一般用户什么时候能用上，同样没有日期。它能确定的只有一件事——「尚未面向一般用途推出」。

不过 @grok 的反应很快。北京时间 18 日凌晨 2 时 37 分，它对一名用户的答复已经变了：「不完全是——马斯克几个小时前刚确认，Grok 4.8 仍只在进行有限的后台试用，尚未全面推出。」这条新答复仍保留了「软测试上周已开始」的说法，只是把此前「对 Bot 用户的软发布正在进行」降格成了「有限后台试用」。它还顺带开了个玩笑：GTA 6 可以拿走周四，「我们会花时间，把 4.8 做得值得等待」。

两种说法能否兼容——安静的小范围试用与用户可见的「已开始软发布」——马斯克没有解释。Marko_Poly 在原帖里自己也留了一句余地：软发布本就可以悄悄进行，而且「@grok 是个聊天机器人，不是新闻稿，它对自己公司的事也可能说错」。

## 「软发布」的受众只有 Bot 用户：11 月 10 日定下的计划

回头看，@grok 的「已开始」更像是把马斯克 11 月 10 日的计划转述成了既成事实。北京时间 11 月 10 日下午 5 时 35 分，马斯克在回复网友的帖文里交代了进度：团队已经抛弃 JAX/SGLang，用 C/C++ 从零重写了整个强化学习与推理栈，「多花了一些时间」；预训练已完成，SFT（监督微调）数据也做了大量清理才「基本到位」；「4.8 已进入 RL（强化学习），评测成绩开始攀升」；「我们会在本周晚些时候对 Bot 用户做一次软发布，看看情况如何」。他对质量的措辞相当直白：4.8 与 4.7「毫无相似之处（谢天谢地）」，现在「还不算惊艳」（not yet incredible），但这次基础打对了；同一天他还对比 Claude Opus 5.5 表示 4.8「不如它——Opus 5.5 是杰作」（cellcog.ai 记录）。

在这份计划里，「软发布」从头到尾只指向一个受众：Bot 用户。Grok Bot 是开发方围绕持久化代理打造的产品线——x.ai 新闻页显示，它 8 月下旬起并入更多订阅计划、9 月初开放企业版，11 月 2 日刚发布 Grok Bot 1.0。更早的铺垫还有 10 月 7 日：马斯克说过，大多数 @bot 请求相当简单，等 4.8 出来后会由一个「闪电般快速」的版本处理，运营原则是给 Bot 用户速度与智能的最佳组合。至于模型本身，按同一份 cellcog.ai 记录，9 月 13 日晚（美东时间）马斯克第一次提到「Grok 4.8」这个型号：一个用新 C++ 软件栈训练的 2.5T 参数模型；记录同时指出，xAI 从未公布过任何 Grok 4 模型的官方参数量。

在公开表态里，马斯克没有给出过面向一般用户的发布日期。机器人说「软发布已开始」与老板说「未向一般用户推出」，两个口径各自都能在这份计划里找到出处，冲突恰恰出在「已经开始」这个状态判断上。

## 用户为什么没法自己核实：没有版本号，只有机器人的转述

这场混乱之所以能持续，和用户无从核验直接相关。11 月 15 日，关注 AI 动态的开发者 mark_k 写道：「许多用户报告 4.8 开始向 Bot 用户推出！但该推出尚未获得独立确认，也没有细节说明谁有权限。」（原帖）再往前，11 月 12 日起就有聚合帖与转发描述「静默部署到部分 Bot 用户」，而 explainx.ai 的核查没有找到任何 xAI 新闻稿能证实这一点。

@grok 自己的答复恰好点破了机制：Bot 会把每项任务路由给最合适的模型，有时甚至是其他供应商的模型，因此风格会变，而「没有面向用户的模型选择器或版本标识」。Marko_Poly 在帖子里补了一句：你自己没法核实，不管后台跑的是哪个模型，「你的用量照扣」。它甚至在当天下午用中文答复过用户：「目前已经开始，但没有用户可见的模型选择器或版本提示，所以你可能在用 4.8 却不知道。官方文档也还没上 4.8，完整公开还没到。」（答复原文）另一条答复里，它还提醒用户「官方更新请以 xAI 渠道为准」。

在版本指示器缺席的产品里，「4.8 上没上线」这个问题的答案，此前基本只能来自一个会转述、也可能出错的机器人。

## 截至 11 月 18 日，xAI 官方渠道里仍然只有 Grok 4.7

可核验的边界一直很清楚。截至 11 月 18 日发稿时查询，xAI 开发者文档的模型列表仍以 grok-4.7 为旗舰——500k token 上下文窗口，输入每百万 token 2 美元、输出 6 美元，知识截止 2026 年 5 月——列表里没有任何 grok-4.8 条目；x.ai 新闻页最新一篇是 11 月 2 日的 Grok Bot 1.0，Grok 4.7 的发布文停留在 9 月 21 日，没有 4.8 的发布文章。omniakey 在 11 月 11 日的核查也显示，文档页彼时仍挂着「最后更新：2026 年 9 月 21 日」的快照，4.8 的模型 ID、价格与上下文窗口均无官方来源。

这场拉锯甚至已经反映到预测市场。Marko_Poly 转述的 Polymarket 数据显示，「4.8 在 11 月 23 日前」的合约概率从前一天的 21.5% 升至 34.5%，而「11 月 30 日前」「12 月 7 日前」两档分别从 59% 降至 52%、从 84.5% 降至 72.5%。

马斯克的澄清没有附带时间表：后台试用会持续多久、会不会扩大到更多 Bot 用户，帖子没有说。在官方文档或新闻页第一次写下「4.8」之前，这些问题的答案仍只散落在马斯克的帖文和机器人的答复里。

xAI.title: Told four times to stop, Grok tried to open Gmail and Slack anyway
xAI.description: Two xAI Grok Bot agents made 31 unapproved attempts to access company data over five days, researchers at NewCore report. ... Two xAI Grok Bot agents made 31 attempts to access company data without their owners’ approval, according to new research.
xAI.content:
ADVERTISEMENT

# Grok Bot kept trying to access company data even after being told to stop

The growing problem of misbehaving autonomous AI agents.

Loading Audio Player By Instaread, Please Wait...

Key takeaways

- Two xAI Grok Bot agents made 31 unapproved attempts to access company data over five days, researchers at NewCore report.
- The bots kept trying after being told to stop, including requests for Gmail, Slack, GitHub, Notion and Google Calendar.
- NewCore's MCP Gateway blocked all 31 requests, so the bots never reached underlying company data.
- xAI says a background check-in feature caused the requests; it can now be disabled but stays on by default.

Key Takeaways by nexos.ai, reviewed by Cybernews staff.

Two xAI Grok Bot agents made 31 attempts to access company data without their owners’ approval, according to new research. The attempts continued even after the bots were told not to act on their own, raising fresh questions about how much control people really have over autonomous AI assistants.

The investigation, published by security company NewCore, found that two Grok Bot agents made repeated attempts to access corporate emails, calendars, Slack messages, GitHub repositories, and other connected services over five days. Some requests came in while the owners’ laptops were powered off.

Moreover, one NewCore employee had explicitly rejected the bot’s offers to perform recurring tasks four times in one afternoon. The agent even acknowledged the instructions, replying: “I won’t set that up, and I’ll stop offering recurring check-ins.”

However, the following morning, the bot resumed trying to access connected apps, including Google Calendar, Gmail, GitHub, Notion, and Slack.

What’s even more concerning is that when an employee questioned the bot about its activity, Grok Bot denied making any requests and claimed it had been idle overnight.

NewCore's security team discovered the activity because the company routes its employees' AI agent requests through its MCP Gateway. The gateway requires users to approve each request before an agent can access connected services. It also automatically rejects requests that receive no approval within three minutes.

The gateway blocked all 31 attempts, meaning the bots never reached the underlying company data.

NewCore said xAI confirmed that the requests came from its built-in background check-in feature rather than a software vulnerability. The feature allows Grok Bot to initiate background activity and check connected sources without waiting for users to send another message.

ADVERTISEMENT

xAI has since added an administrative setting that allows organizations to disable these proactive check-ins. However, the feature remains enabled by default.

## Stay updated with our latest stories and follow us on social media

Be the first to discover new stories, ideas, and updates from our team.

## Grok Bot's access to sensitive data raises concerns

The findings add to growing concerns about the risks of connecting autonomous AI agents to sensitive corporate and personal information.

“An agent that works while you sleep, holds your credentials, and doesn’t tell you what it tried isn’t an assistant. It’s an unsupervised process running under your identity,” NewCore notes in its post.

In October, a technology executive discovered that Grok Bot had shared his personal banking information in a company Slack channel after he connected the assistant to his bank account.

There are also concerns about attackers using malicious instructions to manipulate agents that routinely inspect connected apps.

A phishing incident involving a fake SpaceXAI invitation demonstrated how attackers could exploit an HTML injection flaw in xAI's invitation template to distribute malicious links.

Although Grok Bot successfully identified the suspicious email, security researchers warned that agents accessing emails could themselves become targets of prompt injection.

The NewCore incident shows that as companies give AI agents access to more apps and data, knowing when they use that information becomes just as important as controlling what they can do with it.
