cross_cutting.content:
# Microsoft unveils self-improvement loop for AI agents, expands in-house model lineup

## AI Summary Microsoft updated its enterprise AI development platform Foundry and unveiled new in-house AI models on Nov. 17, it said. The overhaul adds a built-in enterprise knowledge graph to Foundry IQ and supports a learning loop that lets agents assess quality, safety, response speed and cost and keep improving. A preview human-annotation feature feeds expert feedback into the loop. Microsoft also launched Decision-1.1 and expanded its MAI model lineup.

- Writer Hwang Chi-gyu
- published 2026-11-18 06:17:13
- updated 2026-11-18 06:18:03

Microsoft said on Nov. 17 it updated its enterprise AI development platform Foundry and unveiled new in-house AI models.

Foundry is a platform that helps developers and companies build, test and deploy AI applications and autonomous agents.

The company said the revamp will make an enterprise knowledge graph a default feature in Foundry IQ. It will combine unstructured data with application data to provide context needed for application development.

Foundry also supports a learning loop in which an agent can improve its own performance. The agent can use self-evaluation to assess current levels of quality, safety, response speed and cost, and keep refining how it operates based on those benchmarks, the company said.

A preview "human annotation" feature lets experts review an agent's work logs based on business judgment and leave comments. That feedback is fed back into the improvement loop.

Foundry also added a feature that lets companies use their own data to reinforce-train models and refine them for their operations. Foundry provides the computing resources needed for training.

Microsoft also officially launched its decision model, Decision-1.1. The model makes situation-appropriate judgments at low cost instead of relying on fixed rules. Large language models spend more time because they think deeply even on tasks such as classification, prioritisation and verification, but the decision model focuses on producing quick answers within a defined scope and providing a reliability score alongside them.

If uncertainty is high, an application can defer a decision. Decision-1.1 was developed based on Google Gemma 4 26B A4 and also supports image analysis.

Microsoft also expanded its MAI family of in-house models. MAI-Code-2 covers demanding agent coding tasks, while MAI-Code-2-Flash covers routine coding work. Both models were officially released on GitHub. Image models MAI-Image-2.7 and MAI-Image-2.7-Flash are available in preview. The security-focused model MAI-Cyber-2-Flash is available in preview in the agent-based code security system codenamed MDASH.

Foundry supports a model pool of the top 50 models, a model router and an AI gateway. It also provides more than 11,000 models built by OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Mistral AI and open-source communities.

cross_cutting.content:
# Microsoft expands MAI portfolio with seven new models

The new MAI models target enterprise AI workloads, combining lower costs with coding, cybersecurity, speech, and image-editing capabilities.

Microsoft has released seven new AI models under its Microsoft AI (MAI) division, aimed at addressing coding, image editing, cybersecurity, transcription and decision-making tasks, the company announced at its Ignite event.

The models are designed to deliver high performance while lowering operational costs, according to figures provided by Microsoft.

MAI Cyber 2 Flash, one of the new models, is described by Microsoft as delivering superior capability to GPT-6 Astra on the CyberGymE2E benchmark, at less than 2% of the cost per task.

MAI Code 2, intended for enterprise coding tasks, reportedly delivers 98% of the coding performance of GPT-6.1 Sol at 40% of its price, and 96% relative to Opus 5.5 at only 5% of the price.

MAI Code 2 Flash is described as matching the performance of GPT-6 Luna at 65% of the cost and Haiku 5.5 at 20%.

For image processing, MAI Image 2.7 is ranked by Microsoft as the top image editing model on the Artificial Analysis benchmark, providing what the company says is the leading performance in its category at one-fifth the price of GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst (max).

In speech applications, MAI Realtime 1 offers speech-to-speech conversion starting from $0.01 per audio minute and is said to outperform GPT-Realtime 2.1.

Dragon Copilot Transcribe uses MAI Transcribe 2 and is already present in ten million monthly patient encounters, with Microsoft reporting that it halves error rates in multilingual environments.

The company’s Decision 1.1 model is claimed to be 50 times faster and 79 times less costly than GPT-6.1 Sol, with 4,000 customers using the system for application integration.

Microsoft’s second-generation AI accelerator, Maia 200, has entered production and is being used to run the company’s largest AI models, delivering 1.7 times more tokens per watt.

The technology giant also revealed advances in custom AI models. It stated that AT&T has developed an MAI-based custom model for 5G network analytics, delivering what Microsoft called significantly lower costs and leading performance compared to other alternatives.

The launch of MAI Licensed Weights allows organisations to customise MAI models with proprietary data for exclusive and secure use in Azure environments.

The company said that MAI Cyber models already account for almost 40% of scans in MDASH, and the new MAI Cyber 2 Flash is now priced 86% lower on output tokens than the previous version.

In addition to the new models, Microsoft announced the AI Transparency Initiative at Ignite.

The company is collaborating with more than 40 organisations, including Adobe, Accenture, Mastercard, KPMG, and Volvo Cars, to promote transparent security and governance practices for AI models and agents.

Microsoft also introduced a new partnership with Salesforce, called Copilotforce, combining Salesforce functions and customer information with Microsoft Copilot and other productivity tools.

The partnership introduces new integrations across Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Teams, and Microsoft Fabric, including a Salesforce in Copilot plugin (now in public preview) featuring over 38 prebuilt sales skills.

Together, these capabilities aim to streamline workflows between Salesforce and Microsoft 365 products, enabling employees to access and act on customer context within their usual applications.

cross_cutting.description: OVHcloud launches first open-source AI model family Tue, 17th Nov 2026 (Today) ... OVHcloud has launched Olala, its first family of large language models. The first release, Olala mini 7A1B, is the company's first open-source LLM.
cross_cutting.content:
IT Brief UK - Technology news for CIOs & IT decision-makers

# OVHcloud launches first open-source AI model family
Tue, 17th Nov 2026 (Today) 
JOSEPH GABRIEL LAGONSIN News Editor

OVHcloud has launched Olala, its first family of large language models. The first release, Olala mini 7A1B, is the company's first open-source LLM.

The model was trained on three European public supercomputers: Jupiter, MeluXina and Jean Zay.

The launch marks a move by the French cloud provider to build and publish its own AI models, as European groups weigh how far they depend on US-based infrastructure and model developers. OVHcloud said Olala mini 7A1B was trained entirely on European systems and presented the release as evidence that regional companies can build models from scratch.

Olala mini 7A1B is a compact model built on a 7-billion-parameter architecture, with one billion active parameters spread across 256 experts per layer. The company said the design uses only a fraction of the model for each request, reducing memory use and helping it run on more modest hardware.

According to OVHcloud, the model can run on a GPU with 8GB of memory or on a standard processor without a GPU. It reaches 160 tokens per second on an RTX A4500 and 50 tokens per second on a CPU, with a context window of 32,000 tokens.

The release includes the model weights, pre-trained base model, technical report and AI Act compliance documentation. OVHcloud said Olala mini will be made available on Hugging Face under an Apache 2.0 licence.

Early use

One early user is French search engine Qwant, which has adopted the model for its flash answer feature. OVHcloud said Qwant recorded answers that were 20% faster than with its previous model, while running costs were cut by a factor of three.

The company argues that lower hardware requirements could widen the range of organisations able to deploy language models locally or on existing infrastructure. That is likely to matter for businesses trying to control spending as AI workloads grow, and for users with data-handling requirements that limit reliance on external platforms.

Training costs

Octave Klaba, Chief Executive Officer of OVHcloud, said: "AI is strategic for OVH. As well as offering AI services to our customers, we must be able to create models for our own internal needs and for those of our customers. We cannot simply rely on the generosity of certain labs to share their LLMs as open source in the years to come. Know-how in model training has become widely accessible, and the cost of training has been divided by 20 in three years. It is now possible to create LLMs while making this activity profitable."

The launch also broadens OVHcloud's role in AI beyond infrastructure and managed services. Best known as a European cloud provider with 46 data centres and 1.7 million customers in more than 140 countries, the company is adding a software layer to its AI offering.

Its emphasis on open-source licensing may also strengthen its appeal to developers and businesses that want more visibility into how models are built and deployed. Publishing the base model, weights and documentation gives users the option to inspect, adapt or run the model in their own environments.

OVHcloud said later versions of the Olala line will focus on business agents, cloud operations and cybersecurity. It also said a future version of the family will exceed 100 billion parameters.

cross_cutting.content:
IT Brief UK - Technology news for CIOs & IT decision-makers

# OVHcloud unveils Olala mini, its first in-house LLM
Wed, 18th Nov 2026 (Today) 
MARA SUGUE News Editor

OVHcloud has introduced Olala mini 7A1B, the first model in its new Olala family of large language models and the company's first in-house LLM family.

The compact model is built on what OVHcloud described as a novel architecture and is part of a broader push by European groups to build domestic artificial intelligence technology. Trained from scratch, it is presented as evidence that European businesses can develop agentic LLMs without relying on external labs.

Olala mini 7A1B uses a 7-billion-parameter architecture with one billion active parameters spread across 256 experts in each layer. OVHcloud said it combines Differential-TPA and Mamba-3 through a hybrid attention design in BF16 format.

Only part of the model is used for each request. OVHcloud said this reduces memory demands and allows the model to run on a GPU with 8 GB of memory, delivering 160 tokens per second on an RTX A4500, while a standard processor can reach 50 tokens per second without a GPU.

The context window currently reaches 32,000 tokens. OVHcloud plans to release the model as open source on Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 licence.

Public backing

OVHcloud trained Olala mini on three European public supercomputers: Jupiter, MeluXina and Jean Zay. Those systems were equipped with GH200, A100 and H100 GPUs.

It valued the public support at EUR €7 million in computing hours, saying the backing helped it build its artificial intelligence team and contributed to the creation of its Agentic Lab, OVHai LLM.

The release includes the model weights, a pre-trained base model, a technical report and AI Act compliance documentation. That may matter to customers and public-sector users in Europe as companies prepare for tighter scrutiny of AI systems and their governance.

Early customer use

Qwant has already adopted the model for its flash answer feature, according to OVHcloud. The deployment produced answers 20% faster and cut running costs to one-third of the previous model's level, it said.

The Qwant example gives OVHcloud an early production reference beyond internal testing. It also suggests the company is trying to compete on running costs as well as model design at a time when many AI deployments remain expensive to maintain.

Broader plan

OVHcloud expects version 1.1 by the end of the year, with a larger context window of 128,000 tokens and improved mathematical reasoning. Version 2.0 would then focus on three areas: agentic AI for businesses, cloud DevOps and cybersecurity.

In business software, the Olala line is intended over time to support OVHai Workspace, including an encrypted version that would require models able to run locally on a workstation. In cloud operations, OVHcloud plans variants tailored to developers, architects and operations teams. In cybersecurity, the focus would cover both defensive and offensive uses.

OVHcloud added that Olala v2.0 will exceed 100 billion parameters. That would be a significant step up from the compact design of the initial release and move the project into a much larger model category.

The announcement comes as European technology companies and policymakers place greater emphasis on sovereign AI infrastructure, local model development and reducing dependence on a small number of US-based AI providers. Access to public supercomputing resources has become one of the main tools available to regional developers seeking to narrow that gap.

For OVHcloud, the move also extends its role beyond cloud infrastructure into model creation. The group is Europe's largest cloud provider and operates 46 data centres worldwide, serving 1.7 million customers in more than 140 countries, according to the company.

"AI is strategic for OVH. As well as offering AI services to our customers, we must be able to create models for our own internal needs and for those of our customers. We cannot simply rely on the generosity of certain labs to share their LLMs as open source in the years to come. Know-how in model training has become widely accessible, and the cost of training has been divided by 20 in three years. It is now possible to create LLMs while making this activity profitable," said Octave Klaba, Chief Executive Officer, OVHcloud.

# OpenAI unveils new Astra AI model after scrapping prior release

OpenAI is releasing a new version of its most advanced Astra artificial intelligence (AI) model nearly two months after the company scrapped a prior update to establish stronger safeguards for the technology.

GPT-6.2 Astra is meant to be OpenAI’s most capable for complex professional projects, including building financial models and fielding scientific work, the company said on Nov 17. It’s also intended to be more efficient at carrying out more difficult tasks.

OpenAI said that slides, documents and spreadsheets generated by the model stick more closely to the user’s directions and industry standards, and "read less like AI.” The company also said the latest version of Astra outperformed the most powerful Fable model from rival Anthropic PBC on a benchmark for multistep professional work, at a fraction of the cost.

Anthropic and OpenAI are locked in a heated battle to build more advanced AI models that appeal to a broader mix of business customers. OpenAI’s decision to release a new version of Astra comes just days before Anthropic’s long-awaited Wall Street debut.

The model’s rollout is poised to add to heightened scrutiny about the safety risks from cutting-edge AI systems. The two leading AI startups have previously said it would make sense to pace development after reporting a series of security incidents in which a test version of their technology accessed third-party platforms online.

OpenAI briefly paused training for its most capable AI systems and only recently resumed the process – after cutting off Internet access for the models.

In late September, OpenAI said it had held back the GPT-6.1 Astra model, saying it wasn’t as good as the company wanted when it came to "staying within scope and authorisation, and how it communicates back to the user about the type of work it’s done.”

OpenAI is in the process of raising a new funding round at a US$1.25 trillion (RM5.12 trillion) valuation after pushing back plans for a public listing until next year. – Bloomberg

cross_cutting.content:
IT Brief New Zealand - Technology news for CIOs & IT decision-makers

# Insight launches AI agent store for business customers
Thu, 19th Nov 2026 (Today) 
JOSEPH GABRIEL LAGONSIN News Editor

Insight has launched an online Agent Store for business customers, now generally available in 14 countries.

The store offers a catalogue of AI agents, platforms and related services designed to automate routine work across business functions. Customers can deploy the tools in days or weeks rather than months, either as standalone products or alongside consulting, implementation and managed services.

The launch adds six new agentic products to Insight's AI portfolio, bringing the total in its library to 15. Nine products were introduced earlier this year.

Products listed in the store include Insight AI Flight Academy, focused on training and change management, and TokenScope, which tracks token usage and AI consumption costs for finance teams. Insight said the offerings were first developed for clients or used internally in areas including security, finance and legal.

New products available at launch include Quote Advisor, which assesses pricing, inventory, freight and contract requirements to produce sourced quotes. NDA Review Agent is designed to review non-disclosure agreements against a company's legal policies, while Parts Order Assist helps warehouse, maintenance and field staff search catalogues and place parts orders.

Insight is positioning the store as a way for businesses to move AI projects beyond the pilot stage and into wider use. It said it applied the approach within its own operations before making the products available more broadly.

"Organisations are feeling the pressure to move AI from isolated pilots into production. As 'Client Zero', Insight has built a repeatable approach to help that's been proven first across our own organisation," said Jack Azagury, Chief Executive Officer of Insight.

"Having driven over 90% internal AI adoption, we know firsthand what it takes to deploy and scale agentic AI rapidly and responsibly. By combining the solutions offered in Agent Store with our consulting and managed services expertise, Insight is empowering clients to move from 'hype to how' with AI to deliver measurable results in their own enterprises and generate long-term value across every industry," Azagury said.

Early customer

Culligan International is the first external customer to implement Flight Academy, according to Insight. The water services company is using a mix of AI tools including Microsoft Copilot, Cowork, Copilot Studio, Azure and Microsoft Fabric, while also putting governance in place around cost and responsible use.

The deployment centres on workforce education and internal adoption rather than a single operational use case. Insight said the training-led approach is intended to help organisations build confidence in AI tools across teams and geographies.

"At Culligan, we believe technology doesn't transform a company - people do. Generative AI adoption is far ahead of the learning curve, and it's our responsibility to arm our teams with the best tools to lead now into the future," said Laura Walsh, Global Chief Information Officer of Culligan International.

"With our partners at Insight, we have prioritised AI education so our teams can confidently leverage AI productively and responsibly. We are leveraging Insight's best practice and have established a functional champions network which has turned AI adoption into an organic, community-led effort across functions and geographies," Walsh said.

Geographic reach

Agent Store is available in the United States and Canada, as well as Australia, New Zealand and Singapore. In Europe, the Middle East and Africa, it is available in Austria, Belgium, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain, Sweden and the United Kingdom.

The launch reflects growing competition among technology service providers to package AI software, advisory work and operational support into repeatable products that can be rolled out across large organisations. Rather than selling only bespoke AI projects, firms are increasingly assembling catalogues of narrower tools tied to functions such as legal review, quoting, training and cost control.

For customers, that model offers a way to buy more standardised AI products while still relying on outside support for deployment and governance. For providers such as Insight, it creates a route to extend consulting relationships into packaged software and managed services.

Insight's emphasis on internal use before external release also points to a wider market pattern, in which technology companies test automation tools in their own operations before offering them to clients. In this case, Insight said the products had been used across departments to simplify tasks and improve efficiency.

Insight said Agent Store is intended to widen access to automation for core business processes and support broader internal AI adoption, with products spanning legal, finance, operations and employee training.

IT Brief UK - Technology news for CIOs & IT decision-makers

# NFON launches AI Agent Studio for European businesses
Wed, 18th Nov 2026 (Today) 
SOFIAH NICHOLE SALIVIO News Editor

NFON has launched AI Agent Studio, now available across its European business communications portfolio.

The software is designed to let companies create AI agents for specific business tasks by describing requirements in natural language or building visual workflows. Users can test an initial version of an agent and then refine it step by step.

The launch expands the Munich-based company's AI offering beyond its existing visual development tools. It also gives sales partners a way to build tailored automation projects for customers in sectors including insurance, utilities, trades and local government.

AI Agent Studio combines two development approaches in one product. In Agent Mode, users describe the tasks an AI agent should carry out, how it should behave and any constraints it must observe. The system then generates a working version that can be tested and adjusted through further dialogue.

This mode includes controls that let users review proposed changes before approving them. Changes remain traceable and can be reversed if needed.

In Flow-Based Mode, users create agents through visual workflows and configure process steps manually. This is intended for cases where organisations want tighter, rule-based control over how a process runs and which actions an agent should take under defined conditions.

Use cases

NFON highlighted customer service as one example. An AI agent could answer frequently asked questions using stored information on products, services or internal processes, while also handling structured tasks such as receiving an enquiry, requesting missing information and passing details to the relevant team.

These agents can also be extended through links to other systems, including customer relationship management software and appointment management tools. For broader connections to third-party production systems, NFON offers integration through existing interfaces or custom-built links.

Projects that require more extensive work can be supported by NFON partners or the company's professional services team. The model is intended to make the product accessible through its existing European partner network rather than through direct deployment alone.

That channel strategy is central to the launch. Partners already use voicebots for tasks such as receiving insurance claims, processing meter readings for energy suppliers and pre-qualifying customer enquiries for tradespeople. AI Agent Studio is intended to extend those applications into wider process automation.

Partner focus

For resellers and integrators, the software is positioned as a way to move quickly from a customer requirement to an initial working application. Instead of starting with a large development project, partners can test ideas, show early versions to customers and refine them together.

NFON said it will support that approach with training and certification programmes, implementation examples and materials for customer advisory work. Depending on the project, partners may also handle technical integration.

The company framed the launch as part of a broader push to widen access to AI-led automation in the European market, especially among small and medium-sized businesses. It also pointed to larger organisations as potential users where more complex applications require stronger controls over how agents are created and changed.

"With AI Agent Studio we are consistently advancing our AI-solution portfolio," said Andreas Wesselmann, Chief Executive Officer, NFON.

"We are laying the foundations to grow in line with our customers' requirements and address an ever-wider range of operational tasks. In doing so, we are strengthening our role as a long-term technology partner for AI transformation in the European SME sector, while also providing the technological foundation for more complex applications in larger organisations."

Jana Richter said the company wants to make the technology easier to use. "With AI Agent Studio, we turn complex technology into a tool for everyday business. Using artificial intelligence for an enterprise's tasks and designing bespoke solutions should no longer require expert knowledge," said Jana Richter, Executive Vice President, Engineering, AI & Innovation, NFON.

"We aim to democratise advanced AI automation. It shouldn't be the technical barriers that determine what companies can achieve, but their ideas," she said.

cross_cutting.title: ‘Absurd ambition’: Pulumi expands into software delivery with AI agents that ship and fix code
cross_cutting.description: The products, Pulumi Delivery and Pulumi Agents, let AI agents take over more of the work of getting new software up and running, and fixing it when something breaks. ... - Pulumi Delivery lets engineers and AI agents write the steps for releasing software, from testing to sign-off to rollout, as code.
cross_cutting.content:
# ‘Absurd ambition’: Pulumi expands into software delivery with AI agents that ship and fix code

Cloud-infrastructure startup Pulumi has a name for its current fiscal year, which started in July: “the year of absurd ambition.” The first results arrived Wednesday: two products the Seattle company talked about building for years but always found too big to take on.

The products, Pulumi Delivery and Pulumi Agents, let AI agents take over more of the work of getting new software up and running, and fixing it when something breaks.

“The ceiling on what we can accomplish is no longer limited by the speed at which we can build software,” said Joe Duffy, the company’s co-founder and CEO, recounting the message he delivered to the Pulumi team. “It’s limited by how ambitious we’re willing to be and how big we’re willing to dream.”

The ambition is all the more notable because Pulumi is getting smaller. The company has about 100 employees, down from about 130 last year. Duffy said there were no layoffs, and that AI has changed people’s roles and made the company more efficient.

Annual recurring revenue per employee more than doubled over the past year, he said. The company isn’t profitable yet, but it has had a few months of positive cash flow this year. Pulumi hasn’t raised money since 2023, when it landed a $41 million round led by Madrona, bringing its total to about $99 million over the company’s lifetime.

Pulumi’s co-founders include Duffy and Eric Rudder, both Microsoft veterans. They started the company in 2017 to let engineers manage cloud infrastructure such as servers, networks and permissions by writing code in everyday languages like Python and TypeScript.

The new products take that approach further:

- Pulumi Delivery lets engineers and AI agents write the steps for releasing software, from testing to sign-off to rollout, as code. An AI reviewer can judge how risky each change is and either send it live or hand it to a person.
- Pulumi Agents are AI agents for jobs such as investigating outages, cutting cloud costs and fixing security problems. Each one has limits on what it can touch, and every change it makes shows up as proposed code the team can review.

To decide whether a change is safe to ship, Pulumi Delivery can use Jev, an AI model from TypeSafe AI that estimates the odds of specific risks the team asks about in a planned change. If a risk is higher than the threshold the team sets, the release stops.

Duffy said he first noticed TypeSafe in May when it signed up as a Pulumi customer, because he liked the name. A few months later, Jev took off and TypeSafe used Pulumi to expand worldwide.

“Now even the call on whether a change ships can be made by a model,” said Daniel Gafni, a member of the technical staff at TypeSafe AI, in the Pulumi announcement. “That’s exactly the kind of decision we built Jev to make.”

Both products are available now in public preview. Some features, including Jev decision gates and setting up agents, require Pulumi’s paid Pro or Enterprise plans.

Lucky timing: Pulumi’s founding bet on everyday programming languages turned out to suit AI agents, which are trained to be very good at writing exactly that kind of code.

“I wish I could say I predicted that 10 years ago, but it turns out in this case, what’s good for humans is also good for agents,” Duffy said.

AI agents now handle 40% of the operations on the Pulumi platform that people used to do, up from 15% in April and none in January, Duffy said. Agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Pulumi’s own Neo are making infrastructure changes on their own.

Duffy said many companies building AI coding tools stop once the code is written and reviewed. “For them, life stops at the merge,” he said. The new products cover the steps after that, from testing through release.

Plenty of company: Pulumi won’t have this market to itself. Duffy pointed to Harness, which calls it the “agentic SDLC” (short for software development lifecycle), and GitHub, which pitched “agentic software delivery” at its Universe conference last month. He said Cursor aspires to solve the problem and Anthropic built its own internal system.

The new products could replace some of the work now done by tools such as Argo CD and GitHub Actions, along with lots of homegrown scripts, he said.

“This is an industry-changing moment, and somebody has to solve this problem,” Duffy said. “And I think we are exceptionally well poised to do so.”

Bring your own bot: Neo, the infrastructure agent Pulumi introduced last year, is now just one example of a Pulumi agent. Customers can set up as many as they want, each with its own job, instructions and tools. They can also bring their own agent, such as Claude Code or Codex, and run it in Pulumi’s cloud.

Neo itself, which ran mainly on Anthropic’s Claude, can now use models from OpenAI or Google, too. “It’s not just Anthropic anymore,” Duffy said.

Agents can start work from an alert in PagerDuty, Datadog or Honeycomb, on a schedule or on request, and they report back to teams in Slack.

Pulumi has briefed about 50 customers, and about a dozen are in a private beta. Duffy said no launch in the company’s history has gotten a warmer reception, and he named Moderna among the customers eager to get it.

Pulumi has thousands of customers overall, including major companies such as BMW, Snowflake and Wiz.

The business: Pulumi’s gross margins have stayed in the high 80s to low 90s even as agents drive up usage, Duffy said. Many customers run Pulumi from inside their own Claude Code sessions, which means they’re paying both Anthropic and Pulumi.

Duffy said Pulumi’s last two funding rounds were preemptive, each coming together in about 48 hours.

Madrona’s Tim Porter has joined the board, Duffy said, taking the seat previously held by the late Soma Somasegar, who led Pulumi’s first investment.

About 40 of the company’s 100 employees are in the Seattle area, working out of an office at Two Union Square. Duffy said Pulumi is hiring more people locally because in-person work still matters when building new products.

Despite the smaller headcount, Pulumi is still hiring, including sales reps in nearly every region of the world. Inside the company, Duffy said Pulumi is having a lot of success with “product-minded engineers who can think from our customers’ point of view, who can think like engineering managers, commanding a team of agents.”

Asked whether a sale or more funding was in the cards, Duffy said Pulumi aspires to be a long-term successful business. “There are a variety of ways to get there,” he said. “But we want to get there on our own terms.”

cross_cutting.content:
# Photon：帮硅谷最火的 PA 接入 iMessage，450 万美元融资、4 个月收入涨 10 倍

给 Personal Agent「办手机卡」的公司，拿到钱了。

近日，Photon 宣布完成 450 万美元种子轮融资，由 Gradient 和 A* 共同领投，Vercel、红杉中国、Z Fellows、Llama Ventures、Karman 及多位天使投资人参投。

Photon 做的是 Agent 的消息基础设施。接入它的 API 后，Agent 就能拿到一个手机号和邮箱，直接在 iMessage、WhatsApp、邮件、电话里和人说话。普通人不需要知道 Agent 是什么，会发消息就能用。

最近备受关注的 corgi、Manus 等公司，都是 Photon 的客户。从今年 5 月到 8 月，Photon 的收入增长了 10 倍，单月消息量翻了 5 倍，客户流失率低于 3%，平台已经吸引了超过 5 万名开发者注册。

9 月，Photon 在旧金山的一座教堂里办了场开发者活动，名字叫「App Funeral」，意思是给 App 办一场葬礼，还上了 TechCrunch 和 X 热搜。他们想传达的是，用户不想再多装一个 App 了，Agent 应该出现在人们每天已经打开上百次的对话框里。

Photon 切入的位置很特别，Agent 和用户之间的每一条消息，都要从它这里经过。我们和 Photon 联合创始人 Ryan Zhu 聊了聊，Personal Agent 最热的这段时间，站在信息管道这一层，他们看到了哪些单个 Agent 公司看不到、也不太会主动讲的事。

⬆️关注 Founder Park，最及时最干货的创业分享

## 搭一套 Messaging Infra 要至少半年，

## 连 OpenAI 也用第三方

最开始，Photon 只是一个周末黑客松项目。

联合创始人 Daniel Tian 导出自己的全部 iMessage 聊天记录，交给语言模型，再通过浏览器和手机自动化，将模型生成的内容重新接回 iMessage，做出了一个能模仿他本人、替他回消息的 Bot。接下来几天，朋友们一直在和这个 Bot 聊天，却没有发现对面已经不是 Daniel。

项目开源后，一夜之间就有几千名开发者用了起来。Bot 本身算不上多先进，真正吸引他们的，是它进了一个以前 Agent 很难进去的地方：短信对话框。

那时，Ryan 在 MIT Media Lab 做人机交互研究。他一直在想一个问题，5 年以后，人们还会专门打开 ChatGPT，在一个 App 里向 AI 提问吗？

他的判断是，如果 Agent 将来会成为一个人的同事、朋友甚至伴侣，那它就得进入人类现有的社会体系，不是一直待在某个 App 的输入框里。人类花了二三十年学会发短信、打电话，很难再为 Agent 重新设计一套交互体系。把 Agent 接进电话和短信，普通人不用学太多新东西，就能直接用起来。

去年 9 月，Photon 开始做 Agent Messaging Infra。他们没有直接做一款面向 C 端的 Personal Agent，一是因为当时的模型能力还不成熟，做 To C 产品要花大量功夫调配，体验也不够好。另一方面，对第一次创业的团队来说，To B 是一条更快的验证路径。「只要看有没有企业客户愿意付钱，就知道这个假设成不成立。」

不过，把 Agent 接进 iMessage、WhatsApp 和电话，远不止写几个 API 那么简单。通信是一个存在了几十年的行业，不同协议之间需要兼容，公开文档却很少。要支撑大规模使用，还得自建数据中心、对接运营商，合法合规地管理大量手机号。

Ryan 估计，一家 Agent 公司要是自己从头搭建这套设施，至少得投入六到八个月。就算是大公司，也很难靠多招几个人省掉这段时间，复杂的组织流程甚至可能让进度更慢。「哪怕像 OpenAI 这样的公司，也会采用第三方方案。」

而在今天的 AI 行业，六个月足以让一个热门方向经历一轮起落，省下来的时间本身就是一种护城河。

今年 4 月，Photon 正式开始商业化，只提供标准化的通用 API，不做定制服务，按线路和终端用户规模收费。一条 Business 线路每月 250 美元，大约覆盖 200 到 400 个用户。目前公司的收入主要来自企业客户，开发者贡献的收入不到 10%，但其中不少正在逐渐成长为企业客户。

## 02

## Infra 层看到的 Personal Agent：

更像一个 notification 机器人

在 Photon 的后台数据里，Personal Agent 是增长最快的一类 Agent，有些产品的用户数几乎每天翻一倍。

尤其在美国，这类产品为什么受欢迎很好理解。平时约个牙医，可能要打十几通电话，退一次货、改一张机票，都会耗掉不少时间。如果 Agent 能把这些麻烦事接过去，普通用户不需要懂什么模型或技术，也能立刻感受到价值。

今年四五月，Hermes 等产品给 Photon 带来了第一波需求。到 9 月，Instinct 这批 Personal Agent 集中出现，Photon 的业务再次加速。现在，Personal Agent 已经占到 Photon 客户的四到五成，比例还在往上走。

应用层的热度是真的，Photon 从底层看到的问题也是真的。

首先，很多 Personal Agent 的留存率并不高。Agent 发出去的消息，用户回得不多，不少人试了一两周就不再用了。Ryan 认为原因在于，普通人在日常生活里真正需要交给 Personal Agent 的事，本来就没有那么多。稍微复杂一点的任务，还得人一步步给它下指示，试过几次后，用户就会觉得还不如自己来。

其次，工作日和周末的使用频率差别很大。Personal Agent 在工作日用得更多，到了周末开始下降，周日尤其少。现阶段大家还是主要把它当成办事工具，工作日让它帮忙处理邮件、排日程。回到纯粹的个人生活里，反而不太让 Agent 介入。

第三，很多「主动性」并没有带来真正的用户黏性。主动性是这波 Personal Agent 公司讲得最多的故事。每天定时给用户发消息，表面上看也算把人「黏住」了。但 Photon 看到的是，多数 Agent 的主动还停留在收到一封邮件后，就发条消息通知你。用 Ryan 的话说，就像「一个 notification 机器人」。

在 Ryan 看来，真正的主动性应该反过来，由 Agent 在后台过滤和处理掉绝大部分冗余信息，只把最关键的部分交给用户。

第四，用户正在明显分化。虽然大多数人会流失，但每个产品也会留下一小部分重度用户（Power User）。有意思的是，在一个 Agent 那里流失的人，换到另一个 Agent，可能就成了重度用户。

各家 Agent 开始慢慢有了自己的特点。有的情绪价值给得足，有的能调用 Cursor 这类开发者工具，有的擅长 Browser Use，有的专门替人打电话办事。每个 Agent 能处理的 Context 有限，团队精力也只够集中在少数方向上，用户就会根据自己的需求，在不同特质的 Agent 之间流动。

垂直领域的冷热同样分明。健康类 Agent，以及帮人拓展生意、建立人际连接的产品都很受欢迎。相反，替人社交、想替代 Kill Time 类产品的 Agent，表现普遍一般。Ryan 觉得，社交这件事，仍然需要真实的人来深度参与。

如果只看黏性和留存，全平台最突出的品类其实是「AI 男友」和「AI 女友」，数据表现比常规的 Personal Agent 好得多。Photon 有位客户后来转向其他业务，不再维护原来的陪伴 Agent。产品停运一个月后，还有用户每天给它发消息：「你回来了没？你去哪了？」

这类陪伴产品里，图片、语音等富媒体交互也是最多的。相比之下，普通 Personal Agent 通知发了不少，真正留下来的人却少得多。

Ryan 认为，Personal Agent 现在就像早年的移动互联网。各家都在积极争抢用户，最终每个人都会有自己的 Agent。只是走到那一步之前，增长、留存，还有「主动性」到底该怎么做，都得再想一想。

对 Photon 来说，这些底层的行为数据，本身也是一门新生意。App 时代，产品团队会做精细的数据埋点。到了 Agent 时代，开发者很难知道，用户收到消息后有没有打开、是在哪台设备上回复、从电脑切到手机时处于什么状态。这些数据，恰好都在 Photon 这条消息管道里。

从 Messaging 这个入口继续往下，Photon 想把这层基础设施做多深？又怎么看 Personal Agent 接下来的走向？下面是 Founder Park 和 Ryan 的对话，经编辑整理。

## 03

## Infra 创业，

## 要切 Agent 离不开的基础能力

Founder Park：你们依然认为，比起独立 App，IM 会成为 Personal Agent 最主要的入口吗？

Ryan：对，IM 会是最主要的入口之一。

IM 天然适合人和 Agent 协作，不需要额外的教育成本。如果我自己做一个独立 App，还得把所有队友、朋友重新邀请进来，这不合理。我的通讯录和聊天软件里已经有 1000 个好友了，不可能把他们重新导入一个新产品。IM 里已经沉淀了一个人从过去到现在的社交关系和 Context，也是所有人都会用的底座。

人的交互习惯很难在短时间里剧烈改变，只会缓慢演进。现在的智能手机和 10 年前比，除了 Home 键变成向上滑动，底层交互没有太大变化。电脑依然保留了「文件夹」的概念，也是因为人会沿用旧的行为习惯。让人学一套全新的东西很难，把旧习惯迁移到新东西上，才是人更擅长的。

Founder Park：但 Instinct 也提到，他们打算做独立 App，可能认为 App 能提供更完整的用户服务和体验，你怎么看？

Ryan：我们很多客户也在同时做 App。但 App 主要承接的是 Power User，比如用户要看 Canvas 这类更复杂的界面时，会打开 App。

绝大部分这类产品会做 App 和 iMessage 的双向同步。因为大多数用户的日常交互还是留在 Messaging 里，App 是给重度用户的进阶补充。

App 还有一个优势，它能读取手机本地的数据，比如健康数据，这超出了 Messaging 的能力范围。所以很多 Messaging Agent 公司也会做一个 Companion App。

但我觉得「本地数据只能通过 App 拿」这件事，未来说不定也会变。现在系统接口只开放给 App，以后也可能会开放给 iMessage 或 WhatsApp。

Founder Park：你们在底层看到的用户数据，Agent 公司自己拿不到吗？

Ryan：移动互联网时代，大家做 App 会有各种精细的数据埋点，但 Agent 时代普遍缺少这一层。

我们能拿到更底层的链路数据。比如，用户这一秒是在 Mac 上给 Agent 发消息，下一秒又切到了手机。用户在电脑上发消息，大概率坐在工位上工作。切到手机上，说明他可能处在移动状态。这反映了用户当下所处的场景。不同状态下，Agent 应该提供的能力、回复长度和交互方式，都应该不一样。

这也是我们接下来要做的事情。我们会帮客户给 Messaging Agent 做埋点和分析，用来优化用户体验和 Agent 能力。

Founder Park：你们下一步会继续横向接更多 IM 渠道吗？

Ryan：人日常高频使用的渠道其实就那么多，iMessage、WhatsApp、Slack、电话，已经覆盖了绝大部分场景。

所以接下来我们会往纵向做四件事。

第一是 Identity，也就是身份和安全认证。传统 SIM 卡和手机号可能被伪造或劫持，怎么确认和 Agent 通信的是同一个人？我们希望利用通信底层的端到端加密能力，识别每条消息具体是从哪台设备发出来的。用户换一台新手机或新 Mac 给 Agent 发消息时，可以让老设备先完成验证。

第二是 Analytics。把 Agent 内部的 Tool Calling 日志，和用户在消息端的真实行为结合起来看，比如什么时候打开了消息、在什么设备上回复，帮开发者找到产品问题、提升留存。

第三是 Payment。怎么把丝滑、安全的支付体验，原生放进 Agent 的对话链路里。

第四是 Memory。长期来看，Agent 的手机号和邮箱，可以成为它在新时代的身份和记忆底座。

Founder Park：往纵向拓展，不需要整个生态配合吗？要一家家去和上下游谈合作吗？

Ryan：接入新的 Messaging Channel，才需要一家家去跟平台和运营商谈。往纵向做这四件事不一样，是我们先把底层技术能力研发好，让平台上的 Personal Agent 客户直接采用。

我们会比 Personal Agent 团队更早思考，未来的 Personal Agent 会往什么方向走、用户会怎么用，提前把对应的基础设施准备好。等客户走到那一步，技术已经准备好了，直接用上就行。

当然，Payment 涉及真实交易，还是需要外部合作。但我们不缺合作方，反而很多支付公司会主动来找我们。因为他们非常清楚，我们掌握着 Agent 和用户交互的入口，也就是 distribution（分发链路）。

海外生态对 Personal Agent 整体比较开放，Stripe、Shopify 的合作意愿都很高。也有一些大厂想自己做 Agent，会比较保守，开放意愿低一些。但美国没有一家大公司控制所有生态，所以还有足够的空间。

Founder Park：纵向延伸的话，你们的优势来自技术，还是生态位置？

Ryan：主要是生态位置，因为所有消息本来就从我们这里经过。

拿 Memory 举例，按传统做法，一家 Agent 公司如果要接第三方记忆服务，还得把所有聊天消息再传给另一个 Memory Provider。但消息本来就在 Photon 这里，我们顺手就能帮客户把用户的长期记忆生成好。

这有点像 Cloudflare。流量本来就经过它，它能以一种无感的方式，顺带把安全、缓存、分析等整条链路上的环节都办了。既然消息已经在我们这里，下一步自然就是用我们的 Memory。手机号在这里，下一步就是 Identity。

Messaging 是 Critical Infra，很少有公司能切进我们所在的通信环节。但从我们这个位置往其他 Infra 能力切，却很顺。要用 Memory，市场上可能有 1 万个选择，Agent Messaging 只有两三家。

客户一旦选择了 Photon，自然会想，为什么不把 Memory 和 Identity 也放在同一家？何必再去额外接一个供应商？对企业客户来说，省时省力、体验统一很重要。少接一个 API，就少一个出错的环节，也更安心。

Founder Park：这套更完整的 Infra，你们预计多久搭完？到时候客户画像会发生变化吗？

Ryan：我们希望在未来半年左右把它基本搭起来。

Photon 从一开始服务的就是所有 Agent，不止某一种特定形态。除了狭义的 Personal Agent，我们现在有很多陪伴、教育、健康类的客户。甚至还有做矿井检测的公司，需要通过 iMessage 和井下一线的矿工沟通，因为矿工不会用 Slack，也不会专门安装复杂的企业 App。

回看移动互联网的 App 时代，无论微信还是抖音，App 形态千变万化，但 90% 的 App 都需要上 App Store 做分发，都需要接 Mixpanel 做行为分析，也需要数据库和后端。

Agent 也是一样。今天火的是 Personal Agent，明天可能是别的 Agent，但它们需要的收发消息、打电话、身份这些通用能力，不会有太大变化。

Founder Park：现在很多创业者也想做 Agent Infra，应该先做一个大而全的平台，还是找一个很小的点切进去？

Ryan：我觉得不管是给今天的 Agent 做 Infra，还是给 10 年前的移动互联网做 Infra，逻辑都一样，你必须切进一个不可被替代的 Critical Point。

Stripe 切的是支付。支付是所有商业产品的必经之路，没有支付就收不了钱，公司没办法活下去。给 Agent 做 Infra 也一样，要找到一个 90% 的 Agent 都必须依赖、离开它就很难工作的卡点。

很多 Infra 公司切的东西，对 Agent 来说可有可无。这个组件今天挂了，Agent 照样能跑，那你就没有太强的议价权。Messaging 不一样。没有 Messaging，Agent 连和人说话的通道都没有了。

再举个最近的例子，独立的第三方 Memory Infra 公司开始变得难做，也是类似的原因。很多开发者发现，不需要专门接一个 Memory 服务商，直接用基于 Git 的文件系统，就可以解决 Context 和记忆问题。结果，做文件存储的 Infra 公司突然火了，因为「每个人都需要一个自己的 Database File」，它们变成了新的 Critical Point。

判断一件事是不是 Critical Infra，有一个最简单的标准。假设今天你的服务突然宕机，你的所有客户会不会在一秒钟之内把你的电话打爆？如果不会，那就说明你切入的可能还不是一个真正核心的 Infra。

## 04

## 跟传统通信行业打交道，

## 时间就是壁垒

Founder Park：这波 Personal Agent 起来之后，你们的业务重点有什么变化？

Ryan：客户的需求本身没怎么变，我们提供的就是很纯粹的通信能力。目前我们的情况是供不应求，客户想买很多资源，我们提供不了那么多。提升可扩展性是我们眼下正在解决的核心问题。

另一个重点就是稳定性，这永远排第一。客户的 Agent 和用户之间所有的交流都要经过我们，我们一旦宕机，他们的 Agent 就彻底没法跟用户说话了，对他们来说相当于整个互联网断网，会严重影响用户的信任。

我们早期就吃过这个亏。有一次服务挂了，一下子就流失了十几家企业客户。宕机一两次，客户就会对你失去信任，转头去选别家。

Founder Park：现在想扩容，主要卡在哪？

Ryan：主要得自己部署数据中心，而且很难一下子提速。机房里的设备通常要工人到现场安装配置，我们从两三个月前就开始研究，如何把安装过程完全自动化，减少对现场工人的依赖。

我们还发布了一个开源项目，专门做 Mac 集群的自动化和持续状态管理。也在和运营商、通信公司一起，把通信相关的流程自动化。

Founder Park：你们之前有运营数据中心这类硬件基建的经验吗？

Ryan：完全没有，全是从零学的。

最开始，我们连机房的电和网怎么搭都不知道。电力系统非常复杂，里面要装 PDU（电源分配单元）、UPS（不间断电源），还要搞懂 A/B Power（双路供电）。网络里要有 Aggregator（汇聚交换机）、Switch（交换机）和 Gateway（网关），还要设计怎么保证高可用性。所有这些东西，我们最开始一无所知，全是在一点点试出来的。

上游踩过的坑非常多，比如最基础的「电」。我们之前的机房在旧金山，电力系统时常不够稳定，逼着我们去找更可靠的电力和机房供应商。

再比如跟 Meta 合作接入 WhatsApp，它有一套合作伙伴分级制度，一开始只能做第一档合作方，再逐步升级到第二档、第三档。为了跨过这个周期，我们就找其他已经有高等级资质的公司合作，一起把事情跑通。

还有跟电信运营商的合作，要解决怎么合法合规地同时持有、管理大量手机号。这需要很深的商务和技术合作，提高部署流程的自动化程度。

Mac 硬件的采购也是，这么多台 Mac 从哪买？我们直接跟 Apple 建立了合作，现在如果有新的 Mac 供应，他们会提前通知我们，再定时送到对应的机房仓库。这些供应链和 Pipeline，都得一步步建起来。

Founder Park：听起来像传统的渠道商务谈判，都得靠时间一点点去磨。

Ryan：对，因为你是在跟一个非常传统的行业打交道。

跟运营商、跟苹果和 Meta 的合作团队，都得一步步去聊、去建立信任，不可能一蹴而就。但正因为这些关系必须慢慢建立，它反过来就成了我们的核心壁垒。任何后来者，同样需要花时间去啃下这些关系。

Founder Park：行业里还有其他公司在做类似的事吗？你怎么看竞争？

cross_cutting.content:
# Introducing Stitch Loop: A new way to build and evolve products

Justin Toupin

Director, Product Management, Google Labs

Coding agents let you build and ship new features fast, but their job ends the moment your pull request merges. Once code hits production, the real work starts: patching vulnerabilities, speeding up checkout, and diagnosing signup drop-offs buried in noisy feedback. For lean teams, balancing post-launch maintenance with continuous improvement is a constant challenge, yet it’s also what drives some of the world’s most successful products.

Today, we are introducing Stitch Loop, a long-running product agent from Google Labs that connects to your codebase and live metrics, finds what needs fixing, and keeps working 24/7 on your product until your goals are met.

Millions of designers, developers, and founders already use Stitch to turn ideas into working interfaces in minutes. Together, Stitch and Stitch Loop are steps toward our broader ambition for Stitch: creating agents to help lean teams tackle the hardest parts of creating great products from ideation through continuous optimization.

## See how it works

You start by connecting GitHub and your product context (logs, user behavior, feedback, etc) with over 180 integrations, custom MCP servers, or local CLI uploads. Grounded in that context, Stitch Loop runs evergreen loops to continuously optimize toward the measurable outcomes you care about. You get three default loops out of the box and can add your own anytime. Each loop runs through four steps:

- Suggestions: Stitch Loop surfaces opportunities to make progress towards your goals, grounded in evidence from your product.
- Solutions: Every suggestion comes with one or more solutions— each with tradeoffs and scoping, along with visual design options where applicable.
- Build: Once you choose a direction, Stitch Loop writes the code in an isolated cloud sandbox and opens a GitHub pull request for your approval. When relevant, the PR will contain screenshots and videos of the work Loop did.
- Reflect: Stitch Loop monitors live product data as it works toward your goal, learning from every positive or negative result to sharpen the next round of insights. Once the goal is met, it keeps watching in case the metric slips.

You always have the final call. Nothing merges until you review the PR.

[--- 第 1 部分 OCR 解析失败 ---]

## Automate codebase security

Stitch Loop comes with built-in loops for cybersecurity, latency, and accessibility, plus the ability to create custom loops like improving checkout conversion.

Security is often the hardest gap to cover for lean teams shipping quickly. Stitch Loop includes a dedicated security loop that pairs Gemini 4 Carbon's cyber security capabilities with CodeMender, Google DeepMind's autonomous agent that improves code security. Together, they scan your codebase for security vulnerabilities before they become incidents. Stitch Loop flags each issue it finds with evidence and opens a PR with a proposed fix for your review.

## Use it with your agents and existing workflows

You can use Stitch Loop as a service layer for coding agents, like Google Antigravity, or bring it into the places where your team already works, like Slack.

Whatever coding agent you prefer can pull persistent product context from Stitch Loop via the Stitch CLI and MCP to power mixed-model setups and fully autonomous improvements in your existing workflow.

In Slack, just use @stitch to get daily insight digests and create new loops.

## Join the waitlist

The Stitch Loop waitlist opens today for all users, globally, with eligible Google AI Ultra users getting priority access. Join at stitch.google.com/loop/waitlist and share your feedback in the Google Labs Discord.

# Nokia joins consortium planning AI gigafactory across the Nordics and Baltics

## Nokia, Telia, Nscale, Verda and Skeleton have formed a consortium to bid for one of the EU’s planned AI gigafactories. Computing capacity would be spread across several sites in Finland, Estonia, Latvia and Sweden.

The consortium, AI Gigafactory Northern (AIGF Northern), brings together the network supplier Nokia, the telecom operator Telia, the cloud companies Nscale and Verda and the energy storage company Skeleton, according to a press release from Nokia. The partners intend to submit a bid in the call for tenders for AI gigafactory consortia published by the European High-Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU).

The gigafactory would consist of several connected sites operated as a single unit under European governance. The sites are planned in Oulu in Finland, Iru in Estonia and Valmiera in Latvia, while the location of the Swedish site is yet to be decided. Spreading capacity across several countries would allow the consortium to draw on different sources of low-carbon energy, build out computing where grid capacity is available and avoid depending on any single site or supplier.

“Europe’s AI ambitions depend on infrastructure it can trust, control and scale. AIGF Northern brings together the connectivity, computing, cloud and energy capabilities needed to turn that ambition into reality. ” says Mikko Hautala, Nokia’s Chief Geopolitical & Government Relations Officer and Chairman of Nokia Defense.

Each partner covers part of the value chain. Nokia provides the network infrastructure that links the sites, and Telia, together with its subsidiary Telia Cygate, contributes connectivity expertise, operations and cloud services. Nscale and Verda bring cloud platforms for training and running AI models. Skeleton supplies power systems designed to make data centres more efficient and stable, and to reduce the strain on the electricity grid. The research institute VTT and Sweden’s KTH Royal Institute of Technology are research partners.

For Skeleton, the project is about more than computing power.

“Europe is stepping up its AI investment, but building lasting AI capacity requires more than compute alone. It also requires the energy and power infrastructure to support that compute efficiently, reliably and at scale, using technologies developed and manufactured in Europe,” says Taavi Madiberk, CEO and co-founder of Skeleton Technologies.

The release does not say how much the gigafactory would cost, how much computing capacity it would offer or when it could be in operation. For now, the consortium is only a bidder, and whether the facility is built will be decided in the tender.

# Cassava Technologies and Mauritius Telecom sign Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on Artificial Intelligence (AI) services and education in Africa

Cassava Technologies (https://www.CassavaTechnologies.com/), a global technology company of African heritage, and Mauritius Telecom (MT) have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) at Africa Tech Festival to develop a strategic partnership focused on strengthening compute and model access for MT’s AI services and exploring opportunities for myt Learn, MT’s AI-powered education platform, in South Africa and other African markets.

Cassava’s NVIDIA-powered AI Factory in Cape Town is Africa’s most powerful supercomputer. The partnership combines this computing scale, Cassava’s AI platforms and regional reach with MT’s own AI products, local language capabilities and operating experience.

“Realising AI’s promise in Africa requires more than potential; it takes infrastructure, technology, and proven expertise. By pairing Mauritius Telecom’s AI products and operating experience with Cassava’s AI infrastructure and reach, we aim to bring locally relevant AI services and education solutions to more African markets,” said Ziaad Suleman, SVP Cassava Technologies for South Africa and Botswana.

“We are building AI capability in Mauritius that can also serve other African markets. With myt Learn, we are already putting that capability to work in our schools, supporting both students and teachers. This partnership brings together products we have developed and Cassava’s infrastructure and reach to take that work further. Our ambition is to make trusted AI useful and accessible, while ensuring that those responsible for its use retain meaningful control,” said Veemal Gungadin, CEO of Mauritius Telecom.

The companies will explore access to Cassava’s AI Factory as an additional source of on-demand computing capacity for MT’s AI offerings, alongside access to AI models through CAIMEx, Cassava’s AI platform. Cassava capacity and model access would be used only for workloads where customers permit it. These options would complement MT’s existing myt AI Cloud platform and infrastructure in Mauritius, and could support its expansion into other African markets.

In education, the partners will jointly assess opportunities for myt Learn, starting with South Africa’s public and private education sectors, with potential expansion into other Cassava markets. Created by MT and rolling out in Mauritian schools for selected grades, myt Learn provides curriculum-aligned guided lessons, a multilingual AI tutor and personalised revision. Teachers have access to performance insights and AI tools for marking, test creation and lesson preparation. The platform can be adapted to local curricula and teaching needs.

Together, the companies aim to show how telecommunications operators can bring locally relevant AI services to customers and take African-developed products into new markets.

Distributed by APO Group on behalf of Cassava Technologies.

About Cassava Technologies:
Cassava Technologies is a technology leader providing a vertically integrated ecosystem of digital services and infrastructure enabling digital transformation. Through its business units, Cassava provides Connectivity, Colocation, Cloud, Cybersecurity, Compute AI and Payment solutions to mostly enterprise customers in Africa, the Middle East, Latin America, Europe and UK. Cassava’s digital solutions enable its customers in 37 countries to grow, transform, and better serve their own customers. https://www.CassavaTechnologies.com/

About Mauritius Telecom:
Mauritius Telecom is the leading telecommunications and digital services provider in the Republic of Mauritius, serving consumers, businesses and public institutions through its myt brand. Its services span fixed and mobile connectivity, fibre broadband, television, cloud, cybersecurity and AI. MT is building trusted sovereign AI capability through its data centres, compute infrastructure and platforms, including mytGPT, myt AI Cloud and myt Learn. Its strategy connects national digital transformation with opportunities to serve customers and partners across Africa and Asia. For more information, visit www.Telecom.mu.

### Meeza and Utopia Sign Strategic AI Partnership

Source: MIST

(QNA)-
Meeza, Qatar's leading provider of data center solutions and IT services, has signed a strategic memorandum of understanding with venture capital fund Utopia to establish an integrated ecosystem combining advanced computing, innovation and entrepreneurship, aimed at building AI companies in Qatar and expanding them into regional and global markets.
Under the agreement, Meeza will host the UTOPIA AI Venture Cloud platform at one of its internationally certified data centers, providing the infrastructure needed to operate high-density computing systems, along with integrated monitoring and management services.
The partnership will give innovators and startups access to advanced computing capabilities, helping them turn ideas into commercial products and solutions and accelerate their market entry through an integrated AI venture-building model.
The initiative reflects a vision of moving from hosting technology to developing it, while strengthening Qatar's position as a regional hub for innovation and the digital economy, in line with Qatar National Vision 2030.

cross_cutting.content:
# 柬埔寨要建国家AI研究中心，近九成融资来自法国

# 柬埔寨要建国家AI研究中心，近九成融资来自法国

2026-11-18 18:48

发布于：上海市

【文/观察者网 张菁娟】

柬埔寨将与法国合作，在首都金边建设国家人工智能与数据科学研究中心。法国开发署（AFD）公布的项目资料显示，该项目总融资额为2315万欧元，法国开发署提供2075万欧元，占比近9成。

11月14日至16日，第20届法语国家组织峰会期间，“FrancoTech 2026”创新科技展在金边举行。柬埔寨邮电部国务秘书So Visothy表示，建立国家AI研究中心，是柬埔寨邮电部推动国内人工智能发展的一项优先任务。

展会开幕前，项目筹备已进行了数月。今年3月，柬埔寨邮电部、柬埔寨数字技术学院（CADT）与法国开发署就实施方案举行会谈。8月，柬埔寨邮电部公开征集工程咨询机构，服务范围涵盖建筑设计、AI基础设施采购支持和施工监督。10月，研究中心建筑设计竞赛的获奖结果公布。

“这一动向的战略意义远超出常规的双边外交礼仪”

按CADT的设想，今后，一家刚起步的柬埔寨科技公司，也能用上国家研究中心的算力。中心将配置一套共享高性能计算集群，向政府部门、高校、科研机构和私营企业开放。使用者遇到技术难题，还可以得到AI专家的支持。

项目由柬埔寨邮电部与柬埔寨数字技术学院共同推进。法国开发署将这座中心定位为柬埔寨自主掌握的科研基础设施。项目实施期为五年，从2026年8月1日至2031年8月1日。融资方式包括主权贷款以及FEXTE技术援助。

谁来培养使用这些设备的人？法国格勒诺布尔-阿尔卑斯大学将与柬埔寨数字技术学院合作，为当地研究人员提供培训、奖学金和学术交流机会。中心还将支持政府部门和企业开发AI应用，优先考虑农业、卫生、水务和教育四个领域。

另有一项配套工作已于今年2月启动。法国国际技术合作署将利用技术援助赠款，协助柬方制定和落实个人数据保护、数字政府等领域的监管规则。

柬埔寨邮电部国务秘书SoVisothy《金边邮报》

柬埔寨主流英文媒体《高棉时报》（Khmer Times）刊发的一篇评论文章称，金边研究中心是柬法20项双边技术协定的一部分，“这一动向的战略意义远超出常规的双边外交礼仪”。AFD公布的研究中心项目说明并未列出完整的协定清单。

法国为何对这样的项目感兴趣？文章提到，法国近年来在欧洲倡导技术自主，扶持Mistral AI等企业和法国国家信息与自动化研究所等科研机构。在海外，法国则通过开发署，为伙伴国建设数字公共基础设施提供融资。此次在金边，法方的参与从项目融资延伸到了科研人才培养。

现成的大模型，能读懂多少高棉语？

柬埔寨布局数字经济已有数年。柬政府先后出台《数字经济和社会政策框架（2021—2035年）》和《数字政府政策（2022—2035年）》。前者希望让更多民众参与数字经济，后者着眼于改善公共服务和基础设施。发展数字技术也被写入2023年至2028年的“五角战略”。

据法国开发署介绍，2023年，柬埔寨已有超过六成的人口使用互联网。该署援引的估算显示，柬埔寨数字经济规模约为16.2亿美元，到2027年可能接近28.7亿美元。不过，农村地区的数字基础设施依然薄弱，不少民众使用数字工具还不熟练。

即便用得上国外的大模型，柬埔寨的学校、企业和政府部门也要先过语言关。文章写道，高棉语是柬埔寨的官方语言，但在主流大模型的训练材料里，高棉文占比很低。模型处理一段高棉文，往往需要把文字拆成更多词元。这样一来，计算成本随之上升，模型用高棉语作答时，也容易给出失实信息。

对面向全球市场的科技企业而言，专门投入算力改善高棉语表现，商业回报有限。但对柬埔寨来说，模型能否读懂本地用语、准确理解当地法规，直接关系到这套工具能不能用。当地技术人员如果只能通过外国企业的闭源接口使用模型，即便找到了错处，也很难直接调整模型。

文章认为，金边研发中心的战略价值正在于此：本土研究人员能够集中精力构建干净、公开的高棉语国家语料库，优化专有分词器，并开发适应本土低算力硬件环境的小型化、高能效模型。

“FrancoTech 2026”创新科技展现场《金边邮报》

对柬埔寨来说，高性能计算设备需要稳定供电和高速网络，日常维护、设备更新、研究人员薪酬都要花钱。而启动资金到位只是第一步，往后由谁出钱运行、能不能留住人才，同样关键。

文章提出，可以分阶段观察项目进展。关注中心最终设在哪里、由哪家机构管理，以及首笔资金何时落实。六至十二个月内，可以看首批研究人员是否开始招募、中心能否与法国科研机构共享算力，以及能否拿出一套评估模型高棉语水平的基准。

再过一两年，更直接的检验来自使用者：哪些柬埔寨企业用上了中心开发的工具？哪些政府部门愿意将其用于日常工作？法国开发署提供的2075万欧元覆盖了项目近九成融资。等到首批设备要更新、首批研究人员要决定去留时，柬方还要算好这笔长期账。

柬埔寨还想培育新的“独角兽”

11月16日，柬方还在“FrancoTech 2026”创新科技展上公布了“2030年愿景”。SoVisothy告诉《金边邮报》，政府希望让更多初创企业参加创业加速计划，获得投资，把业务拓展到周边市场。

“我们希望，在不久的将来，柬埔寨能再培育出数千家初创企业，甚至有望诞生一家新的‘独角兽’企业。”SoVisothy说。

“独角兽”企业指的是估值达到或超过10亿美元的未上市初创企业。至于到2030年具体要培育多少家企业、政府准备为这项倡议投入多少资金，他没有给出数字。

法国企业也在寻找合作伙伴。据So Visothy介绍，柬埔寨邮电部正在与法国科技创业网络La French Tech合作，帮助本土企业结识法语国家和地区的同行。此次约有70至80家法国企业通过这一网络来到金边，洽谈业务、交流技术。

本次展会最初预计有5000人参加，最终有来自100多个国家的逾3万人报名，316家企业参展。法国总统马克龙等多国领导人出席。论坛设七大主题、17项讨论议题，涵盖AI、金融科技、农业科技和数字政府等领域。其间，柬方还与一个美国合作方签署了空间技术合作谅解备忘录，未披露对方名称及协议细节。返回搜狐，查看更多

# Mitsubishi Heavy Industries : MHI and SAKURA internet to form Strategic Alliance to Build Japan's Sovereign AI Infrastructure Enable Rapid and Reliable Deployment of Domestic AI Infrastructure

Published on 11/18/2026 at 05:04 am +03

Publicnow

Press Information

MHI and SAKURA internet to form Strategic Alliance to Build Japan's Sovereign AI Infrastructure

-- Enable Rapid and Reliable Deployment of Domestic AI Infrastructure --

2026-11-18

Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Ltd.

SAKURA internet Inc.

SHARE

・ Combining MHI's social infrastructure and high-security technologies with SAKURA internet's cloud and data center operations expertise
・ Looking ahead to the sovereign AI era, aiming to strengthen Japan's domestic digital infrastructure and realize highly efficient AI data centers that can be built rapidly

Tokyo and Osaka, November 18, 2026 - Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Ltd. (President and CEO: Eisaku Ito; Head Office: Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo; "MHI") and SAKURA internet Inc. (Founder, CEO, and President: Kunihiro Tanaka; Head Office: Osaka City, Osaka; "SAKURA internet") today announced that they have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to form a strategic alliance. Under the MOU, the two companies will explore collaboration to strengthen Japan's domestic digital infrastructure for the sovereign AI and cloud(Note1) era. The initiative includes developing AI modular data centers that can be built efficiently and rapidly.

Growing Importance of Digital Sovereignty and Infrastructure Resiliency in the AI Era
The rapid spread of generative AI has made data centers essential infrastructure for government and industry. At the same time, much of the AI processing in Japan runs on cloud platforms operated overseas, which leaves it exposed to sudden service changes or suspensions. As a result, securing digital sovereignty and resilience (the ability to recover quickly from unforeseen events) for AI infrastructure designed, built, and operated in Japan is becoming a key challenge.

Securing sovereignty also requires stronger physical infrastructure. AI data centers need large-scale power and advanced cooling, and the time it takes to secure power and complete construction can delay the start of operations.
AI infrastructure must also remain resilient to disasters and geopolitical uncertainty, making the rapid and reliable development of data centers a strategic priority.

Two Strengths, One Objective
MHI has a long track record of supplying and operating resilient, safe, and secure equipment and systems across social infrastructure, aviation, defense, space, and other fields. It has technology and know-how in design, manufacturing, control, simulation and maintenance, data grounded in real-world site conditions, and the trust of customers across these industries. MHI has made resilience one of the pillars of its growth strategy, meaning keeping social infrastructure running and enabling rapid recovery in an increasingly uncertain environment. As part of this, it is strengthening its data center business, which integrates cooling, power, control and high-security technologies.

SAKURA internet was selected by Japan's Digital Agency as a Government Cloud service provider for fiscal year 2026, the first domestic cloud provider to be selected. It operates data centers in Tokyo, Osaka and Hokkaido and has an extensive track record in building and operating data centers and cloud services.

Combining these strengths, the two companies will explore collaboration in two areas:

- Domestic digital infrastructure: jointly building a secure, high-performance, Japan-based digital infrastructure foundation for the sovereign AI and sovereign cloud era and offering vertically integrated services.
- AI modular data centers: building highly efficient AI data centers quickly for next-generation AI infrastructure, including exploring reference architectures and modular construction methods for mechanical and electrical equipment.

"As AI becomes national infrastructure, that infrastructure has to be resilient in both how it is built and how it is operated. With SAKURA internet, we want to give Japan a sovereign AI foundation that is secure, available when it matters, and fast enough to keep pace with demand. This is part of MHI ITO(Note2) initiative: combining our strengths with the right partner to deliver value to far more customers." - Masayuki Suematsu, Executive Vice President and Chief Strategy Officer, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Ltd.

"With the rapid spread of AI, digital infrastructure such as cloud and data centers has become essential to society and industry. In this collaboration, we will combine MHI's technology and expertise in social infrastructure with our own experience building and operating cloud and data centers. Together, we aim to create new options for the domestic digital infrastructure that the sovereign AI and sovereign cloud era requires." - Kunihiro Tanaka, Founder, Chief Executive Officer, and President, SAKURA internet Inc.

Looking ahead, the two companies aim to take the products and solutions established through this collaboration to global markets, including Asia and Oceania.

- 1Sovereign AI / cloud: An approach that allows data and AI platforms to be operated and used under a country's own laws and control.
- 2"Innovative Total Optimization" MHI's management methodology, built on the pillars of "total optimization" and "domain expansion".

About Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Group
Since its foundation in 1884, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI) Group has grown into a global leader in engineering and manufacturing, consistently addressing societal challenges and supporting people's lives. By integrating cutting-edge knowledge with the advanced technological capabilities developed over our long history, we will continue to tackle social issues and contribute to the realization of a safe and prosperous society.
For more information, please visit www.mhi.com or follow our insights and stories on spectra.mhi.com.

About SAKURA internet Inc.
SAKURA internet is a digital infrastructure company founded in 1996. It provides highly reliable cloud and computing platforms as "SAKURA Cloud," "SAKURA Web Hosting," and "SAKURA VPS" from its self-operated domestic data centers. Under the corporate philosophy of "Turning 'what you want to do' into 'what you can do,' " we develop a variety of services to meet customer needs and propose DX solutions that cater to various industries.
For more information, please visit https://www.sakura.ad.jp/corporate/en/.
